articleTitle: Multipath propagation analysis and ghost target removal for FMCW automotive radars
abstract: Multipath propagation induced by large number of reflec-tions from complex environments has been a long-standing challenge that affects automotive radar target detection. This unwanted effect gives rise to power fading and ghost targets, which leads to degraded estimation performance and increased false alarms. In this paper, we present mathematical formulations for multipath propagation model and the corrupted echoes, where frequency modulated continuous wave as a commonly adopted transmit waveform in automotive radars is considered. The impact of the multipath propagation on target detection is then analyzed. Additionally, a simple but effective algorithm is proposed to remove the ghost targets. Numerical simulations are provided to demonstrate the satisfactory performance.

articleTitle: Recognition of radar deception jamming based on convolutional neural network
abstract: Since the radar deception jamming interferes with the radar in complicated electromagnetic environments, recognizing the deception jamming is an intractable problem. Various improved jamming strategies have been proposed, while the jamming technology is updated continuously. In this study, a new radar jamming detection method based on the convolutional neural network (CNN) is presented. The method firstly uses the nearest-neighbour interpolation (NNI) and short-time Fourier transform (STFT) to analyse the signal within the time-frequency (TF) range, to obtain the great adaptability on the different condition; then, it uses CNN to detect whether the signal is contaminated by radar jamming and determine the type of jamming. The simulation results show that this method can not only identify transmitting deceptive jamming and velocity deception jamming effectively, but also has good anti-noise performance and robustness. Compared with the recognition method based on time-frequency distribution, the recognition accuracy is 15% higher than the conventional detection model.

articleTitle: Human activity classification using radar signal and RNN networks
abstract: Radar-based human activities recognition is still an open problem and is a key to detect anomalous behaviour for security and health applications. Deep learning networks such as convolutional neural networks (CNN) have been proposed for such tasks and showed better performance than traditional supervised learning paradigm. However, it is hard to deploy CNN networks to embedded systems due to the limited computational power available. From this point of concern, the use of a recurrent neural network (RNN) is proposed in this paper for human activities classification. We also propose an innovative data argumentation method to train the neural network using a limited number of data. The experiment shows that our network can achieve a mean accuracy of 94.3% in human activity classification.

articleTitle: Combined spectrogram structure and intensity for human activity recognition using modified DTW
abstract: Doppler radars have been extensively utilized for human activity recognition, which is capable of providing contactless sensing in all weather regardless of illumination conditions. We proposed a modified dynamic time warping (DTW) algorithm to discriminate six activities, those are walking, sitting down, standing up, picking up an object, drinking water, and falling, by combining both information of spectrogram inner structure and intensity distribution. Standard DTW for activity recognition usually employs spectrogram envelope as the input sequence and does not specifically consider the multi-dimensional characteristics of human activities. The Micro-Doppler spectrogram of human activities obtained by time-frequency analysis contains rich information such as motion intensity, direction and range. We first scale the intensity of spectrogram into 256 levels and then segment the scaled spectrogram into sequential vectors along time as the input of DTW distance matrix. In this way, both inner structure and intensity distribution of the spectrogram can be extracted and fully exploited. A K-nearest neighbours (KNN) classifier is employed based on the DTW distance for further activity recognition. The experimental results using the given test dataset demonstrate the excellent performance of the proposed method, exhibiting a recognition accuracy of 100% using full training dataset, and 97% for the dataset with test data discarded.

articleTitle: Orthogonal Chirp Division Multiplexing waveform for mmWave Joint Radar and Communication
abstract: For millimeter-wave applications, it is really a challenge for the integrated waveform to achieve both wideband performance in radar and efficient frequency utilization in communication. In this paper, we explored the feasibility of orthogonal chirp division multiplexing (OCDM) as a radar-communication integrated waveform in broadband applications. We proposed the integrated waveform structure and introduced the signal processing protocols. Cyclic decoupling and all grid correction were separately used for obtaining the rough and the fine range information. The simulation results verified the effectiveness of our proposed method in high-resolution target measurements. It also illustrated that OCDM obtains more reliable detection in low SNR comparing to OFDM based on output dynamic range.

articleTitle: A novel ship detection method based on gabor feature
abstract: Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) Systems can be used for discovery and surveillance. According to the current requirements, accurate ship detection is becoming more and more important. However, the accuracy of traditional ship detection algorithm is not satisfying in complex scene. As a consequence, this paper proposes a novel method for detecting ships within SAR imagery using Gabor feature and Two Parameter Constant False Alarm Rate (2P-CFAR) detection technique. First, feature extraction was performed by using Gabor filter. Then, combined with the extracted orientation feature, the ship recognition of SAR image is obtained by 2P-CFAR detector. Finally, false alarms among the candidate targets were removed by geometric features of the ships. To prove the rationality of this method, experiments were carried with two high-resolution Gaofen-3 satellite SAR images in open sea background. The experimental results show that the presented method has preferable performance in the accuracy of ship identification.

articleTitle: Human activity classification with neural network using radar micro-doppler and range signatures
abstract: We propose a method for radar-based human activity classification by a neural network taking both micro-Doppler and range signatures of the target as input. Temporally localized features are first extracted from range-time maps and micro-Doppler spectrograms by convolutional neural networks, and then fed into cascaded long-short-term memory for classification. The use of two types of signatures improves classification accuracy without adding much computational cost. The proposed method is evaluated on a relatively large dataset provided by the IET radar challenge “Human Activity Classification with Radar”. By using cross-validation of the training dataset, the proposed neural network achieves 94.8% accuracy taking dual signatures as input, which outperforms the networks using micro-Doppler signature input (93.5%) or range signature input (87.9%) only. On the test dataset, we achieve 100% accuracy via majority voting of multiple instances of the proposed neural network. This result won the first place in the IET radar challenge.

articleTitle: Target recognition of radar HRRP based on AUMAP segmentation and improved convolutional neural network
abstract: In the high-resolution range profile (HRRP) recognition, segmentation can obtain the target attitude angle of HRRP data, and the methods of segmenting the HRRP data have a significant impact on improving the performance of recognition. Besides, the way of the feature extraction can enhance the separability among the HRRP data and improve the generalization of the classifier. To manage these practical problems, this paper puts forward a new recognition framework containing three steps. Firstly, HRRP data is segmented by Adaptive Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection (AUMAP). Secondly, Key regions of the bispectra are reshaped through bispectra analysis to obtain additional data as input to the convolutional neural network (CNN). Thirdly, the loss function of CNN is modified to solve the imbalance of HRRP samples and improve the stability of the algorithm. Experimental results verify the effectiveness of the framework under the support of HRRP measurement data.

articleTitle: Retrieval of ice cloud properties with a dual frequency optimal estimation algorithm for terahertz and millimeter wave cloud radar
abstract: In this paper, we explore the potential of terahertz (238 GHz) and millimeter (94 GHz) wave radar to retrieval ice cloud properties based on dual frequency optimal estimation algorithm. The relationship between radar reflectivity factor and ice cloud microphysical parameters is established through forward physical model with different a prior value and crystal habits. The results suggest that: (1) The terahertz and millimeter radar measurements contain enough information to constrain the retrieval of ice cloud properties regardless of a priori value and habits; (2) The retrieval error decreases as the accuracy of a priori increases. The error of spherical particle is basically smaller than that of the mixed particles; (3) Quantitative estimates of the retrieval error are provided. The effective radius is retrieved with errors varying between 0-7% and 0-13% for sphere and mixed habits, respectively. The ice water content is retrieved with errors varying between 2-12% and 2-25% for sphere and mixed habits, respectively.

articleTitle: Off-grid DOA estimation for passive radar
abstract: To solve the problem that the true target direction of arrival (DOA) is not on the discrete grid points, we adopt a new off-grid sparse strategy to estimate the target DOA of passive radar. This strategy is the root sparse Bayesian learning method, which utilizes a coarse grid and treats the sampling position in the coarse grid as an adaptive parameter. Then, the coarse mesh is iteratively refined using the expectation maximization algorithm, and the estimated angle is the root of a certain polynomial. Simulation results show that the method has higher estimation accuracy and lower computational complexity in DOA estimation of passive radar. In addition, this method can not only estimate the DOA of multi-target signals in a single snapshot, but also provide new ideas for DOA estimation of coherent signals.

articleTitle: SAR ship detection based on improved YOLOv3
abstract: Traditional SAR ship detection methods rely on manual designed features and are vulnerable to complex background interference with poor generalization abilities. Those methods based on deep learning can automatically extract features and have super-duper anti-jamming characteristics, which is of great significance for future radar intelligent perception. In this paper, to break the limit of only detecting fixed areas for conventional convolutional neural networks, we propose an improved YOLOv3 SAR ship detection method (YOLOv3-DCN) to adaptive sample the size and shape of ship targets. The enhanced YOLOv3 model is designed based on deformable convolution, the ResNet50 variant feature extractor and the ShuffleNetv2 lightweight method. Compared with the original YOLOv3 model, the mAP increases from 93.21% to 96.94%, and the probability of detection increases from 95.51% to 97.75% on SSDD dataset. In terms of the model size, the lightweight designed model is only one-eighth of the original YOLOv3 model, which can be used widely in real life scenarios.

articleTitle: Mainlobe jamming suppression method based on beamspace orthogonal cancellation for distributed array radar
abstract: Distributed array radar can provide unique advantages for mainlobe jamming suppression based on the characteristics of large aperture, wide frequency band and high resolution. However, traditional spatial cancellation method cannot provide desirable performance as the large amount of computation and the degree of freedom cannot be fully utilized in the distributed radar. Therefore, a jamming cancellation method based on beamspace orthogonal cancellation is proposed in this paper. In the proposed method, the beams pointing to each jamming direction and orthogonal to the target direction are firstly formed by using the roughly-estimated jamming direction. Then, each jamming cancellation beam and the target direction beam are used to cancel jamming based on MMSE criterion. The effectiveness of the algorithm is verified by the simulation of non-uniform distributed array.

articleTitle: Hand gesture recognition based-on three-branch CNN with fine-tuning using MIMO radar
abstract: In this paper, we employ a 77GHz frequency modulated continuous wave (FMCW) multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) radar to achieve hand gesture recognition based on a three-branch convolutional neural network (CNN) with fine-tuning. Firstly, the FMCW MIMO radar is utilized to capture the hand gesture data that are the fast-time-slow-time-antenna 3 dimension (3D) data. Then, by applying the discretize Fourier transform (DFT) to the fast-time and slow-time, the multiple signal classification (MUSIC) approach to the antenna dimension, and the multi-frame accumulation, the range-Doppler-angle temporal signatures can be extracted from the captured data. In order to exploit the temporal and spatial correlations of the hand motions, we construct a three-branch CNN to self-learn the hand gesture signatures from the range, Doppler and angle dimension, respectively, and to recognize 9 hand gestures. The fine-tuning approach is proposed to improve the robustness of the proposed network in recognizing an untrained person's hand gestures. After the fine-tuning, the experiment results show that the proposed approach can recognize 9 hand gestures of all trained persons with an average accuracy over 96% and an untrained person with an average accuracy over 96%.

articleTitle: A novel image feature-based traffic flow counting approach using low power consumption radar
abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel image feature-based traffic flow counting approach using low power consumption radar. This new approach exploits the trajectory signature from the range-slow-time images of different vehicles. The proposed approach firstly suppresses the static clutter and merges distance units because the vehicles occupy some range bins. Then, an image feature extraction algorithm, including grey processing, median filtering, binarization, region growing, filtering small-area blocks and morphological processing, is used to extract the trajectories of the vehicles and a target separation algorithm based on the necessary safety distance among the vehicles is developed to achieve the purpose of vehicles counting. The experimental results show that the accuracy of the proposed approach for traffic flow counting can reach 85% for the case that traffic is moving at a crawl and 90% above for the case that traffic is moving freely. Furthermore, the developed approach is suitable for embedded system and the designed traffic flow radar system is moveable.

articleTitle: Real-time processing of ship detection with spaceborne SAR image based on multiple FPGA
abstract: With the need of rapid detection of ships or other iso-time-sensitive targets, a block parallel processing technology based on multiple FPGA was proposed, which realized the parallelization of the estimation of typical sea clutter model parameters and CFAR ship detection algorithm. In order to realize azimth-oriented pipelined processing, the SAR image with a large width in a SAR aperture was divided into 16 sub-block SAR images along the range direction for parallel processing. Each sub-block SAR image was taken as a parallel processing unit in FPGA, and the sea clutter model parameters in it were independently calculated. To further improve the efficiency of parallel processing, each sub-block SAR image adopted 8-way parallel processing channel for rapid processing, so as to achieve rapid estimation of sea clutter model parameters and real-time ship detection. Through theoretical analysis, this technique could meet the time-efficiency requirement of real-time pipelined processing for spaceborne SAR ship detection. Experiments on the ship detection performance of a parallel processing unit using the actual spaceborne SAR image data shown that the technique maintained the same detection performance compared with traditional CPU computing platform.

articleTitle: A lightweight network model for human activity classifiction based on pre-trained mobilenetv2
abstract: Radar-based human activity classification has attracted more and more attention in the fields of anti-terrorism maintenance, post-disaster search and rescue, medical monitoring and smart homes, which not only has the advantage of detecting in harsh environments but also can protect personal privacy to the greatest extent. The combination of deep learning methods and micro-Doppler spectrograms for radar human activity recognition is becoming more and more popular, but the general network model has many parameters and long training time, making it difficult to train a better network model. Therefore, we have designed an efficient and lightweight network model, which is based on the Mobilenetv2 model pre-trained on the ImageNet dataset. The model we proposed can learn the micro-doppler information and can automatically identify tasks of different types of human movements. We use the micro-Doppler spectrogram as the training data of the network model. The model has a small number of parameters. It can train a model very quickly. At the same time, it can trace-off the accuracy and resource requirements. It can be run on the embedded in the system, it can meet the requirements of the human activity recognition system. We have shown very good performance on the experimental data provided by the official, which can not only ensure the accuracy of the model to predict human activities, but also save a lot of training time. At the same time, our experiments found that a single human actvitiy can be quickly and accurately recognized, however, the complex human behavior composed of a series of single actions still needs to continue to work

articleTitle: Signal classification against repeat radar jammers with optimized MIMO radar waveforms
abstract: The digital radio frequency memory (DRFM) repeat jammer, which can transmit signals of close signature to real target returns, is a typical low-cost electronic attacker and poses threats to radar systems. One can optimize multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) radar waveforms to magnify the difference between deceptive signals and real targets, and in this paper, we examine the performance improvement achieved by designing classification algorithms. The training samples are theoretical target returns and theoretical constant-modulus deceptive signals, both modulated with different Doppler frequencies. Three classifiers, namely the support vector machines (SVM), Naive Bayes and k-Nearest Neighbor (kNN), are considered and the SVM performs the best. With 128-chips phase-coded transmit signals, the waveform optimization algorithm achieves a 6dB signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) improvement at the 90% classification rate.

articleTitle: Range-angle two-dimensional anti jamming against dense false targets
abstract: Digital Radio Frequency Memory (DRFM), as an important deceptive jamming technology against modern radar system, can generate a large number of high-fidelity range false targets before and after real target, thus achieving effective jamming. When multiple jammers apply jamming from different angles, the resulting false targets are azimuthally deceptive, which will further impact subsequent target positioning and precise guidance. In response to the above-mentioned multi-angle dense false target jamming situation, this paper proposes a complete narrowband array radar anti-jamming algorithm, which effectively suppresses the range dimensional jamming by Multiplicative Noncoherent Accumulation (MNCA), and filters the residual angle dimensional jamming by spatial filtering, Wherein, the azimuths of the jammers are obtained by K-means dynamic clustering based on constructed angle data set. Theoretical analysis and simulation show that the method has good jamming suppression ability, and can achieve accurate target ranging and angle measuring.

articleTitle: Small aircraft target detection using cascade FP-CNN in remote sensing images
abstract: Aiming at the problem that the remote sensing images of small-scale aircraft targets are poorly detected in deep learning networks, the paper proposes a method of remote sensing image aircraft target detection based on Cascade FP-CNN network. The Cascade FP-CNN network uses feature pyramids to achieve feature fusion of feature maps on different scales, which enhances the target features learned by the network, thereby obtaining high-resolution, high-receptive-field feature maps. In addition, referring to the method for determining the crossover threshold of the Cascade network to set the crossover threshold of the Cascade FP-CNN network, a detection algorithm suitable for small-scale aircraft targets is finally constructed, thereby realizing the accurate recognition of small aircraft targets in remote sensing images. The average accuracy of the algorithm on the UCAS-AOD dataset reaches 96.01%, which is about 2% higher than the existed Faster R-CNN and Cascade R-CNN methods, and the detection capability has been significantly improved.

articleTitle: An adaptive interference cancellation method for automotive FMCW radar based on waveform optimization
abstract: With the widespread use of automotive FMCW radars, the problem of mutual interference cannot be ignored. The mutual interference will directly increase the signal noise floor and even result in false targets in a few cases. To solve this problem, this paper proposes an interference mitigation method using an adaptive canceller. Firstly, the particle swarm optimization algorithm was used to minimize the correlation between the waveforms of the victim radar and the interfering radar. Then, the optimal filtering is achieved by the Least Mean Squares (LMS) algorithm based on the reference signal to output interference suppression result. The simulation results show that the proposed method has a good performance on multi-type interference mitigation.

articleTitle: A GMTI algorithm based on novel channel equalization method for multi-channel imaging radar
abstract: For multi-channel SAR-GMTI system, the consistency between the channels is the indispensable condition for location and velocity measurement of ground moving targets. Therefore, particular attention should be paid to the study of channel equalization. However, traditional channel equalization methods often have the problems of low operating efficiency, large computational burden and poor adaptability, making them less effective. Aiming at this problem, the signal model for multi-channel SAR-GMTI processing is established. Based on this, a novel channel equalization method is proposed in this paper. The experimental results based on the measured data of airborne 7-channel SAR-GMTI system show that the proposed method can effectively eliminate the amplitude and phase error between channels without the need for iterative operation, thus improves the calculation efficiency and GMTI processing effect simultaneously.

articleTitle: Weighted detector for distributed target detection in the presence of signal mismatch
abstract: To solve the problem of detecting a distributed target in the situation of signal mismatch, we propose a weighted detector. The proposed detector is formed by weighting two detectors, which behave quite differently in the presence of signal mismatch. By adjusting the value of the weight of the detector, the proposed detector can flexibly control the detection performance of mismatched signals. In particular, the proposed detector, with a small weight, is much more selective to mismatched signals. In contrast, the proposed detector, with a large weight, is very robust to mismatched signals. In addition, even in the case of no signal mismatch, the proposed detector with an appropriate weight can achieve higher probability of detection (PD) than the existing detectors. Simulation results are provided to illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed detector.

articleTitle: Radar-based hierarchical human activity classification
abstract: Worldwide the ageing population is increasing, and there are new requirements from governments to keep people at home longer. As a consequence assisted living has been an active area of research, and radar has been identified as an emerging technology of choice for indoor activity monitoring. Activity classification has been investigated, but is often limited by the classification accuracy in the most challenging yet realistic cases. This paper aims to evaluate and improve the accuracy in classifying six commonly performed indoor activities from the University of Glasgow open dataset. For activity classification, the selection of features to discriminate between activities is paramount. Activity classification is usually done as one vs all strategy with one classifier and a set of features to distinguish between all the activities. In this paper, we propose to optimise the feature selection and classifier choice per activity using a hierarchical classification structure. This strategy reached 95.4% accuracy for all activities and about 100% for walking, opening the field for personnel recognition.

articleTitle: Accurate slant range model in ground-based radar imaging of the lunar
abstract: Ground-based radar imaging is an important approach for lunar observation. However, due to the long round-trip time delay and long integration time, the invalidation of “stop-and-go” hypothesis presents challenge to the radar imaging algorithms. In this paper, firstly, the accurate ephemeris of large-scale lunar surface is created based on the coordinate transformations. Secondly, considering the error of “stop-and-go” hypothesis, the accurate slant range model between the ground-based radar and lunar surface is presented. Finally, the simulation results are presented to verify the correctness of the ephemeris calculation, and demonstrate the slant range difference caused by the “stop-and-go” hypothesis.

articleTitle: The effects of channel imbalances on the azimuth multi-channel SAR
abstract: Azimuth multi-channel (AMC) synthetic aperture radar (SAR) is an effective technology to conquer the minimum antenna area constraint and can provide high-resolution and wide-swath (HRWS) SAR images compared with the conventional strip-map SAR. In order to suppress azimuth ambiguity, AMC SAR will face an important problem: channel imbalances estimation and compensation. At first, this paper theoretically analysis the effects of channel imbalances including amplitude imbalance, phase imbalance and range sampling time imbalance (RSTI) on AMC SAR images, where all these channel imbalances will introduce false targets in azimuth, and RSTI will also make a significant influence on the range of SAR images. And then, in order to validate the above result, some simulations based on the parameters are carried out, and the real image acquired by GF-3 is also described. In addition, the intensity, number, and position of false targets are discussed. Finally, this paper makes some conclusions and points out the problems of these results.

articleTitle: Waveform design of cognitive radar based on deep learning in the presence of clutter
abstract: Waveform design is a key component of the cognitive radar system. With the development of radar technology, waveform designed by a single-criterion is difficult to meet the radar's multi-tasking and multi-working mode. This paper presents a waveform design method based on deep learning in the presence of clutter. We design a deep learning model to learn the manner of the Mutual Information (MI) criterion and the Signal to Interference and Noise Ratio (SINR) criterion for designing waveforms, which enables the model has the characteristics of MI and SINR criteria simultaneously and realizes a smooth trade-off between the two criteria. The results show that the waveform design based on deep learning method is satisfactory and effective.

articleTitle: Classification in C-band of doppler signatures of human activities in indoor environments
abstract: This paper explains CentraleSupélec team's approach for the challenge of human activity classification with radar [1]. Our methodology is based on a convolutional network classifier processing the range-time and spectrogram representations. The preprocessing and the neural network architecture presented in this paper allowed us to reach 99% accuracy on challenge's test data of the challenge. A more advanced preprocessing using wavelets is also briefly discussed.

articleTitle: Radar working mode recognition based on hierarchical feature representation and clustering
abstract: The classification of intercepted radar signals has gained considerable attention in the field of electronic reconnaissance. Currently, the multi-function radar (MFR) is capable of transmitting complex and agile signals with different working modes, and the classification of radar waveforms using the traditional methods does not provide satisfactory results. Therefore, it is urgent to develop a new intelligent algorithm to recognize the working mode of MFR. In particular, this paper designs a novel feature extraction method to obtain the sequential relationship of the input signals. At the same time, a hierarchy of signal features is established to represent the signals layer by layer, and then the working mode of the emitter is determined effectively by unsupervised clustering method. The effectiveness and robustness of the proposed method is experimentally verified, through simulating the real complex electromagnetic environment and generating the signal samples of MFR.

articleTitle: Coherent accumulation detection for a maneuvering target with doppler ambiguity and doppler aliasing
abstract: High-speed manevuering target detection has been a challenging problem in recent years. The range migration (RM) and Doppler frequency migration (DFM) induced by the complex motions of a maneuvering target should be solved firstly in order to ensure the adequate output signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) for effectively target detection. In addition, the pulse repetition frequency is limited to satisfy the large range observation area requirement, which leads to the troublesome Doppler ambiguity and Doppler aliasing phenomenon and further degrade the target detection performance. In this paper, some characteristics for a maneuvering target with velocity ambiguity and Doppler aliasing target are presented, and then, a modify Keystone transform matched filtering (MKTMF) method is proposed to realize the long-time coherent accumulation for this kind of moving targets. Simulation results are provided to verify the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Differentiable neural architecture search for sar image ship object detection
abstract: SAR image ship detection has important applications in military and civil fields. With the wide application of deep learning in the field of computer vision, more and more SAR ship detection algorithms have applied deep learning. Neural network based on deep learning can automatically extract features instead of hand-crafted features, and has achieved great success. But the design of deep neural networks is time-consuming and complex, which need a lot of professional knowledge and experience. Neural architecture search (NAS) has shown great potential in automated design networks. NAS can find the most suitable architecture on the specified dataset within a given search space. In object detection, the scale of the object varies, which is usually solved by designing feature fusion network. So in this work, we proposed to use differentiable architecture search to search the feature fusion module for SAR ship detection. The experiments on SAR ship detection dataset (SSDD) showed that the discovered architecture can replace the corresponding part of the detection network with 1% performance improvement.

articleTitle: Phase array amplitude and phase correction for HFSWR based on AIS information
abstract: The existence of amplitude and phase error in array will affect the direction-finding accuracy for HFSWR. Firstly, an overview of the signal model containing the amplitude and phase errors in arrays was given, and two correction methods were introduced, including method of using calibration sources and self-calibration method. Then, the impacts of amplitude and phase errors on estimation of targets that from different incoming directions were analysed. After that, the two correction methods were used to correct amplitude and phase error based on simulation data, and the target direction finding accuracy before and after calibration were compared. The results showed that the method of using calibration sources can not only achieve antenna consistency compensation, but also reduce the average error of target estimation to improve the actual direction-of-arrival estimation accuracy. At last, the method of using calibration sources was applied to the measured HFSWR data, in which synchronized AIS information was selected as auxiliary source. The calibrated measured data showed that the mean value of the azimuth estimation error was reduced from 1.906 degrees to -0.1540 degrees and the variance was reduced 1.0108 degrees to 0.8970 degrees.

articleTitle: Robust and fast image processing method for feature extraction of jet engine modulation signals
abstract: Jet engine modulation (JEM), a modulation phenomenon caused by the rotating structure of jet engines. It is a typical feature extracted from radar echo and used for aircraft target recognition. For non-cooperative target recognition (NCTR), the significant characteristics of jet engines, such as the blade number (BN) and the blade length (BL), are obtained by various methods. However, the existing methods either need complex logical algorithms to accurately estimate the characteristics of jet engines or use unstable peak detection processing to further extract features, which are not practical in either case. In this paper, a robust and fast image processing method for jet engine feature extraction is proposed. By using joint time-frequency (JTF) analysis, combined with hole interval estimation and symmetry evaluation correction, the images of JEM signals converted into RGB color by short time Fourier transform (STFT) are processed. The application results of the measured JEM signals show that the method is effective and practical for extracting the characteristics of jet engines steadily and accurately from the JEM signals.

articleTitle: Radar target detection method based on improved YOLOv3
abstract: Aiming at the problems of low detection rate and high false alarm rate in radar target detection under low signal-to-noise ratio environment, a radar target detection method based on improved YOLOv3 is proposed. Considering the characteristics of small scale and few features of radar targets, the original YOLOv3 backbone network is pruned and nonlinear features are added, and the Darknet13 network structure is proposed. The multiple outputs of the Darknet13 network are fused in two scale, deep fusion is used to detect large-scale targets, and shallow fusion is used to detect small-scale targets. In order to solve the problem of imbalance between positive and negative samples of radar data, the focus loss function is used to strengthen the attention to the hard to distinguish samples. Meanwhile, warm up technology is used to optimize the learning rate adjustment strategy to improve the target detection performance and network training speed. The experimental results show that compared with the original YOLOv3 algorithm, the proposed method can improve the average detection rate by 8.4% and reduce the average false alarm rate by 79.8% when the signal-to-noise ratio is 10 dB.

articleTitle: A coherent detection algorithm for the high-speed targets based on radon inverse fourier transform
abstract: Within the long-time coherent integration (CI) in radar detection, high-speed targets generally suffer from the range walk (RW) effect, which leads to the typical coherent detection failure. To acquire robust coherent detection, this paper proposes Radon inverse Fourier transform (RIFT). In this paper, we focus on the fact in fast frequency-slow frequency domain that the echo of the target is characterized as a unique straight line whose location simply corresponds to the velocity. Benefiting from this fact, the velocity can be estimated through velocity searching via RIFT, in which the inverse Fourier transform (IFT) is exploited along the velocity-related straight line. Then, we can conduct the CI employing RIFT with the estimated velocity. In comparison with keystone transform (KT) and Radon-Fourier transform (RFT), the advantages of RIFT are as follows: low computational complexity, no interpolation loss as well as the blind speed sidelobe (BSSL) simultaneously. Numerical results demonstrate the effectiveness and the efficiency of the proposed RIFT. Specifically, the proposed algorithm yields 2dB better antinoise performance than scaled inverse Fourier transform (SCIFT) and frequency-domain deramp-keystone transform (FDDKT) in the high-speed target detections.

articleTitle: Clutter classification for cognitive radar with a deep convolutional neural network
abstract: Nowadays, the electromagnetic environment of radar is complex and changeable, and the traditional algorithm is no longer effective to the situation. Hence, it is difficult for radar to have better performance. In this paper, a clutter classification method for cognitive radar with a deep convolution neural network is proposed to solve the problems. Firstly, the dynamic environment information and static environment information are processed. The VGG-16 network and Bi-LSTM are used to realize the feature extraction and fusion of comprehensive environmental information. Finally, the clutter classification is achieved, so that the detection and tracking performance of cognitive radar can be improved with knowledge assistance.

articleTitle: High-resolution PolSAR classification model based on the fully convolutional neural network and polarimetric parameters
abstract: Polarimetric information is particularly useful in land surface classification for synthetic aperture radar (SAR) images. However, because the information is buried in complex-valued scattering matrix, the new generation of classification methods, which are mainly developed based on deep learning, are not capable of learning it automatically. Therefore, we proposed a fine-grained classification method that incorporates polarimetric information revealed with the Yamaguchi decomposition into a semantic segmentation model based on a Fully Convolutional Network (FCN) architecture. The model uses ResNet-50 as the backbone, and in each processing scale, it exports the high-level polarimetric information extracted with Yamaguchi decomposition and the original backscattering information to a newly introduced ensemble layer. It then increases the amount of information about the image details by integrating outputs of modules with different scales, and finally achieves the classification result with the combined multi-scale and multi-polarimetric information. Compared with widely used deep learning models, the proposed model significantly improved the classification accuracy in experiments using real high-resolution Polarimetric SAR (PolSAR) data.

articleTitle: SAR target recognition based on texture feature and contour feature fusion
abstract: This paper proposes a SAR image recognition method that combines contour features and texture features. The moment feature is selected as the contour feature, and the HOG feature is selected as the texture feature. Considering that the single feature recognition method has limitations and the accuracy of multiple classifications is poor, the feature fusion method is used for optimization. This paper proposes a new feature-level fusion idea, try to use Fisher scoring method to select features, at the same time use FS as the fusion weight, and reduce the dimensionality of the moment features by PCA according to the weight value to obtain the fusion feature matrix. The recognition performance is better than ordinary weighted fusion algorithm. At the same time, the idea of heterogeneous feature fusion is given, that is, decision-level fusion.

articleTitle: Inverse synthetic aperture radar imaging of maneuvering target based on the particle swarm optimization
abstract: Radar imaging of maneuvering target utilizing inverse synthetic aperture radar (ISAR) is very significant in radar signal processing. For the maneuverability, the Doppler frequency of the scatterer on the target is not constant during imaging time. And the classic imaging algorithm is insufficient to generate a well-focused ISAR image due to the time-varying of the signal. Under the assumption that the radar signal of the maneuvering target is modeled as the multi-component cubic phase (CP) signal, this paper proposes a novel ISAR imaging method based on the particle swarm optimization (PSO). The PSO algorithm and the CLEAN technique are used to realize parameter estimation of the multi-component CP signal with higher accuracy and lower computational complexity. Combined range-instantaneous-Doppler (RID) algorithm, the proposed method can generate the well-focused instantaneous images consequently. The experiments on the simulated model and measured data verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Slow-moving target detection with MIMO radar based on time-domain frequency diversity
abstract: For an airborne radar system, the detection of slow-moving targets under the ground clutter has become the research hotspot to worldwide scholars. In order to reduce the minimum detectable velocity (MDV) of moving target, an airborne multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) radar based on time-domain frequency diversity is studied in this paper. The signal model of time-domain frequency diversity MIMO radar is established. Then, by exploiting the idea of range compensation in the frequency diversity array space-time adaptive processing (FDA-STAP), a slow target detection method is given by using a priori range cell information. Simulation results indicate that the frequency step between pulses can separate the slow target from the main clutter area, which is beneficial to the detection of slow targets. The correctness and effectiveness of our analysis are verified through the computer simulation.

articleTitle: One-bit SAR imaging and moving target detection based on frequency shift of dechirp echo
abstract: SAR imaging and moving target detection are hot research topics in the radar literature. SAR involved one-bit sampling is a promising technology for many civilian applications due to its low-cost and low-power consumptions. This paper presents a novel one-bit method for detecting moving targets in SAR images. The proposed method is applied to the signal after dechirp processing. Based on the one-bit quantization, the method introduces a static frequency offset to the original signal, which decreases the spectrum interference of the higher harmonics. In addition, combined with displaced phase center antenna (DPCA) technique, the moving targets are effectively detected after compensation of the two channel one-bit SAR images. Finally, compared with the straightforward one-bit sampling scheme, the efficiency of the proposed method and the relevant conclusion are verified by the simulation results.

articleTitle: Feature selection and decision fusion methods in target recognition
abstract: The recognition of targets from the radar echoes in varying environmental conditions tend to have high complexity, especially for the dataset with large amount of features. Feature selection and an ensemble of classifiers decision fusion (CDF) approaches are proposed to reduce the dimension of features and achieve better target recognition results for various datasets compared to the individual classifier. The analysis was made in this paper using simulated radar echo datasets of five different types of airplanes. Results showed that the CDF approach outperforms the individual classifier approach on account of better performance in different conditions. Recognition results of fusion classifiers offer complementary information, which comprehensively utilize of the characteristics of a single classifier and increase the performance of the whole recognition process.

articleTitle: Pulse-agile waveform design for nonlinear FM pulses based on spectrum modulation
abstract: The transmission of pulses with different intra-pulse modulations within a coherent processing interval (CPI), also known as pulse-agile radar, has several potential applications. For the detection of small targets with long range and slow velocity in the background of strong clutter, the conventional pulse-Doppler (PD) radar is limited by range ambiguity and folded clutter. It is feasible to solve this problem through the agility between pulses. In this paper, a non-repeating, spectrum modulated nonlinear frequency modulation (NLFM) waveform applicable for pulse agility radar is described. Based on the spectrum structure of linear frequency modulation (LFM) signal, the waveform modulates its power spectral density by a random sinusoid to achieve good cross-correlation properties, which can suppress the range ambiguity and folded clutter. Simulation results are provided to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Multi-false-target deceptive jamming aganist SAR based on 1-bit quantization
abstract: This paper proposes a multi-false-target deceptive jamming method based on 1-bit sampling assisted with a single-frequency threshold. The jammer generates a specific single frequency time-varying signal according to the offset of predesigned false points. By comparing the echo data with the time-varying threshold signal, it is quantized into 1-bit sampling data. The 1-bit data is modulated by the false target template, and then retransmitted to the radar, so as to achieve multi-false-target deceptive jamming. Compared with the conventional deceptive jamming, the proposed method can simplify the calculation complexity and improve the efficiency of the jammer. Through the simulation experiment, the focusing quality of the false target is analysed and the effectiveness of the algorithm is verified.

articleTitle: A compact human activity classification model based on transfer learned network pruning
abstract: Human activity classification is a critical part of intelligent human-computer interaction, which is promising in various applications. The radar system provides a complementary input when the visible light cannot work. It can effectively tackle darkness, occlusion, and non-line-of sight conditions. The frequency modulation induced by the micromotion of human movements can be captured and utilized by radar systems. Currently, the integration of deep learning methods and classical signal processing has been more and more prominent in the radar-based human behaviour sensing field. In this work, we propose a compact deep learning model to classify various human activities by the corresponding frequency modulation. Considering most deep neural networks are both data-hungry and resource-hungry, we integrate transfer learning and network pruning techniques to reduce the number of labelled training samples and computational burden. The experiments demonstrate that our method not only outperforms convolutional neural networks trained from scratch but also significantly slims its model size and computing operations.

articleTitle: Migration through resolution cell correction of bistatic ISAR imaging with sparse aperture
abstract: A correction method is proposed for solving the problem of migration through resolution cell in bistatic ISAR imaging with sparse aperture. Sparse aperture data completion based on sparse representation by CAMP algorithm is proposed. After the completion data is obtained, the Keystone transform is used to correct the MTRC. The phase term of angular velocity compensation is constructed to compensate MTCC. The minimum entropy corresponding to angular velocity is searched by golden section method. Based on the imaging results of both scattering point model data and electromagnetic calculation data, it is verified that the proposed method can effectively correct the migration through resolution cell under the condition of sparse aperture and obtain high resolution images.

articleTitle: Machine learning methods applied in detection of buried targets for ground penetrating radar
abstract: The Ground penetrating radar (GPR) is a nondestructive tool to detect buried objects for infrastructure maintenance, archeological surveys, military application and other use. After analyzing the one-dimensional (A-scan), two-dimensional (B-scan) or three-dimensional (C-scan) images of GPR, the position and material of targets can be recognized. And machine learning techniques has become more popular in the data processing of GPR because their relative low cost, high speed and high accuracy. In this work, the application of some machine learning methods such as support vector machine (SVM), dictionary Learning (DL), neural networks (NNs) and hidden Markov models (HMMs) in the GPR for the detection of underground targets will be introduced.

articleTitle: Waveform design of LFM pulse train based on pulse width agility
abstract: In this paper, a method for suppressing range ambiguity and folded clutters is considered. A waveform design method, which adopts linear frequency modulation (LFM) pulse train based on pulse width agility, is proposed. The optimized pulse train, which is obtained by constructing pulse width agile waveforms and optimizing through dynamic programming, has good performance on suppressing range ambiguity and folded clutters. Besides, after joint mismatched filtering, the pulse-Doppler (PD) processing result of the pulse train shows excellent characteristics in both range and Doppler dimensions. Simulation results are provided to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Discrete side-lobe clutter suppression by designing orthogonal projection filter in space-based radar systems
abstract: For moving target detection with space-based array radar systems, the discrete side-lobe clutter caused by the isolated scatters or the moving scatters at antenna side-lobe direction, such as ships, small islands, buildings, power poles of the towers, and etc., usually has large power due to the wide antenna beams and shares the similar Doppler features with the real moving targets in the antenna main-lobe beam. The discrete side-lobe clutter cannot be well suppressed by using the space-time adaptive processing (STAP) and thus to result in false alarms. To address the issue, an orthogonal projection filter is deigned to suppress the discrete side-lobe clutter for space-based radar systems. In this method, the “potential targets”, including the real moving targets and the discrete side-lobe clutter, are firstly pre-selected after the STAP. Then, for the range-Doppler cells of the potential targets, the corresponding orthogonal projection filters are designed based on the differences of the space-time steering vectors between the discrete side-lobe clutter and the real moving targets. After applying the filters, the power of the discrete side-lobe clutter can be reduced significantly, while that of the real moving targets would change little, making it available to eliminate the false alarms. Finally, the theoretical analysis and the airborne radar experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: LPI-based joint node selection and power allocation for target localization in non-coherent distributed MIMO radar with low complexity
abstract: In this article, a low probability of intercept (LPI)-based joint radar node selection and power allocation strategy is proposed for target localization in distributed MIMO radar system. The proposed strategy aims to minimize the total transmit power while guaranteeing a predetermined the mean-square error (MSE) threshold for target location position and velocity estimation, which is evaluated by the Cramer-Rao lower bound (CRLB). In order to solve the underlying optimization problem, a Two-Step technique, which exploits the heuristic algorithm and the semidefinite programming (SDP) method, is introduced. Finally, simulation results demonstrate that the developed Two-Step solution algorithm has much higher efficiency when compared with the exhaustive search approach, and the presented strategy can also provide superiority over other existing schemes in terms of the achievable LPI performance.

articleTitle: Specific Emitter Identification based on empirical mode decomposition and convolutional neural network
abstract: Specific emitter identification (SEI) is an approach that discriminates different emitters by studying the association between the received signals and corresponding emitters, to help realizing advanced military and civil spectrum managing applications. The performance of traditional SEI technique based on expert knowledge and hand-crafted emitter features is limited in engineering, since the designing of features is essentially subject to a certain application scenario and radio environment. To provide a universal SEI method, this paper proposes a novel strategy using adaptive feature generation and deep learning architecture. In particular, the technique of empirical mode decomposition is performed on the non-stationary received signal, and further converted into a grey-scale image. Then a convolutional neural network is applied for feature extraction and emitter identification. In the experiment, we first build a dataset with same intermediate frequency tone signals from four identical Keysight E8267D signal sources with different output power. Then the performance of the proposed method is studied on this dataset, the results indicate that our method is effective for emitter identification.

articleTitle: Prototype metric network for few-shot radar target recognition
abstract: Radar target recognition always faces the problem of few-shot learning due to the complexity of target characteristics, the scarcity of samples,a and the difficulty of labelling. However, Few shot learning in radar target recognition follows the method of optical field and get some achievements, which ignores the characteristics of radar target resulting in low learning efficiency and recognition accuracy. Therefore, we propose three points to improve this situation. First, a metric network is proposed to learn metric function dependent on SAR data. Secondly, we use residual blocks as the feature extractor, which makes it have the ability to learn the complex process of feature extraction of radar target without the problems of degradation. Finally, we use softlabel to replace one-hot label to improve generation ability. We use MSTAR dataset obtained from Sandia national laboratory to verify the algorithm. It is showed that recognition rate of the proposed model is 10.4% higher than that of the prototypical network and is state-of-the-art.

articleTitle: A method for wind turbine clutter recognition and mitigation
abstract: In this paper, a method for wind turbine clutter (WTC) recognition and mitigation based on support vector machine (SVM) and sparse reconstruction is proposed. First, the wavelet transform is performed on the signal to construct a feature vector based on the WTC radar echo model, and a support vector machine is utilized to recognize whether a WTC is exist. Second, a dictionary will be constructed for strong interference components of WTC, before utilizing sparse reconstruction to separate WTC signal. As a result the target signal will be reserved, achieving the mitigation of WTC. The effectiveness of this proposed method is demonstrated through simulation results.

articleTitle: Human motion recognition based-on micro-doppler simulations using transfer learning
abstract: Radar sensors provide unique advantages in human motion recognition, such as privacy protection, operating free from weather and light, etc. However, it is difficult to obtain large radar samples in contrast to optical images due to the limit of time cost and human resources. Although deep convolutional neural networks (DCNN) have achieved great success in image classification, the lack of training samples remains a key problem. In this paper, we utilize micro-doppler simulated data to enlarge training samples, with which bistatic convolutional neural networks (Bistatic-CNN) are pretrained and later we use transfer learning to improve the accuracy of human motion recognition. Furthermore, we compare online dataset from Carnegie Mellon University (CMU) with Kinect sensor in order to figure out the differences. Finally, both simulated data are used as training samples for transfer learning.

articleTitle: Adaptive velocity ambiguity resolution algorithm based on gradient descent
abstract: For Pulse radars, the Doppler spectrum of the targets will fold in the range of radar frequency measurement and the velocity ambiguity occurs, when the Doppler frequency of the target is larger than a single pulse repetition frequency (PRF). Many classical methods of solving velocity ambiguity depend on the distance-change rate. The poor or unknown accuracy of distance may result in unreliable ambiguity resolution. In this paper, an objective function of resolving the velocity ambiguity for staggered PRI radar is proposed. The gradient descent with a self-adaptive updating learning rate is introduced to calculate the ambiguity. The proposed method can find out the true velocity of the target with a small number of iterations, which is not affected by the distance accuracy.

articleTitle: Space-frequency adaptive processing based on subspace technology
abstract: When adaptive antenna array is applied to navigation receiver for anti-jamming, the traditional spatial algorithms cannot deal with broadband interference. Although space-time algorithm can resist broadband interference, it demands large amount of calculation and accurate delay, so this article use the space-frequency adaptive algorithm suppress broadband interference. Compared with the classical space-frequency PI algorithm, introducing subspace technique in frequency domain to further improve the ability of interference suppression. The effectiveness of the algorithm is verified by computer simulation.

articleTitle: Hybrid hidden markov modeling for target recognition based on high-resolution radar signal
abstract: Hidden Markov Model (HMM) is a commonly used modeling approach for the radar target recognition based on high-resolution range profile (HRRP). The HMM describes HRRP with the assumption of Gaussian observation probability, which results in the inaccurate description due to the non-Gaussian property of HRRP. To this end, we propose a hybrid HMM framework, which uses an extra model to fit the observation probability rather than making distribution assumptions. The extra model estimates the posterior probability of the state, and then can calculate the pseudo observation probability, which in turn modulates the other model parameters in HMM. The interplay between HMM and the extra model ultimately leads to a better description for observed data. In this paper, we use the support vector machine (SVM) and deep neural network (DNN) separately as the extra model and validate the superiority of our hybrid HMM in HRRP-based target recognition.

articleTitle: Attitude angle formula derivation for the two-axis-stabilized platform of the ship-borne radar
abstract: The relationship between ship coordinate system and geodetic Cartesian coordinate system is analyzed, the composition of the two-axis-stabilized platform is introduced, ship attitude angles are defined in the geodetic Cartesian coordinate system, the two-axis-stabilized platform attitude angles are defined in ship coordinate system. when the value of ship attitude angles and two-axis-stabilized platform angles are given, this paper introduced the radar beam attitude angle and rotation angle formulas by use of space analytic geometry method, which provides a theoretical basis for the two-shaft-stabilized platform servo-control and radar beam angle compensation.

articleTitle: High-performance radar data recorder architecture based on NVMe P2P transaction and PCIe switch network
abstract: The radar data recorders need higher data storage performance with the improvement of radar technology. In this paper, we propose a new radar data recorder architecture based on NVMe (Non-Volatile Memory Express) SSD (Solid-State Drive) array on the PCIe (PCI Express) switch network and P2P (peer-to-peer) DMA transaction. We use the cascading capability of PCIe switch to construct NVMe SSD array for data capacity expansion rapidly. The NVMe driver in user-level based on the VFIO framework of the IOMMU function is developed to implement the DMA operation between the NVMe SSD and other PCIe devices. An FPGA, with a PCIe DMA engine and data streaming management logic, acts as the radar data receiver. It is NVMe P2P transaction that makes the radar data directly reach the NVMe SSD efficiently, without passing through CPU memory. The file system format is dissected for building data files in SSD directly. According to the test result, the data recording bandwidth reaches about 5GB/s in PCIe Gen3 x8 mode. We conclude this architecture can greatly improve the radar data storage bandwidth and capacity with simple structure, low cost and high flexibility.

articleTitle: Designing radar waveform with constant modular and low integrated sidelobe level
abstract: The topic of radar waveform optimisation has drawn much attraction recently. In this paper, the problem of designing unimodular sequences with low autocorrelation sidelobes for pulse compression radars is addressed, and two novel approaches based on phase optimisation are presented. One of them resorts to the conventional unconstrained optimisation theory to search the phase vector of the waveform vector. Contrary to the aforementioned scheme, the other method carries out an in-depth analysis of the relationship between the phases of the elements in the unimodular sequence and successively updates the vector with a closed-form solution in an element-by-element manner at each iteration, which processes lower computational complexity. Some representative numerical simulations are provided to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed methods.

articleTitle: A novel method of ship detection by combining space-borne SAR and GNSS-R
abstract: The detection of ship targets under medium and high sea conditions is confronted with the challenges of high sea clutter energy and image defocusing of ship target caused by its movement. This paper proposes a concept of integrated detection system of space-borne Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) and Global Navigation Satellite System-Reflection (GNSS-R), which combines the high-resolution imaging capability of space-borne SAR and multi-angle detection capability of GNSS-R to conduct imaging and detection of ships under medium and high sea conditions. This paper focuses on the concept and characteristics of space-borne SAR and GNSS-R combined detection system, and presents the joint processing process of SAR signal and multi-station GNSS-R signal, so as to reduce the energy of sea clutter under medium and high sea conditions and improve the detection performance of ship target. Through the preliminary simulation analysis of SAR signal and GNSS-R signal joint processing, it is shown that Signal to Clutter and Noise Ratio (SCNR) of ship target can improve more than 3 dB.

articleTitle: A position error calibration algorithm for conformal arrays
abstract: The conformal array has inherent advantage of processing polarization information for its antennas equip distinct patterns that influenced by surface curvature and antenna orientation. When antennas suffer from position errors, not only spatial responses but also polarization responses change a lot. Customary calibration algorithms designed for scalar arrays focus only on the spatial perturbations, and their performances degrade when extended to conformal arrays. To cope with that, a position error calibration algorithm for conformal arrays based on calibrated sources is proposed. Firstly, we build a precise model with disturbed polarization responses involved, and separate the position error into the height direction and axial direction. Axial errors in polarization responses are estimated firstly, and then substituted into the designed optimization function to calculate height errors. Simulations validates the performance of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Research on synthetic aperture radar hybrid jamming method based on 1 bit sampling
abstract: In this paper, a 1-bit hybrid jamming method against synthetic aperture radar (SAR) is proposed, which improves the elusiveness of a SAR jammer while reducing the complexity and cost of the jammer significantly. In the proposed method, the SAR signal is 1-bit intercepted and modulated to generate the DJ with false target. On this basis, the DJ is further quantized using time-varying thresholds (TVT). By adjusting parameters of the jammer, the hybrid jamming result combining the DJ with radio frequency interference (RFI) or barrage jamming is achieved in the SAR image, making it confusing to unscramble the true target among the DJ, barrage jamming, and RFI. The validity of the proposed method is verified by simulations.

articleTitle: Paralle acceleration of multi-mode SAR imaging on GPU
abstract: With the continuous expansion of the application field of multi-mode synthetic aperture radar (SAR) system, which can satisfy different imaging demands. In order to get SAR image, it is necessary to image the echo received by multi-mode SAR system. However, the huge computation of the imaging algorithm affects the processing efficiency of SAR system. The power of Graphics Processing Unit (GPU) can suffice the increasing demands in processing, which has been used in many common areas. The acceleration effect of GPU is very obvious compared with Central Processing Unit (CPU) platform. This paper proposed a Chirp Scaling acceleration algorithm based on GPU for multi-mode SAR, and comparison of computational time over traditional CPU and GPU platform. The experimental results shows that the GPU accelerated SAR imaging algorithm can achieve a good acceleration effect.

articleTitle: DOA estimation using an extended spatial smoothing with coprime MIMO radar
abstract: The direction of arrival (DOA) estimation problem for a coprime multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) radar is studied. To improve the angular resolution with limited elements, a sparse uniform linear transmitting array and a uniform linear receiving array are adopted in the MIMO radar, which lead to virtual sparse non-uniform linear array (SNLA) has large aperture. By setting the inter-sensor spacing to be mutually coprime integer multiples of half-wavelength, the angular ambiguity prblem caused by spatial subsampling is completely avoided due to the coprime property. To develop a DOA estimator for coherent targets, an extended spatial smoothing technique is proposed by taking advantage of the special array structure of the virtual SNLA, then the search-free root-multiple signal classification is extended for DOA estimation by taking the virtual SNLA as a part of a uniform linear array (ULA). Simulations results are provided to verify the good performance of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Reinforcement learning for robust radar tracking
abstract: In complicated environments with strong clutter and dense targets, radar tracking may encounter the issue of ambiguities in association. This paper proposes a reinforcement learning approach to reduce the number of misassociations in radar tracking. For each existing track, the characteristics of the target are learned to form a classifier, and then the classifier is employed for detection and association for this track. The parameters of each classifier will be updated using the feedback of the updated track. Experimental results on synthetic data and real data verify the effectiveness of our method.

articleTitle: Interior point method for sparse recovery space time adaptive processing
abstract: Convex optimization is one of the most common method for solving the problem of sparse recovery space-time adaptive processing (SR-STAP), however, most SR-STAP methods are focusing on the construction of problem model and they usually directly search the optimal solution by off-the-shelf software such as CVX. This way ignores the realization of convex optimization algorithms and makes an obstacle to the practical application. This paper proposed a general process of convex optimization algorithm for SR-STAP based on the interior-point method (IPM). It can be separated into two steps, first is to transform the SR-STAP problem to the second order cone programming (SOCP) problem, second is to solve above problem by IPM. The numerical simulation experiments illustrate that the proposed method can effectively recover clutter covariance matrix (CCM), moreover this structure can be easily extended to other convex optimization methods.

articleTitle: Pruning convolutional neural networks for remote sensing images
abstract: Deep convolutional neural networks (DCNNs) have shown excellent performance in remote sensing image processing. However, DCNNs contain many parameters and require many computational resources. It is very difficult to deploy DCNNs on spaceborne, airborne, or other mobile platforms with limited resources. It is necessary to compress the parameters of DCNNs. In this paper, we introduce a novel network pruning strategy that can prune redundant filters or weights of networks and preserve the performance of DCNNs in remote sensing image classification tasks. Unlike traditional pruning methods using a single criterion, this paper improves the pruning process based on the combined pruning method of multiple criteria. VGGNet and ResNet are used to validate our method. The dataset used in our experiments is the Moving and Stationary Target Acquisition and Recognition (MSTAR) dataset. The results demonstrate that our method is effective and can maintain the accuracy of a pruned model in remote sensing image classification tasks.

articleTitle: Human activity classification with radar based on Multi-CNN information fusion
abstract: Based on the radar echo data set of human activity published by University of Glasgow, this paper presents an intelligent classification method for six human activity (i.e. walking back and forth, sitting down on a chair, standing up, bending to pick up an object, drinking from a cup or glass, and frontal fall). This method uses six different ways to pre-process the data set and send them to a seven-layer CNN for training. The final classification results are generated by weighted voting of each model. Through 300 iterations, the classification accuracy of training data reaches 100%. And by uploading the test data classification results to the conference system, it is shown that the test accuracy rate is also 100%.

articleTitle: Modified multi-hypothesis tracking algorithm based on radar target appearance features
abstract: The marine radars are widely used in surveillance system for its convenience and cost-effectiveness, but it always suffers from the sea clutters and other inferences, and there are multiple maneuvering targets in the surveillance area. In these complex scenes, the traditional radar detector and tracker can result high false alarm and target loss. Especially the high false alarm scenes can bring an unacceptable computational burden.In this paper, we propose a practice tracking-by-detection method composed by a convolutional neural network (CNN) detector and a multiple hypothesis tracking (MHT) tracker. In order to deal with complex scenes efficiently and accurately, it utilize modified pruning strategies and multiple data information, such as the kinematic and appearance features. And the experiments on the self-designed simulation radar datasets prove that this method has the ability to reach a good performance with both accuracy and a low computational cost.

articleTitle: Parameter design of ground-based SAR interferometry for landslide deformation measurement
abstract: In this paper, the authors propose a design of ground-based SAR for digital elevation modulation acquisition and deformation measurement for landslide, and analyse the performance by simulation. A linear guide carries two interference antennas thus the system can both acquire elevation by interferometry and measure deformation by differential interferometry. Considering a general landslide monitoring scene, the geometric model of the antenna movement is established. Then, the spatial resolution and measuring accuracy are introduced through the signal models. A set of specific parameters are designed by comprehensively considering performance and cost. Imaging and interferometry simulations are carried out, whose results demonstrate the deformation measurement accuracy reaches millimetre level and the parameters in designing are reliable.

articleTitle: SCRFT-based long time coherent integration method for the hypersonic target
abstract: The long-time coherent integration (CI) technique can enhance the detection performance of radar for hypersonic target significantly. Conventional long time CI algorithms only take into account of the across range unit (ARU) without considering the scale effect. In fact, as the increase of target speed and time-bandwidth product of the sent signal, the scale effect may occur in the echo signal, affecting the pulse compression (PC) and CI performance. To eliminate the scale effect within the long time CI period, this paper introduces an effective method, namely the Scaled Radon Fourier transform (SCRFT). The SCRFT could obtain the energy accumulation for both the intra- and inter-pulse. In comparison with the conventional long time CI methods, the SCRFT can obtain better CI performance. This paper mainly introduces four equivalent implementation forms for the SCRFT and also makes some discussions about the proposed method. Eventually, numerical experiments are provided to evaluate the efficacy of the presented method.

articleTitle: Research on integrated navigation in AEB system based on multi-source fusion
abstract: An autonomous emergency braking system (AEBS) with environmental sensing and adaptive decision control is designed by using multi-source information fusion and adaptive control. To meet the continuous and high-precision navigation and positioning requirements of the AEB system, an integrated navigation system constructed by GNSS, INS, and millimeter-wave radar was designed. Two different strategies of integration are presented according to the availability of the GNSS information. If the GNSS information is available, the GNSS/INS loose coupled integrated navigation is used and if the GNSS information is unavailable, it adopts the velocity constraints to aid the integration navigation algorithm. The test results show that when GNSS information is unavailable, the velocity accuracy of integrated navigation can be maintained within 0.5 m/s. It ensures the navigation accuracy and continuity of the AEB system.

articleTitle: Experimental study of azimuth-elevation three-dimensional imaging at terahertz frequencies
abstract: In this paper, the azimuth-elevation three-dimensional (3D) imaging model is established for terahertz radar, and a fast imaging method based on the non-uniform inverse fast Fourier transform is proposed. Moreover, the azimuth-elevation imaging experiment at terahertz frequencies was conducted for the first time, and the 3D imaging result of the Siemens star model is achieved using real-world data. Then, the effectiveness of the proposed imaging method and the high resolution of terahertz radar are validated.

articleTitle: A new method for retrieve significant wave height using deep learning
abstract: A new method for retrieve the significant wave height of ocean waves using deep learning. At present, the retrieve method based on deep learning cannot obtain the significant wave height from the original radar image. Therefore, we propose an end-to-end network based on deep learning to retrieve the significant wave height. We use real radar images as the dataset. These images are collected by the WaMos II radar system from a scientific research ship, and the label is the significant wave height output by the WaMos II radar system. In order to verify the effectiveness of the model, we propose a new evaluation standard ARE(average relative error), and The ARE of the model is 0.017.

articleTitle: Distorted SAR target recognition with virtual SVM and AP-HOG feature
abstract: Synthetic aperture radar (SAR) plays an indispensable role in national defence and civil fields due to its unique advantages. Although many methods have been proposed, the recognition to SAR images still faces many difficulties, especially to distorted images. This paper first improves the morphological methods attribute profiles (APs) which is widely employed with optical, and hyperspectral images in particular. We combine the APs method with histogram of oriented gradients (HOG) feature (called AP-HOG) to make it suitable for SAR images. Then, the SVM model is used to identify the labelled samples (i.e., Support Vectors) that are closest to the separating hyperplane with maximum margin. We generate different degrees of distorted images based on support vectors, and use the distorted image and the support vector as a new training set for retraining to improve the recognition effect of the distorted image. Finally, we perform experimental verification based on the MSTAR dataset, which proves the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Segmented random sparse MIMO-SAR 3-D imaging based on compressed sensing
abstract: This paper presents a segmented random sparse multiple-input and multiple-output synthetic aperture radar (MIMO-SAR) 3-D imaging based on compress sensing (CS). Since the targets of interest for unmanned ground vehicle (UGV) forward looking array are usually sparse, the system complexity can be reduced using CS theory.
