The sparsity is determined by 2-D images of different positions during UGV is moving forward, which can reduce the reconstruction time by reducing iterations. Combining the MIMO array and the path of UGV, 3-D imaging of the forward scene can be achieved. Segmented random sparse of the original data from MIMO-SAR ensure the accuracy of 3-D reconstruction, by using sufficient bandwidth and spatial information. Simulation results are presented to demonstrate the validity of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Advance stagger scheduling of pulses in cognitive radar networks
abstract: Pulse conflict in radar networks can reduce the quality of imaging and cause the waste of resources. In order to solve the problem of pulse conflict between different sub-radars in the multi-target imaging scene, a method is proposed to stagger the pulse conflict in advance by a virtual timing sequence. In this process, it is also avoided to cover the target with high priority when the radar resource is allocated with low priority. This resource scheduling method can make good use of radar spare time to avoid pulse conflict and the feasibility is verified by simulation. What's more, it can be seen from the results that the method can effectively avoid the pulse conflict, thus improving the pulse utilization rate and the conflict utilization rate.

articleTitle: Hand gesture recognition scheme based on millimeter-wave radar with convolutional neural network
abstract: Gesture is a basic human feature and an indispensable part of interpersonal communication. The development of gesture recognition technology has made it possible for humans to interact with machines and other devices. The millimeter-wave radar can detect range, speed, and angle information during gesture movement, thereby achieving the purpose of identifying different gestures with stronger environmental adaptability. In this paper, we use the AWR1443 millimeter wave radar developed by Texas Instruments to collect gesture signal. According to the characteristics of the signal, the signal processing algorithms such as FFT are used to extract the range and Doppler frequency shift information. Then the range and Doppler frequency shift information are respectively coupled with time to form the Range-Time Matrix (RTM), Doppler-Time Matrix (DTM), and Range-Doppler Matrix (RDM). Based on this, a data set for gesture recognition is established, and the purpose of gesture recognition is achieved by training neural network. We design a RD-T network to make full use of RTM and DTM information. In the end, we replace the MLP in RD-T network with the LSTM to compare performance of LSTM and RD-T.

articleTitle: Recognition of overlapped radar signals via VMD-based multi-label learning
abstract: In complex electromagnetic environment, it is more likely to receive overlapped radar signals. In order to recognize the individual modulation types of these signals, this paper proposes a novel multi-label learning framework consisting of two modules. The first one is VMD-based feature extraction, which is effective and flexible to reconstruct original signals while maintaining useful information. The second one is complex deep network which can be trained simply with single-modulated signal samples. Experiments have demonstrated that the proposed method can achieve better performance than other methods under low signal-to-noise ratio conditions.

articleTitle: Intermediate frequency design criterion for reducing spectrum aliasing distortion in binary phase-coded radar system
abstract: The binary phase-coded waveform, a kind of pulse compression waveform, is widely used in many radar systems. However, its out-of-band spectral sidelobes will cause distortions in practical radar system. One of the distortions, called spectrum aliasing distortion, will occur when the intermediate frequency (IF) signal at fIF is sampled by a sampling rate fS. An IF design criterion in binary phase-coded radar system is proposed to reduce the spectrum aliasing distortion by using the spectrum property of binary codes. The simulations show that with the suitable design of IF the digital signal processing results will be closer to the designed performance, such as the peak sidelobe level (PSL).

articleTitle: A novel multicomponent LFM signal detection based on fast block FRFT
abstract: Aiming at solving the problem that detection of multicomponent linear FM (LFM) signal with large numbers of sampling points cannot be realized in real time, a novel method which detects multicomponent LFM signal based on fast block fractional Fourier transform (FRFT) is proposed. First, the method divides the LFM signal into blocks to reduce computation power of FRFT. Second, each block is compensated with a phase multiplier and accumulated non-inherently in the fractional Fourier domain (FRFD) in order to obtain energy-gathering for different components. To further reduce the computational load, a fast FRFT is used. Finally, each LFM component can be distinguished by a detector with slow and fast thresholds and their parameters are estimated from peaks and their locations in the FRFD. Compared with the traditional direct FRFT method, the proposed method has the benefits including significant decrease of computational load and the possibility to perform computations in parallel. The effectiveness of this method is verified by computer simulation.

articleTitle: Ship detection in marine radar images based on a modified YOLOv3-tiny
abstract: Deep learning has shown great success on object detection task for optical images, yet it's rarely used in marine radar target detection. It is mainly due to the scarce of the labelled marine radar datasets for deep learning. To mitigate such effect, we build a pseudo-color marine radar dataset, which utilizes rich temporal information to remarkably enhance the accuracy of deep radar detectors. Meanwhile, the state-of-the-art one stage deep detector, YOLO family, is transferred into this field. Eventually, we modify the architecture of YOLOv3-tiny by attaching the prediction heads to shallower layers. Based on the pseudo-color dataset, our method, Shallow YOLOv3-tiny, is able to match the speed and model size of the standard YOLOv3-tiny while improving the accuracy significantly. Thus, our method is excellent at performing radar target detection tasks on embedded devices with low computing power and limited memory.

articleTitle: Constant modulus waveform design for MIMO radar transmit beampattern synthesis
abstract: Multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) radar enables the antenna elements to transmit different waveforms freely. This waveform diversity provides great flexibility in transmit beampattern synthesis. By appropriately designing transmit waveforms, we can manage the radiation power effectively. In particular, more power would be concentrated into the interested spatial region, which is very useful in improving the signal noise ratio at the receive point. In this paper, we propose a novel method to optimize the transmit beampattern directly with constant modulus constraint. In the first step, we relax the fourth-order objective function as a quadratic one. In the second step, based on the majorization-minimization (MM) algorithm, we provide an iterative method, to solve the non-convex optimization problem efficiently. Lastly, simulation results demonstrate the superiority of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Study of water surface acoustic wave detection based on terahertz radar
abstract: Underwater targets mainly transfer information by acoustic wave. Underwater acoustic sources cause water to vibrate with the same frequency. The information of water surface acoustic wave can be used for the detection of the underwater targets. Terahertz (THz) wave belongs to millimeter wave, Terahertz radar can be used for the detection of micro-moving feature because the micro-Doppler feature of the Terahertz echo is obvious. The survey and distinguish of underwater targets may be finished by terahertz radar.

articleTitle: A strategy design of using difference beam to improve airspace coverage of LSS target early warning radar
abstract: In recent years, with the widespread application of drones in various fields, the problem of LSS target control in urban airspace, especially in the airspace of the airport, has become increasingly serious. Phased array radar has the advantages of mature technology and high reliability, so it plays an important role in early warning of low-slow-small targets. This paper studies the application of Sum and Difference beams in the search of low-slow-small targets, based on an existing low-slow target early warning radar. This paper also proposes a new strategy design that uses difference beams to improve the coverage of the pitch dimension of the phased array radar. It is proved by engineering practice that this method effectively improves the detection of low-slow small targets in short-range high altitude by phased array radar.

articleTitle: Design and implementation of multi-channel high speed digital transceiver system for P-L band radar
abstract: This paper introduces the design and implementation of multi-channel high speed transceiver system for P-L band radar.The system adopts high speed AD/DA chips to realize the RF direct generation and sampling of arbitrary waveform signals in the range of 2GHz. By adjusting the relative trigger relationship between the system clock and the control logic, the synchronization design of each channel's working clock, reference clock and data transmission is realized .And the transmit and receive synchronization of multiple AD/DA channels is guaranteed. The synchronization consistency between the tested channels is within 5ps.

articleTitle: High resolution radar ground clutter analysis at W-band
abstract: In this paper, the authors analyse the amplitude distribution of high resolution ground clutter using a W-band radar. Six types of backgrounds are investigated. The goodness-of-fit test is used to determine the probability density function. The results show that the distributions of most backgrounds can be approximated by the Weibull distribution.

articleTitle: Receiver placement in passive radar through GDOP coverage ratio with TDOA-AOA hybrid localization
abstract: This paper formulates an optimization problem of receiver placement in passive radar system comprised of third-party non-cooperative transmitters and a single receiver. In passive radar, the receiver placement is of significance to the radar performances since the positions of non-cooperative transmitters are beyond control. In order to improve the localization performances in passive radar, a receiver placement method by geometric dilution of precision (GDOP) coverage ratio is proposed. To ensure high accuracy in passive localization, time difference of arrival and angle of arrival (TDOA-AOA) hybrid localization method is selected to calculate the GDOP. Moreover, in order to solve this receiver placement optimization problem, an receiver placement method which is based on the GDOP ratio in radar surveillance area is proposed. Finally, the proposed method shows its validity and advantage in solving the placement optimization problem via simulations.

articleTitle: Range ambiguity suppression for spaceborne SAR based on up/down chirp modulation and twice range compressions
abstract: There exists some range ambiguity areas for spaceborne synthetic aperture radar (SAR) with higher pulse repetition frequency (PRF), and range ambiguity to signal ratio (RASR) is very important for application but hard to suppress. In this paper, linear frequency modulation (LFM) pulses with up and down chirp were transmitted and twice range compressions are implemented during image formation. Range ambiguity echo is focused in the first range compression and the peaks are filtered to reduce the range ambiguity energy. After that inverse range compression is implemented. Then the second range compression and azimuth compression are implemented to get focused SAR image. This novel method can suppress range ambiguity signal with a slightly more complicated LFM signal and remain good image quality of the targets in main-lobe area. Simulation experiments validate the proposed method.

articleTitle: Clutter suppression based on wiener smoothing in distributed radar with moving platforms
abstract: Distributed radar, which consists of several radar nodes and a fusion center, was firstly introduced by Lincoln laboratory. By inter-node data processing, the entire system can be equivalent to a big and powerful monostatic radar. Clutter suppression in distributed radar on moving platforms is considered in this paper. A method based on Space-Time Wiener Smoothing is developed to realized reliable target detection, where sequential coherent and non-coherent processes are performed to achieve clutter whitening and inter-node accumulation. By establishing the clutter model, and Monte Carlo simulation, it is verified that the proposed method could suppress the clutter echo well, whose performance is insensitive to synchronization error.

articleTitle: Fast coherent detection approach for maneuvering target with complex motions
abstract: Maneuvering target usually confronts issues of range cell migration (RCM) and Doppler frequency spread (DFS) when conducting the coherent integration process. To address these issues and achieve good detection performance, this paper proposes a computationally efficient approach without motion parameters searching. Particularly, the proposed approach firstly performs the third-order keystone transform (TKT) to eliminate the third-order RCM (TRCM). Then, the bilinear parametric symmetric self-correlation processing (BPSSP), scaling Fourier transform (SCFT) and inverse Fourier transform (IFT) are successively operated to estimate the acceleration and velocity. Afterwards, the improved second-order phase differentiation (ISPD) is performed to estimate target's jerk. Utilizing the estimated parameters, the compensation functions could be constructed to eliminate the remaining RCMs and DFSs as well as to achieve the coherent integration of target energy. Compared with other classical approaches, the proposed approach could balance the detection capability and computation efficiency without the blind speed side-lobe (BSSL) effect. Eventually, simulation data verifications are conducted to evaluate the efficacy of presented approach.

articleTitle: Multi-target tracking scheduling optimization under active jamming
abstract: In this paper, the time resource scheduling optimal method for phased array radar (PAR) is studied, which focuses on tracking multi-targets under active blanket jamming. First of all, the mutual information (MI) criterion is introduced as the quantitative metrics of target tracking. Secondly, the system model about radar echo and path gain are derived from the perspective of time resource. Finally, the time resource optimal scheduling model is established, and the improved genetic algorithm is applied to solve it. The simulation results demonstrate the outperformance of the proposed methods in maximizing the number of effectively tracked targets, and the overall tracking performance of the effective tracking target is improved.

articleTitle: Design of conical horn antenna for ground penetrating radar based on flare angle
abstract: GPR(Ground Penetrating Radar) is a high resolution geophysical technique and a non-destructive technology to utilize in detecting the surface in which has the buried objects and structures such as ground layers, landmines, roads and concrete foundations. A horn antenna has better gain enhancement in same frequency range as compare with other GPR type antennas and it is suitable for demining process. In this paper, designing the pyramidal horn antennas calculated from flare angel formula at thirteen flare angle values and making the GPR-scenario with the chosen pyramidal horn design among thirteen designs have been presented by using ANSYS Electronic Desktop 2018, HFSS software.

articleTitle: Target localization based on doppler frequency and range sum measurement
abstract: Target localization is an important technology in passive radar system. An algorithm for target localization based on Doppler frequency and azimuth measurement in passive detection system is proposed in this paper. In this algorithm the mathematical model and the computational relationship are constructed for passive radar system. Also the computation progress for target localization and the process for fuzzy solution are given. In the simulation experiment, the typical scene is constructed and the precision of target localization is also analyzed. Finally, the conclusion is given that the algorithm for target localization based on Doppler frequency and azimuth measurement is effective.

articleTitle: Low probability of intercept-based collaborative transmit resource and bandwidth allocation strategy for target tracking in distributed radar network system
abstract: In this study, a collaborative transmit resource and bandwidth allocation (CTRBA) strategy based on the low probability of intercept (LPI) is presented for target tracking in the distributed radar network system. The primary goal of this strategy is to minimize the total resource consumption while satisfying a predetermined target tracking performance requirement. The closed-form expression for the predicted Bayesian Cramer-Rao lower bound (BCRLB) is derived and computed to gauge the target tracking accuracy. It is shown that the CTRBA is a mixed-Boolean and non-convex optimization problem. We propose an efficient two-step solution methodology to solve the resulting problem. Simulation results demonstrate that the CTRBA strategy can achieve the desired tracking performance with less resource consumption.

articleTitle: A non-iterative objective radiation field generation method for 1-bit coding metasurface
abstract: Digital coding and programmable metamaterials have attracted widespread attention in recent years, which have brought new ideas to the fields of communication, detection, and imaging. Optimizing the code pattern to achieve fast, high accuracy radar detection has practical significance for vital signal detection in scenarios where the body position information is known. In this paper, we derived the corresponding encoding mode from the desired radiation pattern and proposed a non-iterative objective radiation field generation method for 1-bit coding metasurface. Our simulation experiments prove that the method we proposed could generate multiple radiation pattern by only one coding metamaterial without iteration. The comparison of the proposed method and the modified GS algorithm is given in the simulation part to show its superiority. The vital signal detecting application of the proposed method is also illustrated in the simulation part. The proposed method may simplify the specific code pattern's calculation process of future smart devices with reprogrammable functions, which may lead to advances in various applications such as aperture-coded imaging and, directional radiation, specifically designated spot monitoring and long-distance vital signal detection.

articleTitle: Gesture recognition and segmentation based on millimeter-wave radar
abstract: Nowadays, gesture recognition with radar is attracting wide attention from researchers and practitioners. The classification of an isolated and segmented gesture has been studied thoroughly. However, the detection, classification and segmentation of a series of gestures embedded in a data stream remains intractable. To address this problem, we develop a gesture recognition system based on millimetre-wave radar and deep learning. The radar measures range and Doppler features of gestures with high resolution. The data stream collected by radar is slightly pre-treated to suppress interference and extract information. A sliding window is used to slice those streams into appropriate data units, which are then fed to convolutional neural networks to estimate the probabilities of gesture types. By utilizing the change in those probabilities with time, the joint recognition and segmentation of gestures is realized. Experiments with real data shows that the recognition accuracy of 5 gestures is up to 92.48%.

articleTitle: An approach to videoSAR moving target detection based on deep learning with RPCA improvement
abstract: VideoSAR generates image sequence continuously at a high frame rate, which provides great advantages for moving target detection. A key technology in the field of VideoSAR is moving targets detection. Most of the existing moving target detection methods for VideoSAR image sequence are based on shadows. However, the target shadows are difficult to obtain when the sensitivity of the radar system is not high enough. Instead, we detect moving target in VideoSAR frame via the bright lines formed by Doppler shift based on deep CNN (convolutional neural networks). In order to improve the CNN detection accuracy, the RPCA (Robust Principal Component Analysis) is adopted in this paper to separate the foreground image of VideoSAR. After the foreground images are added to the dataset for training, the experimental result verifies that the problems of missed detection, false detection and inaccurate target positioning are significantly improved and the mAP (mean Average Precision) of YOLOv3 for VideoSAR moving target has been particularly increased from 70.99% to 81.69%.

articleTitle: On scattering characteristics of winter wheat at different phenological period based on Sentinel-1A SAR images
abstract: Phenophase period refers to the periodic natural phenomena of plants under the influence of environmental factors and human activities. In recent years, synthetic aperture radar (SAR) has been used to growth monitoring of crops. Due to complex morphological changes at different growth stage of crops, single-phase SAR data unable provide sufficient information to analyze scattering characteristics at different phenological period. In this paper, the scattering characteristics of winter wheat are studied, using time series dual-polarization Sentinel-1A SAR images. And winter wheat planting region in Kaifeng city Henan Province is selected as the study area. Time series C-band radar backscatter coefficient is extracted, then analyze correlation between numerical evolution and phenological change with different polarization data. The variation trend is verified by field measured data. The results show that dual-polarization SAR image is great practical significance for winter wheat phenological monitoring.

articleTitle: A high resolution ISAR imaging method base on image fusion with low SNR
abstract: In order to achieve high resolution ISAR imaging by launching random chirp frequency stepped signal with sparse range and cross range under low SNR, a high resolution ISAR imaging method based on image fusion is proposed in this paper. Firstly, the ISAR image with high range resolution under low SNR, in which the range imaging is realized in view of joint sparse model and the cross range imaging is realized based on traditional compressed sensing model, is obtained. Secondly, the ISAR image with high cross range resolution under low SNR, in which the cross range imaging is realized in view of joint sparse model and the range imaging is realized based on traditional compressed sensing model, is received. Finally, the two ISAR images with higher range resolution and cross range resolution respectively are directly fused, then the final high resolution ISAR imaging results are required. Due to the same data and observation target, the ISAR imaging results via different imaging methods can be directly fused without image rotation or correction and other processing. Therefore, the proposed method not only can achieve high resolution imaging under low SNR, but also has the advantages of simple realization. The effectiveness of this method is verified by the simulation experiments.

articleTitle: A data processing method of maritime surveillance radar on mechanical and electronical scanning mode
abstract: The maritime surveillance radar is prone to have the problems of false track initiation and tracking loss due to the low tracking accuracy of the target using the traditional data processing strategy. To solve these problems, a data processing strategy is proposed based on a mechanical and electronical scanned radar. As the problem of velocity ambiguity is caused by far detection distance and low pulse repetition frequency (PRF), the overlapping algorithm is used and the corresponding constraints are employed for optimization. The problem of too many false tracks as a result of background noise is solved by using Hough transform and logic-based algorithm optimized under the relevant constraints. In addition, an optimization method of Kalman filtering is proposed based on the predicted value of the stable course of maritime targets to solve track jitter. The results of experiment show that this strategy is effective and improves the accuracy of radar in locating and tracking targets.

articleTitle: Simulation and analysis of radar signatures for objects floating on time-evolving sea surface
abstract: A new procedure is developed to simulate the range-Doppler signatures for objects floating on time-evolving sea surface. First, a time-varying scene consisting of a series of integrated sea-object models is constructed by the time-evolving rough sea surface and the micro-motioned objects driven by the sea dynamics. The shooting and bouncing ray (SBR) technique, combined with high-frequency asymptotic methods is used to calculate electromagnetic (EM) scattering from the integrated sea-object scene at each specific radar pulse repeat time interval, where a unique strategy is proposed for the processing of EM coupling as well as occlusion among the simulated scene. Numerical results are presented to demonstrate the validity and usefulness of the proposed procedure.

articleTitle: Accuracy analysis of interferometric imaging radar altimeter for baseline oscillation
abstract: The interferometric imaging radar altimeter with wide swath will satisfy the requirement of high precision, high temporal and spatial resolution sea surface height (SSH) for sub-mesoscale ocean features. In this paper, the model of spaceborne baseline oscillation on the high accuracy of sea surface height (SSH) is established considering the decoherence due to azimuth shift and antenna beam pointing jitter. A spectral analysis method is employed in order to improve the stability and the accuracy of spaceborne interferometric imaging radar altimeter. Without considering additional on-orbit calibration and validation and other techniques, the RMSE of SSH along the cross-track direction ranges from 0.39cm (in the near of the swath) up to 0.96cm (in the far of the swath) when the vibration amplitude is less than 0.04mm. The RMSE are reduced to 0.08~0.2cm after the low-frequency vibration amplitude restrained. Finally, the simulation has proven that the accuracy of sea surface height could be improved by restraining the baseline oscillation.

articleTitle: On the numeric construction of complete
abstract: In this paper, we consider the numerical design of complete complementary codes (CCC), which are quite different from traditional analytical approaches. The design task is formulated as minimizing the integrated sidelobe level (ISL) of a sequence set under unimodular constraint. Exploiting the algebraic structure of ISL, we calculate its value and derivative efficiently via FFT. Then, an algorithm based on BFGS (Broyden Fletcher Goldfarb and Shanno) method is proposed, which is suited to small scale problems. For large scale cases, another line-search-free Limited-Memory BFGS based algorithm is preferred as it omits the memory intensive Hessian matrix update and time-consuming line-search. Simulation results confirm the effectiveness of the proposed algorithms. s, when used to design complementary set of sequences, which is a special case of CCC, they outperform the existing state-of-the-art algorithms.

articleTitle: Experimental study on HRRP-based airborne target recognition using neural networks
abstract: High resolution range profile (HRRP) provides an effective approach to the airborne target recognition. However, the HRRP of airborne target is statistically variational and quite sensitive to the observation angles. Therefore, the traditional recognition approach based on feature extraction usually encounters trouble on finding reliable features. In this paper, we compared the performance of several popular neural networks using electromagnetic simulation data generated with 3-dimensional aircraft models. The experimental results show that neural networks without statistical learning capability, such as long short-term memory (LSTM) neural network, usually do not yield satisfying recognition performance with a limited number of samples. The discriminative infinitely Restricted Boltzmann machine (Dis-iRBM) exhibits stronger capability on learning the statistics of data and has the best performance, especially at harsh scenarios with limited samples, limited azimuth resolution and low signal-to-noise ratio. It is also found that using the data observed from the nose and the wings of the aircraft has the highest recognition rate. The study of this paper contributes to improving the application of neural networks in HRRP-based target recognition.

articleTitle: Simulation of wet atmospheric delay correction for interferometric imaging altimeter based on radiometer
abstract: Wet atmospheric delay is one of the main error sources affecting the measurement accuracy of interferometric imaging altimeter, which has an important impact on the observation performance of interferometric imaging altimeter. The measurement of the brightness temperature inversion wet delay equipped with a microwave radiometer is the main method for the correction of the wet delay of the interferometric altimeter. In this paper, the effect of delay error correction for different number of beams of radiometer is simulated. The root mean square error of radiometer after error correction is analyzed mainly in the case of single-beam, dual-beam, three-beam and multi-beam observations. Finally, it is concluded that with the increase of the number of beams of radiometer, the root mean square error after correction decreases obviously. In the case of multi-beam, although the root-mean-square error is smaller than other beams, the compensation effect has little difference with the increase of the number of beams. In the actual engineering implementation, the increasing number of beams will greatly increase the engineering difficulty. The purpose of this paper is to provide a reference for the beam design of radiometer.

articleTitle: Bistatic frequency diverse array radar range ambiguous clutter suppression
abstract: The bistatic radar has better detection performance and higher survival probability compared with the monostatic radar, but its clutter has serious limitation of range ambiguity and range dependence. This paper proposes a new solution to the severely range ambiguous clutter phenomenon of the bistatic radar. The bistatic Frequency Diverse Array (FDA) radar can separate different range ambiguous clutter since it provides extra degrees-of-freedom (DOFs) in range domain. This feature is useful for range ambiguous clutter suppression. However, range dependence of the spatial frequency also causes secondary range dependence of clutter from adjacent ranges in the bistatic FDA radar. We further alleviate the range dependence by compensating for the clutter. The obtained clutter training samples approximately satisfy the conditions of independent and identical distribution (IID). Therefore, the Doppler Warping (DW) method can be used to make the radar performance better. The simulation results prove the effectiveness of the proposed approach in range ambiguous clutter suppression.

articleTitle: Mainlobe interference suppression method based on blind source separation with support vector machine
abstract: The mainlobe interference causes seriously affects on the performance of radar system. Besides, the traditional adaptive beamforming method would severely deteriorate when the desired signal is contained in the training snapshots. In order to solve the problem, a mainlobe interference suppression method based on blind source separation with support vector machine is proposed in this paper. In the proposed method, the DOA estimation is used on the array received data to determine the number of separated signal channels. Then the blind source separation algorithm is used to separate the received signals to obtain independent target and interference signal waveforms. Finally, high-order features are extracted in the transform domain, and support vector machine (SVM) is used for target and interference identification for determining the target signal channel and completing interference suppression. The actual measured data processing results show that this method can effectively resist mainlobe suppression and deception interference.

articleTitle: Modified signal separation algorithm for wind turbine clutter suppression using morphological component analysis
abstract: Dynamic wind turbine clutter (WTC) seriously affects the target detection performance of weather radar. The modified signal separation for WTC suppression using morphological component analysis (MCA) is studied in this paper. The algorithm firstly decreases the morphological components of the radar echo by filtering the ground clutter. And then, the MCA approach is implemented and the overlapping rate of window blocks used in the short-time Fourier transform (STFT) is increased, which will reduce the spectrum leakage of WTC. Finally, the basis pursuit (BP) and split augmented Lagrangian shrinkage algorithm (SALSA) are presented to decompose radar return signal into the sum of the weather signal and the WTC. Simulation results show that the modified signal separation algorithm proposed in this paper can effectively mitigate the WTC and improve the target detection performance of weather radar, particularly in low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) environment.

articleTitle: 3D imaging of human based on simualated MIMO bio-radar echo
abstract: In recent years, MIMO bio-radar is widely used in medical, rescue, and other scenarios. In this paper, a MIMO bio-radar system with 8-transmitting channels and 8-receiving channels is simulated. Boulic model with 17 human body joints is selected as a detected subject. Based on the simulated echoes of the human target, a three-dimensionalimage can be built using BP imaging method. Then micro-Doppler signature is fully used in converting 3-D image into 2-D Doppler-enhanced frontal image. The processed results test the validation of the simulated method andimaging method.

articleTitle: Speckle suppression of SAR image using boundary and contextual constraint
abstract: Speckle suppression is a important preprocessing step for synthetic aperture radar (SAR). In this paper, a speckle suppression algorithm based boundary and contextual constraint is studied for enhancing image, which includes the establishment of speckle model based on boundary constraint, the analysis of speckle factor weighted constraint model based on contextual regularization, and the process of speckle factor estimation. The performance of this algorithm is validated by using the data acquired over an airship mounted SAR system.

articleTitle: A task scheduling algorithm for phased array radar based on dynamic time window
abstract: Phased array radar can realize the operation of multiple-target tracking, guidance and other working modes while searching, which can ensure the real-time completion of multiple tasks. Therefore, efficient scheduling algorithm is needed to make full use of radar time and energy resources. According to the three characteristic quantities involved in task priority and time urgency, this paper proposes an integrated priority determination method. In addition, the weight of the characteristic quantities is adjusted to meet the different load conditions of the scheduler. And a time window-based backtracking adaptive method is used to solve the conflict tasks at the same time, so as to ensure that the tasks with high priority in the scheduling interval (SI) are scheduled first. Simulation results show that, the proposed algorithm in this paper can effectively improve the success rate of task scheduling and significantly improve the performance of the scheduler.

articleTitle: Parallel implementation of SPWVD algorithm by using GPU with CUDA
abstract: Smoothed Pseudo Wigner-Ville Distribution (SPWVD) is a common and effective time-frequency analysis algorithm which is widely used in signal processing. It's improved from Wigner-Ville Distribution (WVD) by adding a window function both in the time domain and frequency domain which can effectively suppress cross-terms. However, it also enlarges the work remarkably. As a result, the application of SPWVD is greatly restricted. This paper proposed a parallel implementation of SPWVD based on Compute Unified Device Architecture (CUDA) which runs on GPU. By combining reduction operation and shared memory, we design a parallel summation method which can save a lot of time effectively. Numerical experiments are also provided to demonstrate that the proposed method is more efficient especially when the amount of data increases.

articleTitle: Stolt migration algorithm for impulse through-the-wall radar imaging based on compressive sensing
abstract: Impulse radar technology is commonly used for through-wall radar imaging (TWRI) owing to its simple hardware structure and range resolution enhancement. Compressive sensing technique has been applied to impulse TWRI to reduce the amount of measurement data and provide the enhanced imaging quality, which adopts a ray-tracing model and requires prior information of the transmitted pulse. In this paper, however, we propose a CS-based Stolt migration imaging algorithm for impulse TWRI system. The proposed imaging algorithm deduces the sparse transform between the raw measurement space data and the image space data and does not need a prior knowledge of the transmitted pulse. The numerical simulation results show that compared to the traditional Stolt migration imaging method, the proposed imaging algorithm can provide the improved imaging reconstruction quality and reduce the amount of space-time measurements at the cost of increased computation time.

articleTitle: A parallel optimization method for kernel correlation filter based on multi-core DSP
abstract: Target tracking is an important branch in the field of computer vision. In recent years, parallel computing efficiency becomes the key to improving real-time performance in multi-core DSP platforms. This paper proposes the concept of execution parallelism based on Open MP, optimizes Kernel Correlation Filter (KCF) with execution parallelism parameters, and compares it with inter-processor Communication (IPC). This paper aims at the KCF algorithm on the TMS320C6678 platform for the multi-core parallel development of the above two methods. With multiple data-sets, the results are all higher than 60 frames/s. With physical verification by connecting the video board, parallel scheme based on Open MP can achieve a tracking effect of 75 FPS, which has certain engineering practical significance.

articleTitle: The design of crossover based on microstrip ridge gap waveguide of dual-layer medium
abstract: This paper introduces a dual-layer medium type microstrip GWG. In the proposed structure, microstrip and metal pillar are placed in different mediums, the movement of the locations between microstrip and metal pillar will not affect each other. Compared with traditional single-layer medium type GWG, this structure simplifies the complexity of the design. Based on the microstrip GWG of dual-layer medium, a crossover device with a central frequency of 28GHz is designed. Two parallel microstrips are connected to realize the directional power of the crossover, the coupling degree within the bandwidth of 4GHz is within 0.5dB, and the bandwidth of 14.3% is achieved. The proposed crossover is a 0dB directional coupler. It can realize the directional distribution of power and it has good coupling, isolation and directional performance. Therefore, crossover can be well applied in the field of microwave technology.

articleTitle: DOA-range estimation of sin-FDA beamspace based on butler matrix
abstract: Frequency diverse array (FDA) radar has the ability of angle and range estimation. However, the computational complexity is high when spectral estimation is used. To solve this problem, we propose an angle and range estimation algorithm for the sin-FDA based on the Butler matrix beamspace transformation. Firstly, the design method of the beamspace is deduced and explained. Then, the receive signal is preprocessed through the constructed beamspace to reduce the dimension of signal processing while obtaining useful information. Finally, the signal which is obtained after preprocessing is introduced into the Capon and Music algorithm to estimate the parameters of targets. The influence of beamspace preprocessing on target parameter estimation under one target condition is simulated, and the root means square errors (RMSE) under different signal-to-noise ratios are calculated. The simulation results verify the correctness of the conclusion.

articleTitle: Robust beamforming algorithm based on convex optimization multiplier method
abstract: The performance of adaptive beamforming will degrade dramatically in practical application due to angle estimation error in interference signal. Therefore, a robust adaptive beamforming method based on convex optimization multiplier is proposed in this paper. In the proposed method, the DOA information of the interfering signal is firstly calculated using MUSIC algorithm. Then the spatial smoothing algorithm is used to de-correlate. In the following, the cost function is constructed by the Lagrange multiplier method. Finally, a set of optimal weight vectors can be obtained through iteration. Simulation results show that the proposed method can effectively reduce the effect of angle estimation error in interference signal.

articleTitle: A modified spaceborne high-squint SAR imaging algorithm based on azimuth nonlinear chirp scaling
abstract: To process the spaceborne high-squint SAR data, the linear range cell migration correction (LRCMC) is conducted firstly. Although the target linear range cell migration (LRCM) is removed and the range-azimuth coupling of two-dimensional spectrum is reduced through LRCMC, it also causes the azimuth spatial variation of focusing parameters. The spatial variation of focusing parameters is caused by azimuth spatial variation of slant-range and equivalent velocity in spaceborne SAR system. However, the most existed imaging algorithms neglect the azimuth spatial-variant equivalent velocity, which will decrease the imaging quality. In this paper, the azimuth spatial variation of focusing parameters is analysed precisely. And a modified imaging algorithm based on azimuth nonlinear chirp scaling is proposed. Simulation of high-squint strip-map data verifies the accuracy of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Status and prospects of metal space frame radome
abstract: Metal space frame (MSF) radome is built on the ground or ship, with large-span structure to protect radar against environmental factors. In this paper, the main mechanical and electromagnetic performance of the MSF radome is listed and the basic design ideas are described. The research status is summarized from computational analysis and structural design. Mechanical and electromagnetic integrated design methods, fast and hybrid algorithms, functional membranes are expected to be the focus of further research.

articleTitle: Research on parallel architecture design of radar real-time signal processing based on CPU-GPU heterogeneous platform
abstract: In view of the central processing unit (CPU) platform processing performance limits on computationally intensive tasks, as well as the FPGA + DSP<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[1-3]</sup> platform of software and hardware of high coupling and difficult defects, using the graphics processor (GPU) powerful parallel computing power, the CPU and GPU pipeline technology, heterogeneous systems with multithreading, GPU more and more flow, such as strategy, puts forward the real-time signal processing system of the multiple perspectives analysis methods, make full use of the independence between modules and signal processing algorithm concurrency features within the GPU.The experimental results show that, compared with the traditional MATLAB platform, the maximum acceleration ratio based on CPU-GPU heterogeneous platform can reach more than 20000, and the parallel architecture designed can fully meet the real-time requirements of radar signal processing.

articleTitle: Spatial-temporal tensor for robust detection within sea clutter
abstract: Robust radar target detection within sea clutter is a challenging subject in the field of radar signal processing. This paper proposes a novel detection method from the perspective of spatial-temporal tensor. We construct a spatial-temporal tensor by combining the received signals of neighbouring range bins, neighbouring search beams, and neighbouring scans. The kinetic features and characteristic features are then extracted from the tensor, and are combined for true target detection. Compared to the traditional detection method with the same detection probability, our method can significantly reduce the number of false alarms. Comparable experiments on real data verify the effectiveness of our method.

articleTitle: SAR target recognition using feature extraction of multi-scale monogenic components
abstract: In this paper, we combine the monogenic signal with the histogram of oriented gradient (HOG) feature, and propose a new low-level feature: Monogenic-HOG (MG-HOG); then use the bag of words (BoW) model to construct the middle-level feature. Most of the existed features are directly extracted from grayscale synthetic aperture radar (SAR) images. As an extended representation of analytic signals in high-dimensional space, the monogenic signal has excellent characteristics such as rotation and scale invariance in the potential extraction process, and it is also valuable in the image field. However, in the past related work, it is mostly used directly as the feature representation of the image. After experimental validation on the moving and stationary target acquisition and recognition (MSTAR) data set, the proposed feature extraction method has better performance than a number of existed methods.

articleTitle: On the processing of the squint sliding-spotlight SAR
abstract: For squint sliding-spotlight SAR imaging, sub-aperture range migration algorithm (RMA) and the azimuth scaling will result in the time-shift of azimuth signal. The time-shifts will lead to the failure of traditional sub-aperture algorithm and degrade the SAR image performance. In order to minimize the influence of time-shifts caused by the range cell migration correction (RCMC) in RMA and azimuth scaling steps, an improved sub-aperture algorithm based on zero-padding and a newly designed azimuth scaling Doppler-rate for squint sliding-spotlight SAR imaging is given. Simulation and real data results show the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: A multi-feature classification approach based on tensor and AIR distance for inshore ambiguity identification with multichannel SAR system
abstract: In inshore region, it is crucial to identify azimuth ambiguity for moving target (or ship) detection with multichannel synthetic aperture radar (SAR) system. To this end, a multi-feature classification approach based on tensor and affine invariant Riemannian (AIR) distance is proposed in this paper. The proposed method firstly extracts feature tensor (FT) of multichannel SAR images, including correlation coefficient between channels, multi-look interference phase, and spatial structural gradient information. Then, the core feature tensor (CFT) is obtained by alternating optimization and unfolded along the feature dimension and the feature covariance matrix (FCM) is constructed for each range-Doppler unit (RDU). With the AIR distance measure, the inshore region is divided into different clutter regions. Finally, the experiments on real measured data by TerraSAR-X demonstrate that the proposed method can accurately identify the azimuth ambiguity in inshore region.

articleTitle: A new model for waveform distortion required for pulse signal detection and measurement
abstract: Signal to noise ratio (SNR) is an important parameter to evaluate signal detection and measurement methods. However, the results may be worse even when SNR is high, especially under complex environment, where waveform distortion weights more. There are many researchers working on waveform distortion in satellite communication, electrical networks and measurement. However, the influence waveform distortion has on signal detection and measurement is not considered. In this paper, we propose parameters to depict relationship between waveform distortion and signal detection and measurement and propose a new model based on these parameters.

articleTitle: Radar jamming effectiveness evaluation method based on feature space weighting
abstract: Radar jamming effectiveness evaluation is very important in adaptive radar countermeasures. Most traditional methods based on cooperation, evaluating on allied side is not working in the battlefield. This paper proposed a radar jamming effectiveness evaluation method based on non-cooperative feature space weighting. Introduce cross entropy to delimit the ambiguity of similarity of signal parameter's features, the minimum value of cross entropy is the minimum value of ambiguity, and the similarity is becoming more and more clear, so that we can evaluating on the radar jamming effectiveness. This method could make evaluation result clear through the simulation.

articleTitle: Low-complexity implementation of parallel receiver for terahertz communication system
abstract: In this paper, we propose a low-complexity implementation of parallel receiver for high-speed terahertz communication systems, where a parallel timing recovery module and a parallel equalization module are considered. To reduce the hardware cost in timing recovery module, we introduce a ROM-based parallel interpolator and a modified parallel timing error detector, which reduce time delays, lookup tables (LUTs) and digital signal processor (DSP) slices by 25%, 26%, and 36%, respectively. On the other hand, a matched filter with minimum taps is inserted into the timing recovery loop, which reduces the hardware cost compared to the matched filter placed outside the timing recovery loop. To validate the performance of our improved parallel receiver, a fixed-point simulation is performed on MATLAB platform. Moreover, an 8Gbps 16QAM parallel receiver using our improved timing recovery module is implemented on the Xilinx ZCU111 evaluation board running at the frequency of 128MHz. The simulation and implementation results show that our improved parallel receiver has a superior bit error rate (BER) performance and a low implementation complexity.

articleTitle: A novel beam pointing calibration method for GeoSAR
abstract: In this paper we propose a novel high-precision beam pointing calibration method for GeoSAR(Geosynchronous Synthetic Aperture Radar, GeoSAR). The well-known amplitude comparison mono-pulse principle for angle Estimation is used to perform antenna beam pointing calibration. First the calibration beams for GeoSAR are designed, and then the LFM pulse beacon signal is transmitted and received by the ground calibration equipment. After data processing we can achieve high-precision antenna beam pointing results for GeoSAR. In order to verify the validity of the proposed method, a Ku-band reflector antenna system is deployed and the experimental results show that the beam pointing calibration accuracy is better than 0.01°, which confirm that the proposed method can provide a feasible and accurate solution to the GeoSAR beam pointing calibration.

articleTitle: Nonparametric resampling for high-squint synthetic aperture radar imaging
abstract: Synthetic aperture radar (SAR) image resampling is a key technology for SAR image geometric correction, interferometric and tomographic registration. In some geometry like the high-squint (HS) case, image spectrum will be distorted, folded and therefore, existing resampling methods will fail due to the resulting serious image degradation. To solve this problem, we propose a general nonparametric image resampling method for SAR. The main contribution is the new non-parametric method of morphologically generating image-domain interpolation kernel, which can be theoretically applied for an arbitrary SAR image focused either on slant range plane or ground plane. The presented approach is evaluated by showing resampled image quality improvement via the computer simulations.

articleTitle: Design of orthogonal discrete frequency coding waveforms via improved genetic algorithm
abstract: We develop a new efficient method for designing discrete frequency coding waveforms with linear frequency modulation (DFCW-LFM). The method integrates the genetic algorithm with linear congruence generator. The hybrid algorithm is carefully derived and analysed. Moreover, a succinct optimization criterion, which is based on the autocorrelation and cross-correlation of the ambiguous function, is derived to assess the performance of the DFCW-LFM. The simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of this method. Compared with other existing methods, the waveforms designed using our method have lower correlation levels.

articleTitle: Study on modeling unifiedly of rotor blade echo under non-uniform scattering background
abstract: The modeling of the rotor blade echo and the characteristics of micro-doppler under the background of non-uniform scattering are studied. Based on the position of the scattering points and the scattering coefficients distribution, three different non-uniform scenes of the rotor blade models are constructed and unifiedly expressed. On this basis, the effects of non-uniform scattering on the micro-doppler characteristic is studied from the two perspectives of time-domain and time-frequency domain. By comparing the simulation with uniform scattering conditions, the results verified the rationality of the unifiedly model of non-uniform scatteringwhich has important theoretical and application value for the modeling of micro-motion targets.

articleTitle: Design and analysis of chaos-based random multi-carrier waveform
abstract: Application of Multi-carrier waveform technology in radar systems has recently attracted attention. In this paper, to increase the randomness and performance of multi-carrier waveform, the subcarriers are phase modulated by chaos-based random sequences, and the frequencies of subcarriers also change with chaos-based random sequences. Ambiguity function, pulse compression, and the further research of the influence of different chaotic maps on signal performance are all researched and analyzed by simulations. Simulation results show that the ambiguity function of the proposed waveform is close to the "pins",having good pulse compression side-lobe and resolution characteristic.Due to the randomness of the carrier frequency and the internal code,lower pulse compression side-lobes are achieved when the code sequences are different from each subcarrier, and the proposed waveform has structural complexity and uncertainty, which is good for achieving orthogonal multi-carrier waveform set, enhancing LPI and ECCM performance of random multi-carrier waveform.

articleTitle: Synthesized high resolution imaging using a frequency agile waveform with costas modulated
abstract: Frequency agility and complex code modulated waveforms are employed in many radars due to their good electronic counter-counter measures (ECCM) performance. Except this, another advantage of frequency agility is the synthetic wideband, which is benefit for obtaining high range resolution, i.e., one-dimensional (1D) imaging. This paper describes a combined wideband processing technique for a frequency agile waveform with Costas code modulated. Compared to the synthetic range profile (SRP) processing, the frequency-domain recombination method avoids grating lobes, and results in a better 1D imaging. This method reduces the computation compared to the SRP, and improves the recognition ability simultaneously by taking advantage of the frequency agility. These make it good for engineering application.

articleTitle: Optimal spectrum allocation for a cooperative radar-communication system
abstract: A radar waveform with spectral notches is designed to share spectrum for the coexistence of radar and communications. To suppress high range sidelobes caused by the discontinuous spectrum, a novel waveform design for cooperative radar-communication system is presented. In this method, the distribution of working band for communications is first used as the degree of freedom (DOF), and thus the waveform optimization is equivalent to search the optimal spectrum allocation scheme. For this reason, we formulate an objective function of minimizing peak sidelobe level (PSL) with respect to the power spectrum density (PSD) of radar waveform under a prescribed range resolution constraint. To address this problem, a global optimization procedure, namely firefly algorithm (FA) is utilized to obtain the desired PSD configuration. Moreover, a PSD-to-waveform implementation based on PSD fitting is employed to convert the PSD to the transmit waveform. Simulation results show that the proposed method can prevent the cooperative radarcommunication system from mutual interference while ensuring the radar signal with low autocorrelation sidelobes and a fine range resolution.

articleTitle: A novel anti-deception jamming method of time-sensitive target based on trajectory characteristics
abstract: For current time-sensitive anti-deception jamming methods, waveform diversity, spatial-polarization domain filtering and feature library identification are employed to eliminate deception jammings. However, high system design complexity and engineering implementation cost severely limit the application of these algorithms. In order to address the above mentioned problem, a novel anti-deception jamming method based on trajectory characteristics is proposed from the perspective of trajectory processing. Through analysing the trajectory characteristic difference between different types of deception jamming and real target, high-order trajectory fitting coefficients, parameter matching relationship and multi-channel amplitude statistical characteristics are extracted severally. Accordingly, passive deception jamming, active range-Doppler deception jamming, active angle deception jamming and real targets can be distinguished. The proposed algorithm makes full use of the advantages of multi-frame trajectory processing for anti-deception jamming, meanwhile, it takes account both the system design complexity and the anti-jamming performance. Simulation results show effectiveness of this algorithm.

articleTitle: FLOS-BASED DOA ESTIMATION FOR COPRIME ARRAYS IN IMPULSE NOISE ENVIRONMENT
abstract: The existing framework of direction-of-arrival (DOA) estimation approaches for coprime arrays is to operate the equivalent virtual signal which is obtained by vectorizing the covariance matrix of the received signal. However, the secondorder information of the signal embedded in additive impulse noise instead of Gaussian noise is invalid. In this paper, we model the impulse noise as symmetry alpha stable (SαS ) processes reasonably, and propose a fractional lower order statistics (FLOS)-based approach to construct an augmented virtual array which is similar to the Gaussian noise case. By exploiting such a FLOS-based virtual array, the degree-offreedom (DOF) superiority offered by the coprime array can still be held and the robustness to impulse noise can be enhanced. The effectiveness of the proposed DOA estimation approach in impulsive noise environment is validated through simulation results in terms of spatial spectrum characteristic as well as estimation accuracy.

articleTitle: Study on rolling measurement of high-speed rotating carrier based on geomagnetic field
abstract: Usually, a flying carrier can be controlled well, its three attitude angles must be accurately measured. However, in some cases, traditional inertial measurement equipment is difficult to measure the three attitude angles of flying carrier when rotating at a high-speed, especially in the rolling direction. In order to solve the rolling measurement problem in a high-speed rotating carrier. Three methods are proposed here. Two of them only use magnetic sensors to measure geomagnetic filed. The third method use magnetic sensors combining with a MEMS gyroscope (gyro). It can not only avoid increased angle error due to gyros measurement but also efficiently resist magnetic field interference. Finally, in order to verify the three methods, the experiment is carried out on a real system. The three methods are compared through measurement error analysis, and the adaptation of environment is summarized. Results show that methods by measuring geomagnetic filed can accurately calculate the roll angle of a high-speed rotating carrier.

articleTitle: FPGA implementation of SAR Bi-Channel synthesis based on inverse filtering
abstract: In a multi-channel synthetic aperture radar (MSAR) system, non-uniform azimuth sampling is an important factor affecting imaging. If it is not processed and then imaged directly, it will inevitably lead to deterioration of imaging performance. The channel synthesis algorithm based on inverse filtering is a method to solve this problem. However, in actual applications, it is necessary to perform specific optimization processing on the algorithm to meet real-time requirements. This paper designs a new architecture for efficient implementation of channel synthesis algorithms. The design makes full use of the parallel characteristics of FPGA to improve the speed of the algorithm. By optimizing the DDR read-write control logic, the data transfer rate is improved. Finally, the Modelsim software is used to obtain the simulation results. At 150 MHz,the processing speed could reach 461.6MSamples/s (64bit/sample).

articleTitle: Sparse aperture isar imaging method based on continuous compression sensing
abstract: In order to solve the problem of scattering point mismatch in high-resolution imaging method based on traditional discrete compression sensing (CS) theory, a sparse aperture ISAR high-resolution imaging method based on continuous compression sensing (CCS) is proposed. Firstly, based on the theory of continuous compressed sensing, the sparse aperture representation model of ISAR imaging is constructed in the continuous atomic domain, and the reconstruction problem of sparse aperture is transformed into solving the atomic norm minimization problem. Then, based on the positive semi-definite property of the atomic norm, the full aperture data recovery is equivalent to the positive semi-definite programming problem, and the improved alternating direction multiplier method is used to solve the sparse optimization problem. Finally, the recovered full aperture data can be recovered, and the IASR imaging result can be achieved via the conventional inverse fast Fourier transform. The sparse reconstruction is implemented directly in the continuous domain, which avoids the degradation of image quality caused by the discretization of the traditional CS method, realizes the high-resolution ISAR imaging under the condition of low measurement, and also has robustness under low SNR. Theoretical analysis and real data experiments verify the effectiveness of the above method.

articleTitle: Effect of polarimetric calibration on neighbouring points and an efficient selection of calibration points for phased array antenna
abstract: Polarimetric phased array radar has attracted more and more attention due to the ability of efficiently obtaining extra geometric information of targets. Unlike mechanically scanning radar, the phased array radar may cause measurement bias in polarimetric parameters. While a calibration is essential to eliminate the bias, it has not been studied how a calibration at a specific point affects the neighbouring measurements, and the effectiveness of the calibration on them is unknown. The relation between a calibration and the neighbouring measurement bias is crucial for understanding how a calibration works for a specific region, and helpful for establishing an efficient calibration. In this work, the polarization characteristic of phased array antenna element is analysed, and the measurement bias is derived for neighbouring points. The relation between a calibration at a specific point and the bias of neighbouring points is established. It is demonstrated that a calibration is still effective even for a widely separated point. The distribution of a calibration-effective region is presented. A scanning area is divided into a series of effective regions, and points are selected for efficiently calibrating this area.

articleTitle: A novel algorithm for DOA estimation and array calibration in monostatic MIMO radar
abstract: Array calibration is a key issue for the direction of arrival (DOA) in colocated multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) radar. The existing calibration methods get struck at local optimal solution easily when the gain-phase error is too large. This paper introduces particle swarm optimization (PSO) and teaching-learning-based optimization (TLBO) to optimize the multiple signal classification (MUSIC)-based cost function for the joint estimation of the direction of arrival (DOA) and unknown sensor gain-phase. The proposed method combines the random number inertia weight PSO (RNW-PSO) algorithm and the learner phase of TLBO. Benefited from the nature of random number inertia weight and learner phase, the particles can deviate from their original course to improve global search capabilities. Simulation results show that the proposed method is superior to the conventional methods in terms of calibration accuracy and convergence speed.

articleTitle: Missile-borne forward-looking superresolution imaging based on doppler deconvolution
abstract: This paper deals with the problem of forward-looking imaging. An efficient missile-borne forward-looking super-resolution imaging method based on Doppler deconvolution is proposed to improve the azimuth resolution. Conventional deconvolution methods may fail for the missile platform due to its high speed. To solve this problem, the Doppler phase information caused by the missile platform is fully exploited to construct the Doppler matrix in the paper. Then the Doppler matrix is utilized to be integrated with the antenna pattern. Finally, the complex Gaussian distribution and the Laplace distribution in an expanded high-dimensional space is used to model the distribution of noise and targets of the imaging scene, respectively. Based on the Bayesian framework, the forward-looking imaging problem is converted into the convex optimization problem. Simulation results are given to verify the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Application of bayes estimation in radar seeker performance evaluation
abstract: In the development, maintenance and operational application of product, radar seeker performance evaluation process is of great significance for tracking and mastering the radar seeker technology level. The comprehensive and accurate performance evaluation results will provide a reliable decision basis for the quality management. Based on the actual application requirements, the key problems to be solved in the performance evaluation of radar seeker is how test data are processed to arrive at an evaluation conclusion. Based on the characteristics analysis of radar seeker anti-interference performance test, this paper studies the Bayes estimation method for evaluating index parameters under the condition of small samples. Simulation results verify the applicability and effectiveness of Bayes parameter estimation under the condition of insufficient sample size.

articleTitle: MULTI-STATIC RADAR JOINT DETECTION METHOD BASED ON GAUSSIAN KERNEL
abstract: For spatially distributed multi-radar systems, large signal to noise ratio (SNR) difference between channels formed by the multi-radar leads to a decrease in the detection performance of the square-law detector. To solve this problem, a multiradar joint detection method based on Gaussian kernel is proposed, which weights signals received by different channels according to Gaussian kernel functionD With SNRs of channels unknown, the method achieves the optimal detection performance by adjusting the kernel radius. Numerical experiments indicate that the method gives a much better detection performance than the square law detector, especially when the SNR difference between channels is significant.

articleTitle: A two-stage CFAR based change detection method for FOPEN targets
abstract: A change detection method based on two-stage constant false alarm rate (CFAR) detection for targets detection in bitemporal foliage-penetrating (FOPEN) Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) images is presented. First, amplitude difference between bi-temporal pixels and Euclidean distance between bi-temporal neighborhoods are combined to generate a difference image. Second, a two-stage CFAR detector composed of a global CFAR, a local CFAR and a fusion is designed to analyze the difference image and produce a change map within targets. The global CFAR employs a log-normal based CFAR to extract a candidate region from the difference image. The local CFAR use the G<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sup> CFAR indexed by the candidate region to detect the targets in the bitemporal images. The two detection results of the local CFAR in the bi-temporal images are fused to produce a change map within targets. Finally, clustering is applied to reduce false alarms in the change map. Experimental results on the CARABAS-II SAR image dataset demonstrate the superior performance of the proposed method, compared to the baseline algorithm.

articleTitle: Detection performance analysis for FDA radar with correlated RCS model
abstract: Frequency diverse array (FDA) adopts a small frequency increment across its array elements to produce a jointly range-angle-dependent transmit beampattern, which provides novel potentials in target detection, interference or clutter suppression. Since the FDA uses multiple different transmit carriers, its radar cross section (RCS) feature is expected to be significantly different from the counterpart of conventional PA. Hence, this paper first studies the RCS property of complex target for FDA and then analyses the associated target detection performance with the partially correlated RCS consideration. More specifically, this paper considers the incoherent target detection with FDA radar, especially in the presence of non-identically distributed target backscattered echoes. The theoretical analysis results are all examined by numerical examples.

articleTitle: Research on multi-sensor mission planning in target tracking system based on SVM
abstract: In target tracking mission planning, one of the difficulties is to generate Multi-sensor mission planning under the guidance of resources information. This paper proposes a SVM-based target tracking multi-sensor mission planning method. The method firstly generates a mission-planning database as a training set based on typical mission scenarios. Then, the hierarchical learning model was established by SVM algorithm, and the sensor-target allocation and sensor resource allocation were carried out respectively. After the model was trained by the scheme database, the intelligent generation of mission planning scheme can be realized. So that the feasibility and robustness of the method are verified by simulation

articleTitle: 2-D adaptive filter design based on noise data extension
abstract: An innovative realization algorithm for two-dimensional (2-D) adaptive filter is proposed. In one-dimensional (1-D) adaptive filtering, the noise cancellation result is influenced by the correlation property of noisy signals from different channels. The data extending to 2-D of the 1-D noisy signal are established to exploit the transfer property of auxiliary channel. The simulation results show the effectiveness of the proposed filtering method.

articleTitle: A ship detection method with model compression for optical remote sensing images
abstract: Ship detection technology is a hot topic in the field of optical remote sensing image processing, and it has a broad application prospect. However, the existing ship detection method is mostly based on convolutional neural networks (CNN), and its detection accuracy is generally low in optical remote sensing images because the complex environment has brought great challenges to it. In this study, focus on model compression and target samples, a novel training sample selection strategy and a sample composition mechanism are implemented for a compressed CNN-based method. Our ship detection algorithm is based on pruning filters strategy, and can be divided into two stages: (1) we change some images into smaller parts and then stitched. (2) according to the target characteristics, we use a selection strategy to screen positive and negative samples automatically. The results show that compared with the original network architecture, our method has higher detection accuracy and can reduce the computation costs in the test dataset.

articleTitle: An integration method for detection and classification of sea surface targets
abstract: Wideband radar is more and more common in the sea-surface target detection and surveillance. To save the radar system resources and meet radar multi-functional requirement, we proposed an integration method for detection and classification of sea-surface targets with wideband signals. The proposed iterative secondary detection method can balance the target split and multi-targets in wideband echo. The target detection and high resolution range profile (HRRP) length extraction can be accomplished at one time. The multi-features fusion method in the following classification in target size is also applied in this paper. Experimental results and analysis are provided to show that, the proposed method can effectively detect sea surface targets without the confusion of target splitting and multi-targets, acquire the HRRP length of the target with high precision and perform a robust multi-features fusion classification.

articleTitle: An efficient imaging scheme for high-resolution sliding spotlight SAR based on coherent superposition of subaperture images
abstract: Azimuth spectrum folding is an important problem for sliding spotlight SAR imaging, which is usually solved by using subaperture approach. However, with the increase of azimuth extent, the conventional subaperture approach will occupy a lot of computation and storage resources, which is difficult to meet the real-time requirement. An efficient imaging scheme based on coherent superposition of subaperture images is proposed. This scheme implements azimuth compression in each subaperture separately. Then, adjacent subaperture images are registered and superposed coherently in the image domain to obtain the full-aperture image. Compared with the conventional framework of subaperture approach, the proposed scheme does not require full-aperture azimuth compression and improves the real-time performance of imaging. Processing of real data has validated the proposed scheme.

articleTitle: RCS reduction of group targets
abstract: It is interesting to reduce the radar cross section (RCS) for a better stealthy performance, especially for group targets. In this paper, we study the principles to reduce the overall RCS of group targets by adjusting their positions and flight attitudes, toward a radar system whose operation frequencies are known a priori. Several criteria are presented for RCS reduction for different situations. Numerical results indicate that the RCS reduction is possible, given that the accuracy of flight control is high.

articleTitle: Design and implementation of software-defined radar algorithm components for target detection
abstract: The new concept of software-defined radar (SDR) can be used in various applications such as traffic monitoring and safety, security and surveillance. Most of the hardware processing parts have been replaced by software processing in SDR. To complete its expected functions, an SDR system relies on multiple components, among which algorithm components are used to implement signal processing. The algorithm components are of great importance to the performance of SDR, and need to be carefully designed. In this paper, first the principles of algorithm components design are introduced. After that, an example of algorithm component design is presented using a self-developed integrated development platform with a high-performance mathematical operation library, VSIPL, to realize target detection. A verification of validity and versatility is also given in the end of this paper. More algorithm components of radar signal and data processing can be developed and applied to actual application scenarios using this method.

articleTitle: Monitoring and analysis of artificial island subsidence based on PSInSAR technology
abstract: In this paper, the surface deformation of phoenix island in sanya city was monitored based on PSInSAR technology and sentinel-1A data obtained from March 2017 to December 2019. Then, some typical areas in our study area was selected and the trend of regional subsidence over time was analyzed . The results showed that the built-up area of phoenix island was relatively stable except a small amount of slight deformation in local areas and no significant settlement was found in a large area. But for the area to be built, although all reclamation projects have been completed, the area shows a certain amount of uneven settlement and it gradually increases with time. The research results in this paper show that PSInSAR technology can be applied in artificial island deformation monitoring and can provide decision support for artificial island construction.

articleTitle: Shape feature aided target detection method for micro-drone surveillance radar
abstract: This paper presents a shape feature aided target detection method for micro-drone surveillance radar in order to mitigate the false alarms caused by the ground clutter.
