The method consists of a segmentation threshold selection method based on target measurements and a shape-feature extraction method based on Hu moments. Then the performance of the proposed method is verified experimentally using a real radar system. Field experiment using DJI phantom 3 is conducted, and the measured data is analysed. The results show that although there exist some limitations, the proposed method has good performance on eliminating the false alarms caused by the strong ground clutter in micro-drone detection and improving the target tracking accuracy.

articleTitle: Surface soil moisture inversion based on defs-ga-bp model using sentinel-1/2 remote sensing data
abstract: The major work is to retrieve the surface soil moisture under crop cover in this paper. This paper proposes an improved GA-BP model called as DEFS-GA-BP model. This model is proposed to retrieve the surface soil moisture distribution using Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 remote sensing data. After extracting nine polarization features and one roughness parameter from Sentinel-1 data, five vegetation indexes from Sentinel-2 data. The differential evolution feature selection (DEFS) algorithm is applied to select the optimal feature subset. By using the genetic algorithm (GA) to optimize the node weights, the back propagation (BP) neural network is trained using the optimal feature subset and then used to generate the surface soil moisture distribution. The results of inversion algorithm indicate that the proposed DEFS-GA-BP model has a better inversion precision than GA-BP model, and demonstrates its application potential in surface soil moisture inversion.

articleTitle: A joint estimator for coherent integration in frequency agile radar system
abstract: The frequency agility technology is widely employed in current radar system to improve the capability of the anti-jamming and the precision of tracking. However, it's difficult to utilize the phase information in the frequency-agile radar system because the target motion and varying frequency disrupt the coherence of the echo phase. In this article, we present a coherent integration algorithm with a joint estimator based on the globalized Nelder-Mead algorithm. Several simulation results show that the proposed method achieves similar or better coherent integration performance with high computational efficiency, compared with the grid search method.

articleTitle: Research on range alignment in real-time ISAR imaging and GPU implementation
abstract: In inverse synthetic aperture radar (ISAR) imaging, the quality of imaging and the real-time performance of imaging are becoming more and more demanding. With fast and efficient computing power, GPU is widely used in real-time ISAR imaging. In order to achieve real-time high quality ISAR imaging, a range alignment method suitable for parallel computing is designed in this paper. And high quality range alignment is achieved based on cross correlation method and minimum entropy method of mean distance. The algorithm can decouple data and be realized efficiently by CUDA programming on GPU platform. The simulation data experiments show that the method has the advantages of high range alignment quality and fast calculation speed, and can obtain high quality ISAR images in real time.

articleTitle: Dot-shaped single-peak beampattern synthesis method of two-dimensional FDA-MIMO radar
abstract: The existing methods of dot-shaped single-peak beampattern for frequency diverse array (FDA) by using linear frequency interval are mainly for the emission domain. When receiving domain is considered, the method by using non-linear frequency interval will lead to a higher range sidelobe. In order to reduce the range sidelobe and apply to the receiving domain, a two-dimensional multiple-input multiple-output frequency diverse array (FDA-MIMO) radar model is established in this paper. According to this model, two reception modes of two-dimensional FDA-MIMO radar are given. Based on the deduced beampattern expressions, the approach of dot-shaped single-peak beampattern is proposed. Both theories and simulations show that the proposed approach outperforms the existing methods of conventional FDA in energy focusing when using linear frequency interval. When using non-linear frequency interval, the range sidelobe of two-dimensional FDA-MIMO is lower than that of conventional FDA, while range mainlobe is also narrower than the two-dimensional FDA-MIMO by using linear frequency interval.

articleTitle: A novel convolutional neural networks based scheme for SAR images despeckling
abstract: Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) images are contaminated by coherent speckle noise, which may cause difficulties for computer processing such as image classification and target recognition. In this paper, we propose a novel CNN-based despeckling network comprised of multi-scale block, dense block and residual learning unit. Multi-scale block helps the network to better extract feature. Dense block achieves feature reuse, which makes full use of the features previous layers have learned. In addition, residual learning accelerates training process. Compared with other state-of-art methods, experiments results on synthetic SAR images and real SAR images show that our method achieves better despeckling performance and improves training efficiency significantly.

articleTitle: A robust detection and tracking method using neural network
abstract: Target detection and tracking in the sea clutter environment is a challenging issue for radar system. This paper proposes a robust detection and tracking method based on neural network. By using the different characteristics of motion and scattering between targets and other detections (other targets and false alarms by clutter), a classification model is established to distinguish the categories of the targets. The output of the network is used for both the target detection and target association, with the goal of reducing false alarm and track correlation error more efficiently compared with traditional methods. The feasibility of our method is verified by the measured data.

articleTitle: Main lobe dense false target interference suppression method based on AMUSE for multi-channel radar
abstract: The dense false target interference will severely influence the multi-channel radar detection performance, because it can produce multiple interference spikes in the range direction after pulse compression. In order to solve this problem, a main lobe dense false target interference suppression method based on AMUSE is proposed in this paper. In the proposed method the angles of the interference and target echo in radar received signal are firstly estimated by sub-array MUSIC. Then based on eigen decomposition, radar received signal is pre-whitened for the next step of blind signal separation. In the following, the separation matrix is constructed based on the second-order statistics of the whitening signal. Because dense false target interference and target echo are separated by AMUSE, the suppression of the dense false target interference can be achieved. Through the simulation, it is verified that the proposed method can effectively suppress main lobe dense false target interference and improve radar detection performance.

articleTitle: Adaptive main-lobe clutter suppression algorithm based on data selection in spatial domain for small-aperture high-frequency surface-wave radar
abstract: In small-aperture high-frequency surface wave radar (HFSWR) systems, the angle spectrum of the main-lobe clutter suffers from an issue of serious broadening due to the influence of small array apertures. The target-detection performance of HFSWR can be affected, as broadening causes the target vessels to submerge into the clutter. Therefore, in this paper, we propose an adaptive main-lobe clutter suppression algorithm based on data selection in the spatial domain for small-aperture HFSWR. The clutter correlation was estimated by the data that were removed from the target information of the range domain and the angle domain. Then the clutter information was used to suppress the clutter, to reveal the target. Finally, the experimental results of the measured data confirmed that the proposed algorithm ensured a superior suppression performance for the ionospheric clutter and the sea clutter. In addition, the comparison results of two other algorithms are provided in this paper.

articleTitle: Concentric circular array design for beampattern control using vortex electromagnetic waves
abstract: As a newly explored information carrier, orbital angular momentum (OAM) of vortex electromagnetic wave (VEW) has drawn a lot attention in recent years due to its ability of information modulation. In radar detection area, it is required to apply multiple OAM modes to get vortex azimuth resolution. However, the space energy distribution of the VEW varies with the OAM mode number when using circular array. Because of this variation, VEWs with different OAM mode cannot cover the same space area. In this paper, concentric circular array (CCA) is used to solve the coverage problem. By analysing the corresponding relationship between array radius and beampattern mainlobe direction, a concentric circular array radius design method is proposed to achieve multiple OAM modes' mainlobe direction control. According to the simulation analyses, the effectiveness of the proposed method is verified.

articleTitle: Interrupted-sampling repeater jamming(ISRJ) suppression based on cyclostationarity
abstract: Interrupted-sampling repeater jamming (ISRJ) is coherent with transmitted signal by intercepting partially and forwarding transmitted signal and poses a huge threat to radar because it is hard to suppress. This paper focuses on the ISRJ suppression by the difference in statistical domain. By deducing the mathematical expression of auto-correlation and cyclic frequency based on modeling echo signal, the difference in statistical domain between target echo signal with ISRJ is shown and used to construct Frequency-Shift (FRESH) filter. The FRESH filter is used to suppress the ISRJ-based false targets. What's more, the results of FRESH filter is analyzed when the different parameters of ISRJ are choosed. The simulation results demonstrate the applicability of FRESH filter when it is used to suppress ISRJ.

articleTitle: A new method to estimate ship velocity vector for spaceborne SAR
abstract: Ship velocity estimation algorithms for spaceborne synthetic aperture radar (SAR) play an important role in monitoring major waters and ports. A new method to estimate the velocity of moving ships in spaceborne SAR is proposed, which can get the ground range speed and azimuth speed of ship,as well as improve refocusing quality. This method is applied directly on the single-look complex (SLC) image data, and a Map drift (MD) algorithm and extraction geometric features of ships are introduced to derive its two-dimensional velocity formula. Furthermore, it does not require external data support. Finally, real strip-map SAR image from GF-3 satellite was used to test the proposed method. The estimated velocities are exactly matched with the data recorded by the international automatic identification system (AIS). Moreover, compared with present method, the proposed method can get vessels' full speed information with higher accuracy, and greatly improve refocusing quality at the same time.

articleTitle: Characteristics analysis of ground penetrating radar signals for groundwater pipe leakage detection
abstract: As a high-efficiency, non-destructive geophysical method, ground penetrating radar (GPR) has been widely applied to detection of subsurface pipes in urban areas. The detection and localization of water pipe leakage is of great significance. In this paper, a controlled model experiment was carried out to investigate of the characteristics of GPR signal reflected from the leakage area surrounding a water pipe buried in sand. Oscillation signal trailing the reflection from the top of the pipe in radar image is found after the water leakage. The phenomenon is further interpreted by conducting a full wave simulation of electromagnetic waves propagation though the leakage area. The results are important to accurately interpret field GPR data to localize water leakage.

articleTitle: Time spatial spectrum correlation based multiband infrared target detection
abstract: Multiband infrared sensors based dim and small target detection is a core technique in reconnaissance and early warning applications. However, there exist two difficulties including noise disturbance in the single band image and low SNR in single frame image. We propose a novel and effective multiband infrared target detection algorithm by utilizing time spatial spectrum correlation technology. Specifically, a multiband image preprocessing is advocated to filter noise, together with the multiscale patch contrast measure to extract the potential target. Afterwards, a multiple bands image based target spectrum detection algorithm is utilized to extract candidate targets effectively. Besides, the long-shortterm target correlation method in sequential images is exploited to eliminate the false alarm in a single frame. Experimental results on six infrared image sequences demonstrate that our algorithm improves the detection rate and reduces the false alarm rate with multiband sequential images, which outperforms the other state-of-the-art algorithms.

articleTitle: GPU acceleration of a fast phase compensation algorithm in inverse synthetic aperture radar
abstract: Phase compensation is an essential part of inverse synthetic aperture radar imaging. Minimum entropy-based phase compensation methods have been widely applied due to their robustness under low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) situations. However, these methods suffer from huge computation complexity and therefore, can be hardly used in real-time imaging situations. In this paper, a novel real-time phase compensation method combining Doppler centroid tracking (DCT), prominent range bins extraction, and fast minimum entropy phase compensation (FMEPC) is proposed. To achieve high efficiency, the parallel version of the proposed algorithm is implemented on Graphic Processing Unit (GPU). Experiments based on real-measured data show that almost 10 times speed-up can be realized.

articleTitle: A radar target detection technique based on deep neural network
abstract: In this paper, a method of designing “pseudo-color map” of radar echo is proposed to detect radar objects by using neural network target detection technology. Compared with the traditional scheme, it features low false alarm rate, strong detection ability and self-evolving ability. This paper also introduces the neural network used, presents the detection algorithm and technical scheme, and finally the system verification and derived conclusions.

articleTitle: Simulation analysis of first order sea clutter spectrum for shipborne bistatic HFSWR
abstract: Compared with onshore bistatic high frequency surface wave radar (BHFSWR) and shipborne monostatic HFSWR (MHFSWR), shipborne BHFSWR combines the common advantages of both. It is worth noting that the motion state of both mobile stations needs to be considered. In this paper, the spreading characteristics of first-order sea clutter and the doppler shift of the shipborne BHFSWR were analysed theoretically. Then, the simulation results of forward motion and yaw motion are given, and the co-modulation of the echo signal by the motion of the transmitting and the receiving station was investigated. The simulation results show that the amplitude-frequency characteristics of the first-order sea clutter were more complex when the shipborne transmitter and shipborne receiver were at different uniform motion. Finally, combined with the flexibility of shipborne platform, a new scheme was proposed. That is, it can be adjusted the posture information of the shipborne platform, the detection coverage can be better and the spread range of the first-order sea clutter can be reduced.

articleTitle: Time-frequery image processing based jet engine modulation extraction method towards target recognition
abstract: Jet Engine Modulation (JEM) characteristics are widely used in airborne radar to detect and classify helicopter, propeller-driven aircraft and jet aircraft. Airborne clutter and low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), however, veils the JEM phenomena. Factors such as Observation Angle, Blade Pitch, Intermodulation of Rotors and Radar Cross Section (RCS) scintillation, can affect the JEM characteristics of radar echoes significantly. Thus a robust and optimized JEM extraction method is in sore need. In this paper, we propose a fusion detection method, using super resolution to obtain JEM time-frequency images. By means of pre-processing, time-frequency analyzing and fusion detecting, JEM characteristics areextracted from complex background. Further measurements and data analysis verify its effectiveness. We anticipate that this method will form the basis for the development of JEM engineering and indicate possible lines for airborne radar's target classificationin future.

articleTitle: DOA estimation of wideband chirp signals based on matched filter
abstract: The direction of arrival (DOA) estimation of wideband chirp signal is studied in this paper. The wideband chirp signal becomes a short pulse which is approximated by a sinc function with the use of matched filter. Based on the covariance matrix of the sinc function, the proposed method constructs a new signal model in which the steering vector is independent of the frequency and depends only on the DOAs of incident signals. Then existing narrowband DOA estimation methods can be applied to estimate wideband chirp signals DOA. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm shows superior performance in DOA estimation of the wideband chirp sources.

articleTitle: A novel azimuth super-resolution method base on parameter searching
abstract: Radar azimuth super-resolution has always been a hotspot in the field of radar detection. In this paper, a novel azimuth super-resolution algorithm base on parameter searching is proposed by searching the optimal target azimuth parameters iteratively based on least squares criterion. Particle swarm optimization is used to speed up the iteration. The proposed algorithm does not rely on prior knowledge which result in better adaptation and robustness. Simulation results show that the proposed method can effectively improve the resolution performance under low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) conditions. The maximum resolution can be increased by 12.5 times, when SNR is no less than 10dB.

articleTitle: Ensemble bayesian max-margin one-class classifier for SAR target discrimination in complex scenes
abstract: Synthetic aperture radar (SAR) target discrimination is the key stage in a typical SAR automatic target recognition system, and directly influences the performance of the whole system. However, the performance of some traditional discriminators is degraded in some complex scenes and sensitive to the hyperparameters. To enhance discrimination performance in complex scenes and reduce the sensitivity to the model parameters, a novel discrimination method, ensemble Bayesian max-margin one-class classifier (EnB-MMOCC), is presented in the paper. In EnB-MMOCC, Dirichlet process mixture is introduced to cluster the input data, and a max-margin one-class classifier is learned with max-margin criteria in each cluster. With the ensemble of some simple classifiers, the complex nonlinear classification can be implemented to enhance the classification performance. Experimental results based on real SAR data demonstrate that EnB-MMOCC can not only enhance discrimination performance, but also be robust to the model parameters.

articleTitle: Research on a new wavwform design method to improve velocity range
abstract: Millimetre wave radar can realize non-contact measurement, with long detection distance, high accuracy and strong anti-interference ability. It has achieved good results in the measurement of distance and velocity, and is widely used in the field of radar measurement. However, the maximum unambiguous velocity of the classic chirp continuous waveform limits the measurement range, which is usually solved by using multiple chirp signals with different FM slopes. But in this case, a longer measurement time is required, which contradicts the high update rate. Therefore, this paper designs a new waveform, adds frequency hopping between sequences, and proposes an unambiguous velocity detection method within a single measurement period. The simulation results show that the new waveform does not need to add an additional frequency modulation sequence, which effectively expands the radar velocity range within a single measurement period, while ensuring a sufficiently large accumulation gain.

articleTitle: Short baseline direct position determination based on precise synchronization
abstract: The short-baseline positioning has unparalleled advantages over the equipped long-baseline mu lti-station time difference positioning in site selection, inter-site communication, site maintenance, etc. But the existing short-baseline position determination algorithms often have problems such as low positioning accuracy and poor performance in low signal to noise ratio (SNR) scenarios. In view of the above problems, in this paper, we propose a short baseline direct position determination method based on precise synchronization. A direct position determination optimization criterion based on the Maximum Likelihood(ML) was introduced after we establishing the short baseline signal detection model. Furthermore, we elaborated on the engineering application process of the algorith m. The effectiveness of the proposed algorithm was verified in the simulation experiment section.

articleTitle: Optimal allocation of time resources for phased array radar multi-target tracking based on BP neural network
abstract: Aiming at the different threat levels under phased array radar multi-target tracking, the Bayesian Cramer-Rao Lower Bound (BCRLB) of the target position estimation is used as the allocation criterion, this paper establishes a multi-target tracking time resource allocation optimization model based on threat degree. The model based on threat degree to track the target can be divided into two categories, different types with different time resource allocation method. Due to the time-consuming operation of this model and optimization algorithm, this paper also proposes a multi-target tracking time resource fitting method based on BP neural network. Computer simulation shows that the model and method can keep the target tracking in the best state, and the BP neural network will reduce the time consumption by thousands of times.

articleTitle: Design of vehicle vision system based on millimeter-wave radar
abstract: In this paper, the millimeter-wave radar sensors and binocular vision sensor are applied to the vehicle sensors system. Taking advantage of the high precision, strong real-time performance of the millimeter-wave radar, the characteristic of binocular vision sensor that contains rich scene information, a set of visual sensor system based on millimeter-wave radar auxiliary for vehicle was designed. The key technology needed in the system design was studied. According to the principle of binocular camera ranging, stereo matching was carried out to get the parallax map to obtain the three-dimensional information of the target. Radar and camera data fusion model was established, through coordinate transformation, the joint calibration of millimeter-wave radar and camera sensor was carried out, and the multi-thread method was used on data real-time synchronization. The measurement accuracy and robustness of the sensor system were improved. This system not only can be used as vehicle applications, but also can be applied to the ships, aircrafts in the future.

articleTitle: A KU band high integrated active phased array antenna for radar seeker
abstract: The volume and weight of the load on missile are strictly required because of the small space and limited bearing capacity of the missile platform. A high integrated active phased array antenna is designed in this paper. The system architecture of three-dimensional laminated installation and three-stage RF blind interconnection is adopted to realize the design of high integration, light and small size, high reliability of the missile borne active phased array antenna. The sum, azimuth difference and elevation difference beams of the active phased array antenna can be formed simultaneously, which can be applied for SAR imaging and monopulse estimation. The measured results of the active phased array antenna show that the side-lobes are smaller than -23dB while the sum-and-difference null depth are about -40dB, and the scanning angles reach to ±60° in azimuth and elevation directions. This active phased array antenna has many advantages such as high integration, low side-lobe, two dimensional large angle scan and compact structure.

articleTitle: Concept of geo-SAR system with DBF antenna and range ambiguity performance discussion
abstract: This manuscript proposes the performance analysis of Digital Beam Forming (DBF) technology applied to Geo-SAR system. High Earth orbit SAR satellite is the development trend of microwave remote sensing. Geo-SAR satellite can cover ± 8.2° Earth cone field of view through using two dimensional scanning DBF antenna. Furthermore, using DBF multi beam receiving technology, multiple 200km×200km scenes distributed in a scale larger than 4000km×4000km can be imaged simultaneously. This makes Geo-SAR with DBF SAR antenna payload have the ability of fast maneuvering imaging for multiple targets in a wide range, which is called high manoeuvrability. According to the characteristics of Geo-SAR satellite, this paper illuminates the scanning capability and multi-target observation ability of DBF antenna. It further studies that the improvement of range ambiguity(RASR) by phase weighting, and proposes to complete the weighting of each channel of the antenna based on Dolph-Chebyshev algorithm. The simulation results show that the proposed method can improve the range ambiguity by more than 20dB for X-band Geo-SAR system.

articleTitle: An effective marine target detection algorithm based on YOLOv3
abstract: In order to solve the problem of low signal-to-noise ratio of target detection under strong sea clutter, an effective marine target detection algorithm based on YOLOv3 network is proposed. According to the characteristics of radar echo data, after data pre-processing the RGB image suitable for the detection network is constructed, and the number and aspect ratio of target anchor boxes are extracted by K-means clustering algorithm, and the network parameters are adjusted to obtain the optimized target detection model through multi-scale training, so as to detect targets in the sea clutter, and the target position is marked by the anchor boxes, provide effective information characteristics for the tracking method. The experimental results on the radar measured data show that the proposed method can suppress a large number of clutter and detect small and weak targets accurately, taking into account the speed and accuracy of detection, and verify the robustness of the algorithm. This approach simplifies the radar signal processing, reduces the computational complexity, and lays a foundation for the construction of intelligent radar.

articleTitle: Complex resonant frequencies extraction method of target buried in medium based on matrix pencil method
abstract: Conventional complex resonant frequency (CRF) extraction method has some inherent drawbacks, which contain ill-posed problem of equation and noise-sensitivity. In order to overcome these drawbacks, a CRF extraction method based on the Matrix Pencil(MP)is proposed in this paper. In the proposed method, two Hankel matrixes are firstly structured using the later-time transient response. Then a matrix pencil is defined by related Hankel matrixes. Finally, the problem of CRF extraction is transformed to an ordinary eigenvalue problem solved by the SVD. Simulation results of the CRF extraction in free space and homogenous medium demonstrate that the MP method is feasible and can effectively improve CRF extraction performance.

articleTitle: Design of intelligent high-resolution remote sensing satellites based on new integrated electronic system
abstract: As the brain of intelligent satellites, the on-board integrated electronic system is the core system in the overall design of smart satellites. Based on modular integrated electronic technology, this paper innovatively adopts system engineering methods to uniformly design the information processing, control and management procedures, hardware and software equipment of intelligent satellites to realize the sharing of information resource and the optimization of the entire satellite system, which takes the lead in the research area of intelligent satellites in China. The research content mainly includes hardware architecture design and software network architecture design of intelligence satellites. In terms of hardware architecture, creative ideas of modular and open structure design are adopted, and standardized interfaces are designed for on-board hardware, realizing efficient integration and plug-and-play of satellite hardware. As for the software network architecture, the hierarchical design is inventively adopted to facilitate the reuse of software resources; through the unified deployment of on-board computing resources, the ability of autonomous management of tasks and the autonomous processing of data is improved to facilitate rapid application. The overall ingenious design has the characteristics of openness, versatility and flexibility, and meets the application requirements of intelligent satellites.

articleTitle: A method for position offset correction of ship target on SAR image based on AIS data
abstract: This paper proposes a method for the ship target azimuth offset correction on the Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) image using Automatic Identification System (AIS) data. Traditional AIS and SAR image ship matching usually use AIS position, size, and other information. This paper uses a continuous position sequence around the SAR image acquisition time, that is, the complete trajectory, to calculate the slant range between the ship and the space-borne SAR platform. By deriving the slant range, the radial velocity can be obtained. According to the radial velocity, the azimuth offset of the moving ship is estimated to correct the ship's position on the SAR image.

articleTitle: Contrast-based SAR ship detection in superpixel level
abstract: Ship detection from synthetic aperture radar (SAR) images is one of the crucial issues in maritime surveillance. However, it is very difficult to detect ships by traditional detection methods because of the complex background of high-resolution SAR images. We propose a contrast-based target detection method in superpixel level. Experimental results based on ocean SAR images have shown that the proposed method can obtain stable detection performance both in strong clutter and heterogeneous backgrounds. Meanwhile, it has a low computational complexity compared with some existing detection methods. Firstly, the method introduces superpixel segmentation to partition the SAR image. Then according to the difference in the gray distribution and intensity of the target and clutter superpixels, the difference between the target and clutter is increased based on the weighted information entropy and local contrast of the superpixels to achieve target superpixel detection. Finally, the obtained superpixels of the suspected target are clustered, and false alarms are removed based on the geometric characteristics of the target. The method performs detection at the superpixel level, which can ensure the detection accuracy and improve the detection efficiency.

articleTitle: RADAR EXTENDED KALMAN FILTERING METHOD BASED ON MAXIMUM CORRENTROPY
abstract: The filter model in radar tracking system is usually nonlinear and non-Gaussian, but the design of tracking filter in radar system usually depends on the linear Gaussian system. Once the system is nonlinear and interfered by non-Gaussian noise, the radar tracking performance will deteriorate seriously. In order to improve the tracking accuracy of radar in nonlinear and non-Gaussian environment, the maximum correntropy extended Kalman filter algorithm is applied to the radar tracking system in this paper. The filter uses the maximum correntropy instead of the traditional minimum mean square error as the optimization criterion, which has strong positioning accuracy and robustness. The simulation results show that this method can effectively solve the non-Gaussian noise interference to the radar tracking performance and improve the radar tracking accuracy.

articleTitle: The analysis of the performance model of Sun-Synchronous wide swath ocean altimeter satellite
abstract: Compared to Conventional sub-satellite pointing altimeters, the Sun-synchronous wide swath ocean altimeter satellite provides extremely accurate measurements of SSH and wide swath ocean measurement for mesoscale ocean phenomenon at the same time. The two performance models of space-borne wide swath ocean altimeter are compared in this paper. The biases may originate from imperfections of performance model. And a novel model of the effect of satellite attitude jitter control accuracy on height error is proposed. In particular, we demonstrate that the change trend of the height error from this model is as similar as the simulation results.

articleTitle: Estimation of sources number and DOA by pseudo-covariance matrix constructed from single snapshot
abstract: The high frequency ground wave radar has a longer accumulation time, resulting in less received data that can be used for spatial spectrum estimation. Aiming at this problem, this paper designs a pseudo-covariance matrix construction method based on single snapshot, and theoretically proves that the matrix is suitable for Gerschgorin disk algorithm (GDE) criterion source number estimation and multiple signal classification (MUSIC) algorithm Direction of Arrival (DOA) estimation. In order to improve the estimation performance, matrix weighting algorithm and beam domain algorithm are used. The simulation results show that the estimation of sources number and DOA based on the pseudo-covariance matrix can achieve good performance under the actual radar signal-to-noise ratio (SNR).

articleTitle: Electromagnetic radiation analysis and synthesize of UAV target with the theory of characteristic modes
abstract: The theory of Characteristic Modes can better express the physical concept of radiator. In this paper, a fast method for synthesizing the radiation pattern of an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) platform is presented based on the characteristic mode theory. We can synthesize specific radiation patterns of the target to reduce or increase radiation energy in specific directions.

articleTitle: Lightweight convolutional neural network for false alarm elimination in SAR ship detection
abstract: SAR ship detection is an important task of SAR image interpretation and plays a significant role in global marine surveillance. However, since there are usually many false alarms in the detection results, a desirable performance is rarely achieved. Aiming at this problem, this paper proposes an improved method for the ship detection process, using the lightweight convolutional neural network EfficientNet-B0 as a false alarm elimination network, cascaded after the detection stage, to reduce the false alarm rate in the detection results and improve the overall detection accuracy. The results on the MSTAR data set show that EfficientNet-B0 has a good classification effect, and the experiments on the custom data set also verify the effectiveness of the network.

articleTitle: Adaptive spectral filter design for clutter mitigation in doppler weather radar
abstract: Aiming at mitigating moving clutter for non-polarimetric Doppler weather radar, this paper proposes a method named the adaptive object-orientated spectral (AOBS) filter. Based on the spectral continuity of precipitation and clutter, the AOBS filter generates a filtering mask implementing on the range-Doppler spectrogram to remove the clutter and noise, and retain the precipitation. Data from a three-beam weather radar whose main-beams have polarimetric measurements are used to demonstrate the effectiveness of the AOBS filter. The proposed method has the potential to be applied in the standard wind profiler.

articleTitle: The algorithm of weak signal tracking based on sliding frequency lock loop
abstract: In some special environments, such as indoor environment, GNSS signal is greatly attenuated when reaching the receiver, so some high-sensitivity tracking technologies must be adopted. The existing high-sensitivity tracking algorithms have a large amount of computation, high complexity and take up more resources. Therefore, a low-complexity weak signal tracking algorithm based on sliding frequency lock loop has been proposed in this paper. For the GPS L1C/A signal, the sliding coherent integration of the data within one data bit (20ms) can increase the pull-in range of the frequency discriminator without changing the current loop structure, so as to lower the tracking threshold of the frequency lock loop and improve the tracking sensitivity of the receiver. The simulation is carried out for the data with the carrier-to-noise ratio of 15dB-40dB, the doppler frequency of 0Hz and 30Hz, and the data with an initial doppler frequency of 30Hz and an acceleration of 0.4g/s. Experimental results indicate that the proposed algorithm can stably track signal with the carrier-to-noise ratio of 16dB (-158dBmW).

articleTitle: Application of improved genetic ant colony optimization in radar resource interference allocation
abstract: Under the condition of limited interference resources, how to maximize the benefits of multiple jammers interfering with multiple radars has become a research hotspot. This paper has designed a reasonable interference evaluation method. Aiming at the disadvantages of genetic algorithm and ant colony optimization, made some improvements, and combined genetic methods and ant colony optimization, besides, a new crossover and mutation method based on constraints is proposed, which overcomes the shortcomings of invalid iteration of genetic algorithm and easy to fall into local optimal solution of ant colony optimization. Through simulation analysis, the fused algorithm can reach the optimal value within a short number of iterations, improving the utilization efficiency of the jammer.

articleTitle: Correlation filter based UAV tracking system on FPGA
abstract: Vision-based target tracking technology is one of the hotspots in the field of computer vision currently. It is not only widely used in civil fields, such as autonomous driving and traffic supervision, but also in the field of defense, such as battle-field surveillance and missile guidance. Nowadays, UAVs (Unmanned Aerial Vehicle) are more and more widely used in the military field and Counter-UAV system is vital to national security. Accurately UAV tracking is obviously important to the Counter-UAV system. Take the advantages of high real-time, high parallelism and low power consumption of FPGA (Field Programmable Gate Arrays), this paper proposed a small target tracking system of UAV based on FPGA platform which mainly benefits from the correlation filtering algorithm. Tested on 5 sequences of UAV tracking, the average accuracy is more than 97%, and the processing speed is 41 fps.

articleTitle: Wide-swath SAR based on networking of multiple small satellites for maritime applications
abstract: Multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) synthetic aperture radar (SAR) or multi-channel SAR can achieve the high-resolution wide-swath imaging, and staggered SAR can avoid the imaging blind zones. However, MIMO or multi-channel SAR depends on higher performance of the satellite platforms. In order to reduce the demand for satellite resources, separate the transmitter and receiver of the SAR and place them on different small satellites to form the multi-satellite network with a spacing of 3-10 km. Wide-swath SAR system based on networking of multiple small satellites for maritime applications is proposed in this paper, where the wide swath can be quickly scanned during one pulse repeated period (PRP) by the high-gain and narrow transmit beam, and all the echoes of the entire coverage can be obtained by the multi-channel receivers with low-gain and wide beam. The high SNR echoes of the different sub-swath can be reconstructed with digital beam forming (DBF) technology along the range direction. A wide-swath SAR imaging with 230-km swath and 3-m resolution based on three small satellites is provided as an example, and the corresponding simulation results have been given at last.

articleTitle: Low probability of intercept-based adaptive waveform selection for phased array radar system with passive sensor cooperation
abstract: This paper proposes an low probability of intercept (LPI)-based adaptive waveform selection strategy for phased array radar system with passive sensor cooperation. The trace of estimated value of the error covariance matrix is utilized to be the accuracy metric for target tracking. The primary objective of the proposed LPI-based adaptive waveform selection strategy is to reduce the radiation times of phased array radar system by jointly optimizing the revisit interval and waveform parameters, which is constrained by a predetermined target tracking accuracy threshold. Several numerical results are provided to verify the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed waveform selection strategy in terms of the LPI performance of phased array radar system.

articleTitle: High-isolation dual-polarized magneto-electric dipole antenna based on LTCC technology
abstract: This paper presents a high-isolation dual-polarized magneto-electric dipole antenna based on low-temperature co-fired ceramic technology (LTCC). The pattern of the unit is symmetrical on the E-plane and the H-plane. The impedance bandwidth for this antenna lower than -10 dB is 20.89%, and the isolation between the two input ports is over 20dB. The antenna has good radiation performance and cross polarization performance, and the antenna element can obtain a gain reach up to 7dBi. Between the strip line and the floor, a cavity structure is formed around the feeding structure by metalized vias. This structure improves the feeding efficiency and improves the impedance matching performance. A circle of metalized vias is added to the periphery of the antenna radiation layer to block surface waves to a certain extent, increasing the isolation between the elements in the array, and ensuring the performance of the elements in the array. Because the antenna is designed based on low-temperature co-fired ceramic technology, the unit has highly integrated packaging capabilities and excellent electrical performance.

articleTitle: Hybrid cramer-rao bound for joint estimation of target angle and nodes position deviations in coherent distributed radar
abstract: Based on Hybrid Cramer-Rao Bound (HCRB) theory, this paper analyzes the influence of the target angle on the estimation accuracy of distributed radar position deviation and the influence of the self-calibration on the target angle. Firstly, the theoretical model of HCRB is derived by considering the information from the fast-time dimension, slow-time dimension and multi-node radar dimension of the radar system. Then, based on the estimation accuracy curves of the radar node position deviations, this paper analyzes the priority of the x or y direction position deviation estimation in the actual scene. Also, this paper simulates and analyzes the improvement of target angle estimation accuracy by compensating different direction position deviation. Finally, this paper calculates the target angle which has the best estimation accuracy in specific configuration, and these results are consistent with the simulation results.

articleTitle: A cache structure and corresponding data access method for Winograd algorithm
abstract: Convolutional neural network performs well in some regions but contains much computational complexity and data transfer between storage module and computation module, which limits its application. The Winograd algorithm can accelerate the convolution layer, which is the most expensive to computing resources in CNN. In this letter, a kind of cache structure and data access method called Jump-Step flow is designed for Winograd algorithm to reduce the data transfer. The Winograd PE replaces multiplication with addition to accelerate the convolution operation. This allows it to work out 4 elements in 3 clock cycles, which contains 72 OPs, 2× better DSP efficiency than average. With the cache structure and data access method, each element is read only once from storage module even different tiles share data and it achieves 4× reduction in data transfer between between PE and storage module than general Winograd, 9× reduction than conventional convolution.

articleTitle: Application of narrow pulse suppression in interference direction estimation
abstract: With the development of PD radar signal processing methods, the advantages of traditional white noise interference are being weakened and active interference generated by radar jammers is increasingly appearing. On this condition, new methods on anti-jamming are needed. In traditional narrow pulse suppression process, the narrow pulse signal is often replaced with average noise or zero, and is directly discarded. This approach actually wastes the interference source information that may be contained in the narrow pulse. In this paper, we propose a new method to extract information from the narrow pulse by using narrow pulse suppression and the MUSIC algorithm, which may be of use in interference direction estimation.

articleTitle: Improving the accuracy of model order estimation in multiband signal fusion
abstract: This paper proposes a method to estimate the model order based on the singular values of a synthetic real matrix. The synthetic data matrix includes the complex observation data and its conjugate data, which fully exploits the existing data information, is more suitable for model order estimation of multiband signal fusion spectrum than the complex observation matrix. Simulation experiments show that this method has better results than the traditional model order estimation methods based on complex observation data matrix, the model order can be estimated at a lower signal to noise ratio (SNR).

articleTitle: Efficiently designing unimodular waveform for colocated MIMO radar
abstract: The problem of designing a unimodular waveform with the similarity constraint for the colocated multiple-input multiple-output radar is investigated. A new approach named by the phase-based multiplier method is proposed to optimise the waveform subject to both the constant modular constraint and the similarity constraint to maximise the signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio in the presence of the signal-dependent interference and the additive Gaussian white noise. Compared with the existing alternative methods, the new approach has lower computational complexity. Furthermore, the numerical simulations demonstrate that the performance of the proposed algorithm outperforms the existing methods.

articleTitle: Multi-bernoulli based track-before-detect for distributed targets with unknown amplitude
abstract: Track-Before-Detect (TBD) is a kind of joint detecting and tracking framework. Compared with the classical tracking algorithms, TBD approaches use the image from sensor as the measurement input and take advantage of target amplitude feature to track targets. However, it is difficult to obtain prior amplitude information of the non-cooperative targets in practice. This paper mainly addresses the multiple distributed targets joint detecting and tracking problem with unknown amplitude information. The target historical measurements are stored through multi-frame buffer method, and principal component analysis (PCA) is introduced to extract target amplitude information and eliminate the influence of outliers. The first principal component is used to be the target amplitude information estimation from the radar image measurement sequence in multi-Bernoulli TBD framework. The performance of the proposed algorithm is verified on the simulated data and its effectiveness is proved.

articleTitle: A SAR motion compensation algorithm based on INS and GPS
abstract: Back Projection (BP) algorithm has been widely used in SAR imaging, and SAR motion compensation largely determines the quality of SAR imaging. This paper first analyses the error source of SAR motion compensation, and then proposes a SAR motion compensation algorithm and its FPGA implementation for uniform acceleration motion model. The algorithm performs coordinate system conversion and interpolation processing on INS data and GPS data, and obtains the real-time radar antenna phase centre through recursion, thereby solving the problem of accurate compensation for SAR imaging of moving platforms. Finally, it is verified that the FPGA implementation of the algorithm can meet the requirements by comparing the results with the simulation results of MATLAB.

articleTitle: Phase unwrapping error correction for phase-derived velocity measurement under low-SNR conditions
abstract: An algorithm to correct the phase unwrapping error for phase-derived velocity measurement (PDVM) method under low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) conditions is presented in this paper. The PDVM method for wideband linear frequency-modulated (LFM) radar can measure the velocity of a space target with high-accuracy. Under low-SNR conditions, the phase unwrapping process might occur errors which reduces the accuracy of the measurement. The proposed method analyses the factors affecting the phase unwrapping process under low-SNR conditions and presents an accurate correction for the process. Simulation results demonstrate its effectiveness. The root-mean-square error (RMSE) of the PDVM results was less than 0.025m/s when the SNR was greater than 15.8dB.

articleTitle: A novel parameter estimation method for RPRI radar
abstract: In this paper, a parameter estimation method is proposed for the random pulse repetition interval (RPRI) radar detecting maneuvering target. In the proposed method, keystone transform (KT) is first applied to correct the baseband linear range cell migration. Then, a Radon linear canonical shift correlation transform (RLCST) is defined and applied to extract the non-uniform quadratic frequency modulated (Nu-QFM) signal traverse the motion trajectory and estimate the frequency parameters simultaneously on the two-dimensional frequency plane. The linear canonical shift correlation transform only requires complex multiplication and nonuniform fast Fourier transform (NUFFT). Owing to the application of NUFFT, the searching processing is unnecessary for the nonuniformly spaced signal and the computational cost is reduced greatly. Furthermore, theoretical analysis illustrates that the proposed method can overcome the random phase fluctuation and is appropriate for multitargets. Compared to other representative methods, the proposed method improves the computational efficiency on the premise of retaining the estimation performance. Simulation results verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A method of channel calibration using periodic monitoring for phased array radar based on FPGA
abstract: After being used for a long time or the working environment changes a lot, the relationship of amplitude and phase among transmit/receive channels of phased array radars may change, which will cause the drop of beam gain, departure of direction and deterioration of the side lobe that will affect the performance of radars. The article proposes a method of channel calibration for phased array radar based on FPGA, which employs the method of monitoring the amplitude and phase of the channels in every single period and calibrates the calibrated values refer to the reference values. This method doesn't need an additional channel and is based on FPGA, which has the advantages such as high precision, being simple in operation and low cost of hardware. The precision of amplitude can reach 0.001dB and the precision of phase can reach 0. 06°.At the meantime, experiment has been carried out to prove its feasibility.

articleTitle: A direct path interference suppression method for GNSS-based passive radar
abstract: Owing to the advantages of low cost and great concealment, GNSS-based passive radar has gradually become a hotspot in the field of remote sensing and target detection. One of the main problems in GNSS-based radar is direct path interference (DPI) and it severely affects the detection of target echo signals. A direct wave suppression method based on signal reconstruction for GNSS-based passive radar is proposed to solve DPI in this paper. After acquiring the information of the code phase and time-delay, a direct wave signal is reconstructed consistently with that in the main channel by synchronizing the amplitude and phase for the direct wave cancellation. Experimental results demonstrate that this method effectively suppress the direct path interference and benefit the target detection processing.

articleTitle: A new vegetation index for cooperative inversion of winter wheat covered surface soil moisture based on sentinel-1/2 remote sensing data
abstract: Aiming at the problem of the interfere of winter wheat on radar backscattering coefficient in surface soil moisture inversion, a new vegetation index called Fusion Vegetation Index (FVI) is defined in this study. Based on the Multi-Spectral Imager (MSI) data of Sentinel-2, and the Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) data of Sentinel-1, using FVI to retrieve water content of winter wheat, combined with Water Cloud model, the interference of winter wheat in soil moisture inversion was reduced. The results show that good soil moisture retrieval results can be obtained by combining with FVI.

articleTitle: Multi-target tracking algorithm based on RSHT-TBD preprocessing
abstract: In view of the problems existing in multi-target tracking in clutter background, such as the difficulty of track initiation, the large number of initial tracks and the serious influence of clutter on track tracking, a multi-target tracking algorithm based on recursive Hough transform track-before-detect (RSHT-TBD) preprocessing is proposed. Firstly, RSHT-TBD technology is used to preprocess the radar measurement data to eliminate the large number of clutter points and false tracks. Then track initiation and filtering processing are carried out with the preprocessed measurement data to achieve effective detection and tracking of multiple targets in clutter background. Simulation results show that the proposed algorithm can realize fast track initiation and effective tracking for multi-target in the background of strong clutter, and the tracking performance is better than the traditional tracking algorithm.

articleTitle: Experimental research on an FM broadcast based TNR passive radar system
abstract: Aiming at the detection performance degradation of the bistatic passive radar due to the time-varying characteristics of the FM broadcast signal bandwidth and radar cross section(RCS) fluctuation, an FM based T<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">N</sup>R passive radar system was studied and the field test was conducted. In this paper, the location principle of an FM broadcast based T<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">N</sup>R passive radar is discussed. Then, the selection principle of multiple FM broadcast signal is proposed based on the detection principle of passive radar and the characteristics of the FM broadcast signal. Finally, the experimental results of the passive radar system are given. The results show that the FM broadcast based T<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">N</sup>R passive radar system can achieve better the detection probability and the target location accuracy than traditional bistatic passive radar.

articleTitle: Array sparse optimization method based on adaptive genetic algorithm
abstract: In the field of passive radar array optimization, in order to overcome the problem that the existing array is constrained by the position of the array elements and the number of array elements, we propose a sparse array optimization method based on adaptive genetic algorithm. The method of selecting the array elements by this proposed method is mainly based on the maximum array aperture, the minimum array element spacing, and the Cramer-Rao bound (CRB) as constraints, and the adaptive genetic algorithm as the optimization method. This proposed method has higher direction-of-arrival(DOA) estimation success accuracy and higher DOA estimation success probability, compared with common unoptimized sparse arrays with the same number of array elements and minimum array element spacing.

articleTitle: Research on anti jamming technology of multi source signal separation based on reciprocal decomposition
abstract: Blind source separation (BSS) is a process of separating and recovering a relatively independent target source signal from the observed multi-source mixed signal including interference and target. BSS uses the difference between the target echo signal and the interference signal to separate the echo signal from the interference signal, which can suppress the influence of the interference signal on the target echo, and can also extract the interference signal from the mixed signal. We can take more effective anti-interference measures by analyzing interference signals.

articleTitle: Lower bound estimation method of PSLL of beam pattern for planar nonuniform distributed coherent aperture radar
abstract: The peak side lobe level (PSLL) of beam pattern is an important factor of distributed coherent aperture radar. Therefore, the lower bound estimation method of PSLL of beam pattern is proposed for the planar nonuniform distributed coherent aperture radar in this paper. In the proposed method, the main lobe of beam pattern is firstly fitted by two-dimensional Gaussian function. Then, the power density ratio of side lobe to main lobe is calculated according to the total received power and the received power of the fitted main lobe. Furthermore, the lower bound of PSLL in the sense of Dolph-Chebyshev is obtained by means of sine function fitting method. The proposed method can provide the lower bound of PSLL of beam pattern to guide the array configuration design of distributed coherent aperture radar.

articleTitle: Sea-surface large target detection via scale-varying median ratio in generalized pareto clutter
abstract: When the resolution of radar is up to the order of meters or sub-meter, sea-surface large targets occupying numerous range cells result in the reference cells from targets. Thus, a scale-varying median ratio (SVMR) detector is proposed to find large targets in generalized Pareto clutter. It is proved that the SVMR detector is constant false alarm rate (CFAR) with respect to the scale parameter of clutter. Finally, real data are used to verify the rapidity and robustness of the proposed detector.

articleTitle: Mismatched filters applied to polyphase codes amplitude-phase compensation
abstract: Recently polyphase codes have drawn significant attention since they have a high degree of design freedom and low autocorrelation sidelobes. Nevertheless, in practical radar system, the transmitted polyphase signals could be greatly distorted due to the non-ideal circuits. Therefore, it's necessary to compensate the distorted signal to improve the practicability of polyphase codes. A traditional compensation procedure is to compare the transmitted signal with a reference signal, and compensate the distortion in the frequency domain. In this paper, the mismatched filter processing is adopted to reduce the pulse compression sidelobes and realize the amplitude-phase compensation of the distorted signals. According to the processing results of the experimental data, the mismatched filter processing method can reduce the sidelobe by about 15dB.

articleTitle: CNN based primary surveillance radar plots classification with application to experimental data
abstract: In this paper, the plots classification problem for primary surveillance radars has been investigated via the convolutional neural network (CNN). The basic principle and algorithm flow of CNN has been introduced compared with the traditional plot classification approaches. Experimental data form a type of L-band primary surveillance radar has been used to verify the proposed plots classification scheme based on CNN. Finally, The data processing results show the efficiency and advantage of the studied CNN approach in this paper.

articleTitle: Wideband interference suppression for SAR using short-time fractional fourier transform method
abstract: Radio frequency interference (RFI) in space is a significant factor that deteriorates the image quality of Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR). Especially when the RFI is nonstationary wideband interference (WBI), the impact on the image is more serious. The energy of wideband signal can be focused in FrFT-frequency domain by using fractional Fourier transform (FrFT), which makes filtering easier. However, this FrFT method ignores the nonstationary property of WBI. To suppress nonstationary WBI effectively, a novel WBI suppression method for SAR using short-time fractional Fourier transform (STFrFT) is proposed, which combines the superiority of FrFT and time-frequency (TF) analysis. Firstly, by searching for matched-order, detecting the instantaneous label by CFAR technique and performing STFrFT, the time signal is focused on the short-time fractional Fourier domain (STFrFD) with high-resolution and no cross-terms. Then, the singular value decomposition method is applied to mixed signal to remove the WBI component. Finally, the clean data is obtained by inverse-STFrFT. Experimental results are provided to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Multi-domains based human activity classification in radar
abstract: In human activity recognition (HAR) based on radar, significant research exists on statistical features extracted from the spectrogram (μD), whereas the research which considers other domains is less developed. This paper is aimed to investigate three domains of radar data: μD, Cadence Velocity Diagram (CVD), and range-time (RT) information, evaluating which ones are best suited to classify specific activities. In addition, information fusion is applied to enhance classification accuracy and compare it with the results of single domain approach. Based on the previous results, a hierarchical structure is proposed to improve the performance of classification further. The preliminary results show that different domains have distinctive sensitivity to specific activities. RT information is sensitive to the moving target crossing range bins, while CVD is more sensitive to body movement. The μD is more balanced, which means it can observe both moving targets and body movements. Furthermore, improvement in accuracy is approximately 6-23 % using feature-level fusion. A hierarchical classification approach is also investigated, which has accuracy in the order of approximately 92 %.

articleTitle: Complex field-based fusion network for human activities classification with radar
abstract: In the context of assisted living, human activity recognition (HAR) is of increased importance to maintain people at home living independently longer. Compared with directly using spectrograms (μD) or range profiles (RP) as inputs for classification discarding either range or explicit Doppler information, range-Doppler-surface (RDS) can more fully represent the information contained in the observed activities. However, because the data are collected from different activities, people, and locations, the RDS has a requires non-trivial adjustments for pre-processing as discussed in this paper to maintain the number of points in the RDS to fixed integer. Although it has improved performance (92%) compared to CNN (90%), this algorithm also discards phase information as most algorithms do in HAR with radar. In contrast, the phase information of the range-Doppler domain, although its performance was not the best (88%), it had no obvious weakness in the recognition of all the movements. Our proposed complex field-based fusion network (CFFN) combines the amplitude and phase which improves both the accuracy of classification (94%) as well as accelerating training time by 12.5%.

articleTitle: High-precision human activity classification via radar micro-doppler signatures based on deep neural network
abstract: Radar-based human activity recognition has been of great interest due to its capability to resolve problems of the security and health system. Deep learning-based methods are widely used to recognize human motion at a micro-scale. However, most of the deep learning networks require large amounts of data. Here, we propose high-precision and efficient human activity classification method via radar micro-doppler signatures with data augmentation and deep neural networks. The proposed method can achieve higher than 99% classification accuracy for different human micro-motions. The most useful solution for classification accuracy improvement is the data augmentation and we try different ways and finally two effective methods are chosen, i.e., selecting different rangebins and spectrogram amplitude display values. In the network model, we compared the recognition accuracy of our model, AlexNet and VGG16 in human activity classification, and found that VGG16 has better generalization ability. In data augmentation, we compared the impact of different rangebins and different display amplitudes on recognition accuracy during human activity classification. Experimental results show that the accuracy deviations generated by selecting different rangebins and spectrogram display amplitude values for target classification are about 2.56% and 1.31% respectively. Selecting the optimal parameters to expand the data can achieve higher than 99% classification accuracy. It is demonstrated that selecting the appropriate rangebins and setting the optimal spectrum display amplitude are crucial for processing micro-doppler signals of the raw radar data.

articleTitle: Micro-doppler feature and image based human activity classification with FMCW radar
abstract: Since FMCW radar measures the range, the Doppler and the angle of the targets frame by frame in time sequences, invariant micro-Doppler features become a tough challenge for deep learning based classification and recognition in radar signal processing and artificial intelligence communities. This paper presents an approach to create micro-Doppler images from range-Doppler images sequences by sum of Doppler profiles in targeted range bins. The time invariant micro-Doppler features are extracted by statistical characteristics and motion pattern of the human activities. The statistical features reflect the distribution of the micro-Doppler and the energy property of movements for different human activity classes. The motion pattern features are decomposed by Singular Value Decomposition (SVD). Furthermore, the micro-Doppler features are analyzed to find significance by Support Vector Machine (SVM). Based on these micro-Doppler significance, Faster RCNN is trained and used for detection of human activities. Experimental results show that the proposed micro-Doppler features can distinguish the human motion pattern very well and the accuracy of the Faster RCNN based human activity classification achieves more than 95%.

articleTitle: A novel non-stationary clutter compensation algorithm for ariborne radar with a yaw angle
abstract: The yaw angle between the antenna panel and the flight velocity direction of an airplane causes the spatial steering of ground clutter changing with the range units, that is, the main-lobe clutter is non-stationary along range dimension, which will cause the performance deterioration of clutter suppression, degrading the ground slow-moving target detection ability. To solve this issue, a novel spatial-temporal compensation algorithm is proposed in this paper. In the proposed algorithm, a range compressed clutter signal is firstly transformed into Doppler domain. And then, a spatial-temporal filtering function is established using the prior radar system information to compensate the range-dependent spatial steering of the clutter signal. After eliminating the non-stationary of the observed clutter scene, the subsequent clutter rejection can be well accomplished by applying the multi-channel processing technique, improving the moving target detection performance. Simulation results are provided to validate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: An approach for high squint space-borne SAR imaging based on generalized scale transform
A fast coherent integration algorithm for maneuvering target detection and high-order motion parameter estimation
abstract: In this paper, a novel long-time coherent integration method for maneuvering target detection as well as high-order motion parameter estimation is proposed. In the proposed algorithm, after transforming the range-compressed signal into the range frequency domain, the range unit walk and range curvature caused by target uncooperative motion are firstly compensated by using the range frequency reversal transform (RFRT), where the envelope migration for a fast-moving target with Doppler ambiguity can be also well dealt with. Then, the echo signal of this maneuvering target in a range unit is modelled as a high-order polynomial phase signal, in which the chirp rate and the quadratic chirp rate are two important Doppler parameters indicating the target coherent integration performance. Based on a symmetrical instantaneous autocorrelation function, the nonstationary phase fluctuation is well eliminated by applying the Radoncubic phase function-Fourier transform (RCFT). Finally, the long-time coherent integration can be effectively and efficiently realized after performing the target motion compensation. The effectiveness of the proposed method is validated by the simulated and real-measured radar data.

articleTitle: Probability hypothesis density filter for phased array radar working in TAS mode
abstract: The probability hypothesis density (PHD) filter is a multi-target tracking (MTT) method based on random finite set (RFS), providing an approximation implementation of the multi-target Bayes filter by propagating the first order moment of multi-target posterior. The PHD filter not only takes into account the accuracy of target state estimation, but also has good real-time performance, which is very suitable for radar MTT applications. In order to apply the PHD filter to scenarios with phased array radar working in track-and-search (TAS) mode, this paper proposes a time-matching recursive PHD filter. In order to handle the MTT in a TAS scenario where adjacent directions of the surveillance area are not continuously scanned, the proposed filter propagate PHD of each sector independent of others. It also introduces the time-matching filtering framework and multi-sensor multi-target recursive filtering framework to update PHD multiple times for each single sector at each time step, which can handle the MTT in scenarios where sectors have different sampling rates. The proposed method is simulated using the Gaussian mixture model, and the results, compared with those of standard PHD filter, demonstrate the effectiveness of it.

articleTitle: Moving target detection and velocity estimation based on spaceborne video SAR
abstract: To improve the detection probability and limited minimum detection speed in the process of moving target detection for single-channel space-borne SAR. A method of moving target detection and parameter estimation based on space-borne video SAR was proposed in this paper. the spaceborne radar is operated in the spotlight mode for an extended period of time while taking video. Firstly, reasonable frame period is selected according to the speed range of the target to be detected. Then the position and velocity vector of the moving target image are detected and estimated based on the SAR video image. Finally, the quantitative relationship between the motion parameters of the moving target image and the actual motion parameters is deduced according to the SAR moving target imaging theory. and the moving target detection, location and velocity estimation based on the video SAR are realized. By extending the time dimension of information acquisition, the detection probability of moving objects is effectively improved. Finally, the effectiveness of the method is verified by computer simulation.

articleTitle: Design and verification of a compact single-board solution for commercializing cost-effective 77 GHz automotive front radar
abstract: To develop a cost-effective 77 GHz front radar towards serious automotive product, a single-board solution has been implemented and verified in this work. A compact printed circuit board (PCB) with all necessary components for complete radar module was built up on its both sides. The system architecture is based on the integration of specially designed antenna arrays with the monolithic millimetre-wave integrated circuit (MMIC) chip TEF8102 for 77 GHz transceiver front-end and the S32R274 for digital signal processing (DSP), and micro-controller as back-end, respectively. The radiation patterns of the antenna array for transmitting channel were characterized on radar module level and compared with simulated results. Good agreement on the field of view (FoV) between simulation and verification was observed. The transmitted linear frequency modulated continuous wave (LFMCW) signals were verified at centre frequency of 76.38 GHz with 800 MHz span. The power flatness achieved ± 1 dB in worst case. The error percentage regarding to the slope deviation in MHz/μs achieved 0.1%. A two-way test was done in real traffic scenario. The scattering points of four moving vehicles towards radar module were clearly captured. Static metallic rods could be stably detected too. This shows a satisfying verification for automotive front radar application a step further from system aspect.

articleTitle: Interferometric radar for activity recognition and benchmarking in different radar geometries
abstract: Radar micro-Doppler signatures have been proposed for human activity classification for surveillance and ambient assisted living in healthcare-related applications. A known issue is the performance reduction when the target is moving tangentially to the line-of-sight of the radar. Multiple techniques have been proposed to address this, such as multistatic radar and to some extent, interferometric radar. A simulator is presented to generate synthetic data representative of 8 different radar systems (including configurations as monostatic, multistatic, and interferometric) to quantify classification performances as a function of aspect angles and deployment geometries. This simulator allows an unbiased performance evaluation of the different radar systems. 6 human activities are considered with signatures originating from motion-captured data of 14 different subjects. The results show that interferometric radar data with fusion outperforms the other methods with over 97.6% accuracy consistently across all aspect angles, as well as the potential for simplified indoor deployment.

articleTitle: Design and polarization scattering characteristics of L-shape reflector
abstract: This paper presents a new L-shape reflector to enhance the cross-polarization radar cross section (RCS). Cross-polarization component can increase the jamming effect against the polarization radars. Such L-shape reflectors can also be used as radar tags in cars, books and so on for radar target detection. By bending the structure of traditional dipole reflector to L shape, the direction of surface current is changed, which produces the cross-polarization component. We have simulated L-shape reflector with different lengths of branches in X-band. Compared with the scattering characteristics of traditional dipole reflector, the linear depolarization ratio (LDRvh) of the L-shape reflector can be easily controlled by changing the length of two branches.

articleTitle: Phase unwrapping based on fusion of ant colony and genetic algorithms
abstract: Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (InSAR) is a microwave imaging system with all-weather earth observation. Because of its wide observation area, high precision, day and night operational capabilities, it has a significant advantage in monitoring large-scale surface deformation. Phase unwrapping is a key step in InSAR data processing. The core of Goldstein traditional branch unwrapping method is the establishment of branch-cutting lines. The shorter the overall length of the branch line, the solution is more accurate. Based on the idea of solving the shortest path of Travelling Salesman Problem (TSP), a new algorithm combining ant colony algorithm and genetic algorithm is proposed. Based on the advantages of these two algorithms, we avoid the disadvantages of excessive parameters, slow calculation speed and low efficiency in ant colony algorithm, reduce the time consumed by ant colony algorithm in solving local optimal solution, improve the local search ability of ant colony algorithm, establish shorter branch line than traditional branch method, prevent "islanding effect" and improve the precision of phase unwrapping. The tests performed on real and simulated interferometric SAR data confirm the validity of the proposed method.

articleTitle: 3D ISAR imaging: Multi-view image fusion problem
abstract: Inverse synthetic aperture radar (ISAR) is capable of generating the three-dimensional (3D) reconstructions of the non-cooperative target via a dual interferometric system, which is called 3D InISAR imaging. The output of 3D InISAR is a 3D point-like image of the target, namely point cloud, each point contains the 3D coordinates (range, cross-range and height with respect to the image plane). Compared to the traditional two-dimensional ISAR imaging, 3D InISAR can avoid the unknow image projection plane and cross-range scaling issues. However, due to some limitations of 3D InISAR imaging, such as scatterer scintillation, self-occlusion and so on, some information of the target in 3D ISAR reconstruction from a single observation view may be missing.
