In order to obtain a more complete 3D ISAR reconstruction, an incoherent multi-view image fusion method based on the principal component analysis and iterative closest points algorithm is proposed. Results of the simulated data verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Semantic segmentation knowledge based MMRF optimal method for fine-grained urban infrastructure classification
abstract: Automatically understanding pixel-level semantic relation in urban area from very high resolution (VHR) aerial images is the kernel way of urbanization development and planning. However, due to aerial images covering a large urban area with VHR, manually annotated pixel-level multiple instances from urban area is unimaginable. Then, when the low quality pixel-level labelling dataset used for semantic segmentation network supervised learning, these methods cannot provide the fine-grained urban infrastructure classification mapping results. Related to this problem, we proposed the semantic segmentation knowledge (SSK) based multi-scale Markov random field (MMRF) optimal method for fine-grain urban infrastructure classification mapping. First, proposed feature ensemble way is employed to final prediction layer to fuse multiple inputs. These multiple inputs can leverage network to produce the better SSK. Second, the multi-scale wavelet decomposition and SSK are used for modelling of MMRF to produce finer urban classification results. Finally, several experiments based on ISPRS dataset is used for demonstrate that proposed method can produce fine-grained land cover classification results than the state-of-the-art methods.

articleTitle: A novel method of space-borne cognitive SAR signal generation based on FPGA and DDS
abstract: Future space-borne cognitive synthetic aperture radar (SAR) can autonomously extract scene environment information in orbit, and use knowledge base and intelligent decision processing technology to quickly adjust radar signal parameters to achieve adaptive detection. Therefore, the space-borne cognitive SAR needs to have the ability to generate signals autonomously and controllably. A controllable generation method of space-borne cognitive SAR signals based on FPGA is proposed in this paper, which introduces the time-domain hybrid sampling technology and uses multiple under-sampling FPGA on-chip direct digital synthesizers (DDS) to work together. It can automatically calculate the phase parameters of each DDS according to the input signal parameters such as the frequency bandwidth, and time width of the radar signal. Multi-channel under-sampled linear frequency modulated signals are generated by the multiple DDS, and then spliced in the time domain and output to an external high-speed DAC to obtain the final intermediate-frequency SAR chirp signals. Simulation analysis shows that the proposed method can generate intermediate frequency SAR signals with any frequency bandwidth in the range of 50MHz to 450MHz, when the high-speed DAC with a sampling rate of 2.0 GSPS is selected. This method can meet the needs of on-orbit intelligent adjustment of space-borne cognitive SAR chirp signals.

articleTitle: Four quadrants array antenna design for monopulse radar applications
abstract: A two-dimensional (2D) monopulse microstrip array antenna for X-band missile terminal guidance radar application is proposed. The design consists of microstrip array radiation front-end and four quadrants microstrip hybrid couplers back-end. The microstrip array comprises four rectangular patches etched on the top side of upper substrate layer. Four corresponding 3dB directional couplers are connected to form a four quadrant monopulse comparator and etched on the bottom side of lower substrate layer. Both layers are made of Rogers 5880 substrate and punched with four metal probes to prove the feeding from back-end to front-end. The whole structure can be fabricated with standard multilayer printed circuit board (PCB) or 3D printing process. Optimization results show about 11.5dBi max gain of sum pattern and -28dB null-depth of difference pattern in E and H planes at 10GHz center frequency.

articleTitle: Polarimetric bias correction of alternate-arranged V-Dipole array
abstract: This paper aims to eliminate the polarimetric biases of V-dipole phased array antennas using lower measurement cost. We analyze the polarization characteristics of the V-dipole with the integration method. An alternate-arranged 8×8 V-dipole array is designed and simulated. Based on the analysis of mutual coupling, the polarimetric performance of the array is presented. To correct the polarimetric biases using lower measurement cost, a cluster-based method is proposed to reconstruct the array pattern. The method uses partial elements to design polarimetric correction and treats the selection of elements as a clustering problem. The results prove the method helpful to minimize the biases using limited measurement cost.

articleTitle: Joint estimation of DOA and mutual coupling for wideband signals via block multiple measurement vectors
abstract: Based on the structure of block joint sparsity, a wideband DOA estimation method is proposed in the presence of unknown mutual coupling. First, the wideband array signal model is established with the Toeplitz property of mutual coupling matrix for the uniform linear array. Next the block sparse recovery model of each sub-band frequency is transformed into the block multiple measurement vectors (BMMV) model of the whole wideband signal by focusing operation. Then, a novel BMMV algorithm is proposed. Finally, the proposed algorithm is used to realize the joint estimation of the wideband DOA and the mutual coupling matrix. Simulation results show the effectiveness and feasibility of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Fast frequency domain reverse-time migration based on NUFFT for ground penetrating radar
abstract: The traditional migration algorithms for ground penetrating radar (GPR) imaging have the disadvantages of low accuracy and high computational complexity. Therefore, a fast frequency-domain reverse-time migration (FRTM) algorithm for GPR based on nonuniform fast Fourier transform (NUFFT) is proposed in this paper. The proposed algorithm is formulated by spectrum Green's function, which avoids the multiple extrapolations of forward and backward wavefields, and greatly saves the calculation and storage resources. Furthermore, NUFFT is adopted to handle the uneven and huge amount of data collected in the actual scenario. Therefore, the rapid accumulation of imaging results can be achieved for each shot in the frequency domain. Simulation results show that the proposed algorithm can formulate the same high-quality focused image as conventional time-domain RTM algorithm but less time and storage resources are required. The proposed algorithm is suitable for real-time imaging of GPR equipment.

articleTitle: Modified frequency division algorithm for motion compensation of synthetic aperture radar
abstract: For high-resolution synthetic aperture radar (SAR) system, the acquired echoes are easily contaminated by the platform's deviations that are referred to as motion errors. The motion errors behave the properties of range- and aperture-variance and degrades the final image severely, which makes motion compensation become an essential procedure. In this paper, a modified frequency division algorithm (MFDA) has been developed based on the azimuth-frequency mapping and time-scaling transform. The proposed method takes into account both the range- and aperture-variant characteristics of residual motion errors and could completely compensate the along-track and cross-track motion errors. Moreover, this fashion could be integrated into the traditional image formation algorithms with no changes. Finally, we would present numerical experimental results charactering the performance of the proposed MFDA.

articleTitle: Design and implementation of image feature parallel computing system based on FGPA
abstract: The extraction of image features is the basis for the realization of image tracking algorithms. In the field of civil radar, an algorithm for pedestrian recognition by fusion of visual information and millimeter-wave radar information has emerged. The fusion of visual feature information with radar information is a development direction in the field of target detection in the future. This paper introduces an feature calculation system, which uses the high parallelism of FPGA to complete the calculation of HOG and LBP features and uses advanced fusion to quickly complete the fusion of the two features. At the same time, the system designed an improved double-pipeline structure to calculate the HAAR feature. The final feature calculation system is implemented on the Zedboard of Xilinx. And apply it to a specific tracking algorithm, the algorithm processing efficiency is greatly improved.

articleTitle: A novel blind tracking method for high-speed laser communication
abstract: In this paper, a novel decision feedback tracking method is proposed, which is based on frame demodulation for high-speed laser communication with less prior information. In order to reduce the length of the pilots and improve the tracking accuracy, a frequency control word addressing and pointing decision algorithm are introduced to recover the local pseudo code from the received data for tracking. Simulation results demonstrate that in the high-speed laser radar communication, this method has better tracking performance than traditional methods when the pilot length is short.

articleTitle: SAR target recognition combining class information and classification hyperplane
abstract: Automatic target recognition (ATR) in synthetic aperture radar (SAR) images plays an important role. An important step in SAR target recognition is to transform the raw data to a feature space with the property of within-class compactness and between-class separation. However, due to the problem of target aspect angle sensitivity in SAR images, the difference of some targets belonging to the same class in different poses is greater than the difference of targets belonging to different class in similar poses, which often causes misjudgement. To solve this problem, we first use the twin support vector machine (TWSVM) to obtain the classification hyperplane of each class. Then, based on the obtained hyperplane, the projection matrix is constructed by fusing the prior class information of the target. In this way, the sample can be close to the classification hyperplane of the same class and distant from the classification hyperplane of a different class. This algorithm can improve TWSVM's ability to classify SAR images. Experiments are conducted on the moving and stationary target acquisition and recognition (MSTAR) database. The results verify the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Comparison of time-domain algorithms for video synthetic aperture radar processing on landing trajectory
abstract: This paper describes an implementation of fast factorized back-projection algorithm for parabolic landing trajectory. A new method of creating polar coordinates with fast factorized back-projection algorithm is proposed to solve the problem that the cosine law is invalid in nonlinear flights. The image quality parameters of direct back-projection and fast factorized back-projection algorithms would be analysed in the application of video synthetic aperture radar, and the imaging processing efficiency would be compared to select the most suitable algorithm for video synthetic aperture radar imaging under parabolic landing track.

articleTitle: Radar and infrared fusion scheme for artillery locating radar
abstract: In order to enable the artillery locating radar to grasp the battlefield dynamics in real time, a multi-sensor fusion method of the artillery locating radar was designed. Radar and infrared sensors are scientifically fused. Use the mode of radar shutdown and infrared sensor working normally to achieve continuous monitoring of battlefield dynamic. When the infrared sensor detects the target, it immediately triggers the radar to turn on, and reports the target's azimuth, pitch and other information to the radar host computer, thereby guiding the radar to quickly detect the target airspace. Experimental results show that this method can effectively shorten the early warning time, and it takes about 0.6s from infrared discovery to radar detection to the target. Radar and infrared sensor realize information complementation, and have better battlefield silence ability and survivability, which can provide strong support for our equipment to evade strikes and find enemy weapon launch positions.

articleTitle: Detection, tracking and recognition of multi-targets using fusion data from different sensors
abstract: To unify the multi-targets detection, tracking and recognition in the surveillance system, a multi-targets detection, tracking and recognition method using the fusion data from different sensors is proposed, which is based on jump Markov system model Gaussian mixture probability hypothesis density filtering (JMS-GMPHDF). First, the multi-model Gaussian mixture probability hypothesis density filtering (GMPHDF) of multi-targets is independently designed according to the different categories of targets, and the Gaussian terms are labeled during the processing of each filter. Second, Gaussian term synthesis and category judgment are performed based on the speed and acceleration information of targets, and the type judgment is performed based on the electronic support measures (ESM) information. Final, through comprehensive management of the track, a certain track with the information of the movement status, category, model and track number can be formed. Simulation experiments verify that the method can effectively synthesize the radar and ESM data, make the correct category and model judgments, and finally form a deterministic track during the detection and tracking.

articleTitle: Geometry and signal properties of multiple azimuth angle spaceborne SAR
abstract: The multiple azimuth angle spaceborne (MAAS) SAR can observe the region-of-interest (ROI) with different azimuth angles during single pass, which can significantly increase the flexibility of SAR observation and obtain more information of ROI. However, the imaging geometry and signal properties vary complexly with azimuth angles during single pass. Thus, in this paper, the geometry and signal properties are studied for the MAAS SAR. Firstly, the MAAS SAR is introduced and the imaging geometry is built. Then the geometry properties are analysed by simulations. Finally , the signal properties , including the range cell migration (RCM), azimuth resolution, two-dimensional (2-D) spectrum, and 2-D impulse response function (IRF), are studied both by theoretical analysis and simulations. All of the results and conclusions can be helpful for the system design, imaging algorithm development and application of MAAS SAR.

articleTitle: A novel target detection method based on convolutional neural networks
abstract: The purpose of radar target detection is to discover targets and separate them from background noise and clutter. Traditional detection methods, such as constant false alarm rate (CFAR) detectors, are all based on statistic models of noise and clutter. A novel target detection method based on convolutional neural networks (CNN) is proposed in this paper. Firstly the received radar signals enter a CFAR detector with a low threshold. Then outputs of the CFAR detector are further tested by using a trained CNN to decide whether there exists a true target at the cell under test (CUT). Such a detection method is named CFAR-CNN detector. Compared to the traditional CFAR detector, the proposed method can offer a high probability of detection and achieve a significantly low false alarm rate at the same time. The experiment based on measured radar data in sea clutter background verifies the excellent performance of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A weak target integration detection scheme based on MSK-LFM radon-fourier transform
abstract: The weak target detection is an important problem in radar signal processing research. To improve the radar detection performance, a novel integration detection scheme via Minimum Frequency Shift Keying-Linear Frequency Modulation Radon-Fourier transform (MSK-LFM-RFT) is proposed. Firstly, the single frequency carrier of MSK signal is changed into LFM signal's carrier. Then MSK-LFM integrated signal is given. Secondly, the weak target echoes, after pulse compression, can be integrated via MSK-LFM-RFT. Finally, a weak target exists or not is confirmed by Constant False Alarm Rate (CFAR) detection. Numerical experiment results show that weak targets' detection probability can be significantly improved via RFT algorithm without changing the hardware system of radar. And the different signal number (SN) and distribution may affect the integration effect of MSK-LFM-RFT. Compared with Direct Sequence-Chirp Spread Spectrum Radon-Fourier transform (DS-CSS-RFT), the detection performance of MSK-LFM-RFT is better because of the continuous phase of the waveform.

articleTitle: Fast algorithm of joint polarization and DOA estimation for irregular array under coherent sources
abstract: In the framework of array signal processing, the rank loss of signal covariance matrix of coherent sources causes the failing of subspace decomposition algorithm, therefore the subspace fitting technique (SFT) is conventionally employed to estimate the direction of arrival (DOA) of bearings. The drawback of SFT is its high computational complexity, especially when the polarization and DOA of bearings both need to be estimated which requires a four-dimensional search. Meanwhile, due to the antenna arrays in the actual environment is mostly irregular, the generalized fast algorithm of estimation of array signal processing cannot be utilized. In the paper, the fast algorithm of joint polarization-DOA estimation is developed for irregular array under coherent sources. Aiming at the disadvantage that the polarization smoothing algorithm destroys the polarization information, the generalized subspace fitting algorithm is studied which separates the spatial angle and the polarization angle estimation. In order to fix the problem of excessive calculation of generalized subspace fitting algorithm, the oblique projection algorithm is studied. The polarization vector of the bearing signal can obtained through projection algorithm with less computational effort. Simulation proves the effectiveness of the proposed algorithms.

articleTitle: A new jamming method against ground-based radar with long pulse duration based on partial signal sampling theory and frequency-shifting
abstract: In order to achieve longer detection range and higher range resolution, the pulse compression radar usually adopts the chirp signal with a large product of time width and bandwidth as the transmitted signal. Considering that the transmitting antenna and receiving antenna of a jammer work in a time-sharing mode in practical engineering, then the corresponding delay time of jammer after detecting radar signal will become much longer, which may degrade the deception performance of the range deception signal on radar target detection. To solve this problem, this paper proposes a new style of jamming signal based on partial sampling and frequency-shifting jamming signal, which can produce realistic decoy target by sampling partial pulse of radar signal and performing the frequency-shifting. The proposed method is simple to implement and hence provides a valuably theoretical reference to realistically realize the deceptive interference corresponding to a ground-based radar system with long pulse duration.

articleTitle: A novel SAR groung moving target imaging algorithm
abstract: The movement of the target leads to range cell migration (RCM) and Doppler frequency migration (DFM), which seriously threatens the ground moving target imaging. To overcome those problems, the paper gives a novel Synthetic aperture radar (SAR) ground moving target imaging method based on least square method (LSM) and Lv's distribution (LVD). Firstly, the known radar platform motion parameters are used for completing the range curvature correction. Secondly, the efficient LSM assists in estimating the range walk scope, and completing the range walk correction, the same scattering point energy is collected into the same range cell. Thirdly, the LVD is used for obtaining motion parameters related to scatterers, together with completing the high-order term compensation, and obtaining the ground moving target image. Finally, the proposed method is validated via the simulated as well as real SAR data processing results.

articleTitle: A parameter estimation method for binary frequency shift keying radar signal intercepted by nyquist folding receiver
abstract: Nyquist folding receiver (NYFR) is one of novel ultra-wideband receiving structures. The NYFR can intercept radar signal in a wide frequency space with high interception probability and it can intercept the signal beyond the restriction of the Nyquist sampling theory. The binary frequency shift keying (2FSK) signal has been widely employed in many radar systems. Therefore, the 2FSK radar signal will be intercepted by the NYFR. In this paper, the parameter estimation of the 2FSK signal intercepted by the NYFR is investigated. The NYFR output signal model is firstly given and the estimation process is analysed mathematically. Finally, several simulations demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: High-speed target range compensation for terahertz ISAR based on a real-time measurement scheme
abstract: Due to the short wavelength and large bandwidth, Terahertz radar can achieve high resolution in a very short time, which is widely explored for high-speed moving targets. However, the target reflection in Terahertz band varies much faster compared in other band, i.e. the correlation degrades heavily between adjacent echoes. It brings a big challenge to traditional range alignment methods in THz-ISAR imaging. Considering the real-time processing for high speed, a new range alignment scheme is proposed in this paper. The instantaneous velocity and range are estimated during a short interval, which can be used for range compensation of dispersion induced by high speed and envelope walk. This method mitigates the influence of degrade correlation and low SNR, and has potential for maneuvering targets. Simulation and real data experiments validate the performance of this scheme.

articleTitle: Location accuracy analysis of multi-angle SAR based on radargrammetry method
abstract: The spaceborne multi-angle SAR can perform multi-azimuth observation of the same scene with different obliquity orbits, and the target can be located by the multi-angle SAR images with the radargrammetry method. The positioning accuracy of target is affected by the system error and coregistration error. In this paper, the target location accuracy of multi-angle SAR is quantitatively analyzed. The stereo radargrammetry location accuracy of single orbit and multi-orbit images with different azimuth angles is analysed with simulated experimental data.

articleTitle: Analysis of HRWS MIMO-SAR system based on satellite formation along track
abstract: This paper analyses the influence of the scaling changes of the distributed sparse array of the small satellite along track on the space position of the small satellite, as well as the influence on the signal reconstruction. The satellite position variable is an affine function of the time variable. The linear term of satellite spacing along track causes nonuniform spatial sampling, whereas the linear term of vertical baseline causes signal steering vector mismatch. Both can resolve the Doppler ambiguity. The results of the simulation reveal that the distributed satellite sparse long arrays are equivalent to dense short arrays. Moreover, the effect of the linear term on the performance of the distributed multiple-input multiple-output synthetic aperture radar system is analysed based on dense short arrays.

articleTitle: NLOS target localization behind an L-shaped corner based on grid matching
abstract: This paper considers utilizing radar multipath returns to locate a non-line of sight (NLOS) target hidden behind an L-shaped corner. To handle this problem, we propose a novel NLOS target localization algorithm based on grid matching. First, a multipath propagation model based on the characters of the real data received by an L-band single-input single-output (SISO) ultra-wideband (UWB) radar is established. Then, a novel NLOS target localization algorithm based on times of arrival (TOAs) of round-trip multipath returns to construct the grid matching matrix is proposed. The principle of this algorithm is to calculate the TOAs of each grid based on the multipath propagation model, and then find the grid that is closest to the measured TOAs. This method can cope with the case while some missing multipaths happen. Simulation and experimental results validate the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: A robust equalization method for dechirp channels
abstract: The dechirp technology can greatly reduce the hardware speed requirements for large data acquisition for a wideband phased array radar using a linear frequency-modulated signal. But the echo was associated with amplitude and phase fluctuations caused by in-band fluctuations in fast time. In the actual system, due to the dechirp distance window error, the fast time compensation coefficient may not be aligned with the actual frequency. A robust equalization method is proposed for dechirp channels in this paper.Simulation results show that this method can effectively achieve the robust processing for fast-time channel compensation.

articleTitle: Angles estimation for wideband signals using ARC nested array
abstract: According to the theory of nested array, this paper consider the problem for direction of arrival estimation for wideband sources using arc nested array. This array can provide more degrees of freedom than that from uniform linear array (ULA) with the same sensors, and enable to estimate K sources with M<;K sensors. By means of interpolation technique, we convert the arc array to a virtual non-uniform linear array firstly, then the problem for arc nested array can be solved equivalently to a linear nested array. Based on the wideband signal model established by the arc nested array, the coherent signal subspace method (CSM) is used to estimate the wideband signal DOA.

articleTitle: Simulation of time-varying wideband radar scattering characteristics for targets above sea surface
abstract: In this paper, a new procedure is proposed for simulation of the time-varying wideband radar scattering characteristics of targets above sea surface. A geometric model of the composite target-sea scene is developed by combination of target aerodynamics and time-varying sea surface generation. Multipath scattering model is applied to address the electromagnetic (EM) scattering interaction between the target and the sea surface, where high frequency approximation techniques are used for EM scattering calculation. Simulated Doppler spectra and high resolution range profiles (HRRPs) are presented to demonstrate the validity and usefulness of the proposed procedure.

articleTitle: Modulation recognition of emitter signals based on SDAE-ODCNN
abstract: In order to improve the recognition rate of emitter signals modulation under low signal noise ratio (SNR), an end-to-end method based on the stacked denoising autoencoder (SDAE) - one dimensional convolutional neural network (ODCNN) is proposed in this paper. The SADE-ODCNN is designed in this method and trained through a two-step training. In the SDAE-ODCNN model, the encoder of the SDAE can extract the denoised and compressed features of the received emitter signals. Then the ODCNN can further extract features to realize the recognition. The simulation results show that the average recognition rate of the method can reach 0.94 under 0dB. Thus the proposed method has a good application in the field of emitter signals modulation recognition.

articleTitle: High-resolution detection of near-distance range and azimuth with vortex electromagnetic waves
abstract: The vortex electromagnetic (EM) radar, which carries orbital angular momentum, can provide extra rotational degree of freedom and potentially be exploited in high-resolution detection of near-distance range and azimuth. The near-field detection principle of EM vortex wave is introduced. Through the echo mathematical modelling and analysis of the vortex electromagnetic wave, the processing of near-distance range and azimuth is obtained. The simulation analysis demonstrates that the developed method has better high-resolution detection performance of range and azimuth in near distance.

articleTitle: Detection method based on network model trained with mixed data sets
abstract: In complex scenes and practical applications, the traditional radar target detection method has inaccurate matching of clutter and target characteristics, resulting in a serious decline in its detection performance. In response to this problem, this paper presents a network model trained with mixed data sets to complete the radar target detection task. Specifically, we mix the time-frequency graphs of different sea regime data sets on IPIX radar and different polarization data sets on IPIX radar, and then input them into the designed convolutional neural network model for detector training and testing. Experimental results show that this method can extract data features well, improve the poor adaptability of detection networks under different data sets, obtain higher classification accuracy, and is more suitable for application in complex actual scenarios.

articleTitle: Sentinel-1 Quasi-PS InSAR for identification and monitoring of landslide deformation
abstract: Landslide is one of the major geological disasters in the world that causes casualties and economic losses. The Differential Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (DInSAR) is an important landslide monitoring technology. However, due to the limited to SAR image resolution, small-scale landslide is often difficult to identify and monitor effectively with PSI technology. Low-resolution images that greatly reduce the density of Permanent Scatters (PSs) of the monitoring area, limiting the wide application of this technology in practice. Thus, Sentinel-1 IW mode images combined with Quasi-PS InSAR enables the application of DInSAR techniques in small-scale landslide monitoring. In this study, Quasi-PS InSAR has been employed together to 41 Sentinel-1 (S1) images, IW mode, to monitor the landslides (Three Gorges Reservoir Area, China). The results show that the S1 data and Quasi-PS InSAR allows for obtaining high density of PSs. Due to the high effective PSs density, the boundaries of the landslide deformation of the Fanjiaping landslide has been highlighted. This study indicates that the Quasi-PS InSAR together with S1 data can be an important means to characterize deformation rates and extension of complex small-scale landslides in challenging areas.

articleTitle: Impulse through-the-wall radar imaging method based on one-bit compressive sensing
abstract: The one-bit compressive sensing (CS) signal reconstruction methods perform data measurement using only the sign information with one bit, which can alleviate the burden of storage and transmission of large data volume and reduce the cost of the analog-to-digital converter. In this paper, a new one-bit CS based imaging method for impulse through-the-wall radar (TWR) system is developed. The proposed imaging algorithm named by enhanced-binary iterative hard thresholding (E-BIHT) algorithm utilizes the two-level block sparsity to achieve imaging reconstruction of observed scene. The simulation results show that the proposed imaging approach can provide the enhanced imaging reconstruction quality with higher reconstructed signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) compared to the traditional BIHT imaging algorithm.

articleTitle: The comparison of sensitivity and dynamic range for different phased array architectures
abstract: In this article, a general hybrid beam-forming model was used to analyze the difference between x kinds of active antenna array architectures. A two-dimension diagram and a figure of merit with two digitization factors wereproposed to assess the digitization level of these different architectures. Also, based on a cascade methodology, we conducted theoretical analysis on the sensitivity and dynamic range performance of the hybrid beam-forming receiving systems regarding both analog and digital domains, which have fewer mentioned in previous studies. Under several simplification assumptions, the general cascade expression degraded to the classic cascade formulas with two revisions. A further comparison was taken between the two digitization factors as independent variables The result reveals a simple but significant conclusion that assuming using the same components, the sensitivity and dynamic range performance advance along with the increase of the digitization level, and it reach the optimum when the array becomes element-level full digitization.

articleTitle: The development of low-noise pulse traveling wave tube amplifier for radar scatterometer
abstract: The traditional pulse traveling wave tube amplifier has been faced with some technical problems, such as high noise power spectral density, poor internal clutter index and low re-frequency gate modulation stability, which seriously restricted its application in the direction of radar scatterometer. A new type of low-noise pulse Traveling Wave Tube Amplifier (TWTA) is developed. The power supply firstly uses active filter controlled by pulse width modulation (PWM) technology to reduce the pulse current fluctuation of satellite bus. Secondly, a linear voltage regulator based on proportional integral differential (PID) regulation is used at the back stage of boost circuit to further reduce the ripple noise of cathode. The modulator circuit uses the multi-stage suspension isolation technology and frequency spreading circuit to increase the modulator gating stability and realize the function of low repetition pulse width modulation. Based on the above designed low-noise pulse traveling wave tube amplifier integrated with the power supply and TWT, the technical indexes that the noise power spectral density of the amplifier is lower than -110dBm /Hz and the clutter rejection of the product is lower than -75dBc are realized. It is applied to flight verification of a scattering scoring system to achieve the target that the wind speed measurement is better than 1.5m/s.

articleTitle: Detection and tracking of multiple targets using dual-frequency interferometric radar
abstract: Multiple-target tracking (MTT) usually requires either a network of distributed radars at different locations or single radar installed with expensive phased arrays. The moving targets with small radial velocity cannot be localized/tracked in 2-D space using single Doppler radar without an antenna array. To overcome this problem, we propose a new MTT method using dual-frequency interferometric radar. Targets' detection is performed based on the range-Doppler map, while tracking is accomplished by extracting radial and angular velocities from time-varying Doppler and interferometric spectrogram, respectively. However, the presence of multiple moving targets in radar field-of-view (FoV) generates nuisance intermodulation terms in the interferometric response. The dual-frequency interferometric radar is capable of resolving this issue by transmitting high frequency waveforms for radial velocity extraction and low frequency waveforms to extract angular velocity while suppressing intermodulation terms. The correct association between 2-D velocities of each target is performed by determining initial direction of arrival (DOA). The Global Nearest Neighbor (GNN) method for measurement-to-track association is followed by modified gain extended Kalman filter (MGEKF) to estimate the state of each target separately. The proposed algorithm is simple to implement in practice and removes the need of radar network and complex array processing techniques. Extensive simulation results have been presented to evaluate the performance of the proposed algorithm in terms of root mean square error (RMSE) in state and trajectory estimation.

articleTitle: An angle estimation method after mainlobe interference suppression
abstract: Target angle estimation plays a significant role in the field of radar detection. However, current electromagnetic environment is becoming increasingly complex, where the mainlobe interference would dramatically decrease the performance of radar angle estimation. This paper proposed a method of angle estimation based on maximum likelihood estimation for mainlobe interference suppression scenarios. An angle estimation loss function after spatial filtering is derived, and the target angle is estimated by minimizing the loss function. The effectiveness of proposed method is illustrated by simulations.

articleTitle: Riemannian distance based generalized side-lobe cancellation method for nonstationary clutter suppression
abstract: High-frequency mixed-mode surface wave radar combines advantages of both surface wave radar and sky wave radar and is capable of ocean remote sensing and early warning. However, the non-stationary clutter is the biggest challenge for the practical radar system which can submerge the low velocity vessels. Generalized side-lobe cancellation method has been successfully developed to suppress the clutter in high-frequency radar, but the performance of the method degrades in heterogeneous environment for the clutter statistics changes significantly. The invalid training data degrades the clutter suppression performance. To suppress the non-stationary clutter efficiently, a Riemannian distance based generalized side-lobe cancellation method is proposed to select the valid training data and improve the performance. Firstly, a single notch filter and virtual sliding sub-array method are utilized to block the main-lobe component. Then, a Riemannian distance based training data selection strategy is proposed to suppress the non-stationary clutter. The validity of the proposed method has been examined by measured data.

articleTitle: Fast factorized digital beam forming for conformal array
abstract: Digital beam forming (DBF) is capable of generating high resolution scanning patterns in pitch and azimuth dimension significant for electrical scanning. When the number of array elements is large and scanning resolution is high, the calculation complexity becomes a heavy burden for DBF method. In order to solve this problem, a subarray-based conformal array fast factorized DBF(FFDBF) algorithm is proposed. This method is based on the recursive principle to process subarray division and subarray beam forming in several levels. The lowest level subarray contains least array elements and smallest resolution of scanning pattern. The scanning patterns of lower level subarray are interpolated and added to form scanning pattern of higher level subarray. Following this method, a high-resolution scanning pattern of the whole array is formed and effectiveness of the proposed method is verified by simulation results.

articleTitle: A high-resolution imaging experiment with mini-UAV-based stepped frequency BFSAR
abstract: SAR system can achieve high range resolution by transmitting signals of large bandwidth, which is not easy especially for mini-UAV-based bistatic forward-looking SAR (BFSAR) system due to the platform limitation of load capacity and power consumption. Meanwhile, the bistatic configuration requires high clock synchronization between transmitter and receiver. In this paper, a stepped frequency SAR system is used to obtain high resolution image. Firstly, we introduce the experimental system and the hardware coarse synchronization. Secondly, we use the information of direct-path signal to further compensate the synchronization error, and splice the sub-bands to reconstruct the broadband spectrum. Finally, the effectiveness of the stepped frequency system and the imaging processing are verified by real data.

articleTitle: Modelling and analysis of sea clutter’s influences on airship-borne weather radar for typhoon observation
abstract: The weather radar on the airship can receive not only the echo of meteorological particles but also sea clutter in the typhoon observation over the sea surface. Since sea clutter will interfere with the monitoring of rain targets, it is necessary to clarify the impacts of sea clutter. This paper mainly studies the modelling and analysis of the effects of the mainlobe clutter and sidelobe clutter on the airship-borne weather radar observations. Besides, the signal-to-clutter ratio (SCR) of the clutter area is quantitatively estimated and calculated. Finally,it can be concluded that the SCRs in the area affected by the mainlobe clutter are less than 20dB when the incident angle is below 60 degrees and the SCRs in the area affected by the sidelobe clutter are mostly less than 20dB for small incident angles (<;10 degrees). The research can support the further researches on clutter suppression methods in airship-born weather radar.

articleTitle: Study on spaceborne multi-channel SAR moving target positioning technology
abstract: The doppler frequency generated by the target's radial moving will cause its azimuth position in the SAR image to deviate from the true position. In order to obtain the true position of the target, it needs to be relocated. However, when the PRF of a multi-channel system is smaller than the doppler bandwidth, directly using traditional methods will cause spectrum aliasing. This paper proposed a multi-channel spaceborne SAR moving target positioning algorithm combined with spectrum reconstruction algorithm. This method improves the positioning width and expands the application range of traditional methods. In addition, this paper also gave an analysis on the impact of SCNR on positioning accuracy, and the requirement of SCNR can be calculated back through the expected positioning error boundary. Finally, the algorithm was verified by simulation data.

articleTitle: Improved clutter-map detection for radar targets in K-distributed clutter
abstract: This paper deals with the problem of traditional constant false-alarm rate (CFAR) detection methods are difficult to adapt the temporal and spatial varying K-distributed clutter. An improved clutter-map detector combining a near optimal detector under K-distributed clutter and Nitzberg clutter-map technology is proposed. Obtaining a stable test statistic estimate of the clutter of the cell under test (CUT) according to the data of the CUT from past several scans, and the modified clutter map stores the test statistic estimate of each CUT. Each test statistic estimate is updated based on the data from a new scan as the new test statistic estimate of the current primary data. According to this proposed method, Nitzberg clutter-map technology can be combined with many different detectors to adapt different clutter model. Then the proposed method and the existing methods are compared from the aspect of performance with simulation data. The experiments results demonstrate that the proposed method has better performance than the existing detectors.

articleTitle: DOA estimation method of short snapshots based on cultural pigeon-inspired optimization algorithm
abstract: In order to overcome the shortcomings of the existing traditional DOA estimation methods which require lots of snapshots, a maximum likelihood (ML) function based on reconstructing pseudo-covariance (RP) matrix from the received short snapshots data is designed and named as RP-ML. To obtain the optimal solution of RP-ML, cultural pigeon-inspired optimization (CPIO) algorithm is designed to solve the RP-ML function with high convergent accuracy and fast convergent speed. The simulation results show that the proposed method which is called as CPIO-RP-ML is superior to previous DOA estimation methods with short snapshots. CPIO-RP-ML not only can find the direction of coherent sources, but also can obtain excellent performance with single snapshot, and it is very valuable for engineering applications.

articleTitle: Multi-scale saliency-based ship detection in SAR images
abstract: Airborne or satellite-based synthetic aperture radar (SAR) is an effective system for detecting ships because of its working all-weather. However, SAR images have complex speckles from sea clutters result automatic ship detection is a challenging task. This paper proposes a multi-scale visual saliency method for automatically detecting ships in SAR image data. The proposed model is simple, less computationally expensive and capable of detecting ship targets in SAR data. Experiments on real SAR data show that our model could detect ships accurately by using multi-scale analysis and saliency information fusion.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic scattering characteristics of targets for bistatic low frequency ultra-wideband SAR
abstract: The low frequency ultra-wideband bistatic synthetic aperture radar (LF UWB BSAR) has the well penetrating ability, high-resolution imaging, as well as the increased information. In this paper, the electromagnetic scattering characteristic of the targets for the LF UWB BSAR has been analyzed. Firstly, the equivalent model of the targets is established. And then, the standard hexahedron discontinuous Galerkin time-domain (DGTD) method is proposed to calculate the bistatic radar cross section (RCS) of the targets. Simulation experiments are shown to prove the validity of the analyzing method for the electromagnetic scattering characteristics of the targets.

articleTitle: Spatial fuzzy C-means clustering and deep belief network for change detection in synthetic aperture radar images
abstract: In this study, spatial fuzzy c-means (SFCM) clustering and deep belief network (DBN) method is presented for change detection in SAR images. There are three primary steps of this approach, they are given as follows: 1) Difference Image (DI) is firstly obtained by calculating the similarity of gray levels between multitemporal SAR images. 2) SFCM clustering is used to analyze DI, which combines the spatial information factor and the fuzzy cluster membership function, thus can effectively eliminate the interference of speckle noise. 3) DBN, a powerful data processing methodology that integrates deep learning techniques to extract underlying features and structures of complicated data, is trained to classify pixels to be changed or unchanged. The effectiveness and robustness of the proposed method are verified by experimental results with the Ottawa dataset.

articleTitle: An accurate range model of moving target based on mth-order Taylor expansion for GEO SAR
abstract: Considering that Geosynchronous Earth orbital Synthetic Aperture Radar (GEO SAR) allowing a wide area viewing combined with short revisit cycle, it is suitable for many applications such as natural disaster monitoring, military reconnaissance and soil moisture detection. In this paper, a novel method for calculating the precise propagation distance of moving target in GEO SAR is proposed. This method mainly solves the following two problems: 1 Existing low-order Taylor expansion range model shows insufficient accuracy under ultralong integration time. 2 The iterative approximation range model has high accuracy but cannot be expressed by analytical expression. By deriving the general formula of the mth-order Taylor expansion of pulse transmitting and receiving distance, a complete set of processes to calculate the total propagation distance is formed, and the expansion order can be adjusted according to the error requirement. Finally, a series of simulation experiments have been conducted to verify the fitting effect of the new range model.

articleTitle: DOA estimation of coprime array based on quantum penguin search algorithm in impulse noise
abstract: We propose a new DOA estimation method to solve the following problems that few studies have applied for coprime array to impulse noise or multi-coherent source environments, and the existing DOA estimation technologies based on coprime array can not achieve highly accurate estimation under impulse noise, low signal-to-noise ratio, small snapshot number and multi-coherent source environment. In impulse noise environments, according to the snapshot sampling data of the received signals of the coprime (CP) array, and based on the virtual array of the coprime array, the extended infinite norm fractional lower-order covariance (INFLOC) matrix of the weighted signal is constructed, and a new robust maximum likelihood (ML) equation named as INFLOC-CPML is designed. Based on quantum coding, simulated quantum revolving gate and penguin search mechanism, the quantum penguin algorithm (QPA) is designed to efficiently solve the new equation and get high-precision optimal solution. In conclusion, the new DOA estimation method named as QPA-INFLOC-CPML has the advantages of faster speed, higher accuracy, decoherence, a larger array aperture, strong anti-impulse noise ability and wider application range.

articleTitle: A novel dual-band MIMO antenna for WLAN applications
abstract: A small-size dual-band MIMO antenna with high port isolation is presented. The proposed antenna is basically composed of two pair of folded planar monopoles with edge-to-edge separation of nearly 0.03λ0 at 2.4GHz. The high isolation is achieved by introducing a folded T-shaped stub attached to the ground plane in the middle of two pairs radiators. Detailed effects are analyzed. In the whole WLAN operating band, the simulated and measured isolation is more than 15dB, and the Envelope Correlation Coefficient (ECC) is less than 0.1. Furthermore, other good performance, radiation pattern and compact size could enable the proposed antenna to be used in portable devices.

articleTitle: Target classification based on radar track using bilstm
abstract: The track information is an important feature for radar target recognition. In this paper, the authors propose to classify targets based on radar track using bi-directional long short-term memory (BiLSTM) and self-attention mechanism. More specifically, the forward and backward operation in BiLSTM is able to capture temporal dependence of the track. The resulting deep resprentations of the track is refined by a self-attention mechanism to enhance the most discriminative parts. A fully connected layer followed by softmax operator is used to determine the type of the track. Experimental results show that the proposed method outperforms conventional algorithms.

articleTitle: A novel noncircular fourth-order DOA estimation algorithm exploiting the difference and sum co-array concept
abstract: In this paper, a novel co-array based noncircular (NC) fourth-order MUSIC algorithm is presented for detecting NC sources. The proposed method, whose array model can be arbitrary linear array, provides a strategy for efficiently combining NC property, cumulant operation and co-array concept. As a result, the difference and sum co-array (DSCA) can be constructed. Comprising both the difference set and the sum set, the DSCA has much larger aperture than the difference co-array (DCA) and the traditional NC virtual array. Particularly, since the cumulant operation instead of the Khatri-Rao (KR) product operation is adopted for constructing the co-array, the coherent issue usually generated by the KR product operation will not occur. Therefore, the available degree of freedom (DOF) will not be reduced by half. Furthermore, the proposed method can be considered as the basic theory for further constructing a high-order DSCA with higher DOF. Simulations evaluate the performance of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Weighted knowledge-aided matrix completion algorithm for wind turbine clutter mitigation
abstract: Matrix completion (MC) is the process of estimating missing entries from a matrix using some prior knowledge. However, when solving the MC problem, the same constant is used to threshold the singular value, which will lead to the loss of large singular values. Since the potentially weighted assisted information of different singular values can be obtained by the observation matrix, we apply a weighted knowledge-aided MC algorithm to weather radar wind turbine clutter (WTC) suppression. By assigning different weights to each singular value in the nuclear norm, it avoids thresholding all singular values with the same constant, and thus obtains the optimal approximation of the original matrix on the lower rank. Theoretical analysis and simulation results verify the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm, which can recover data with higher accuracy.

articleTitle: LFM-CCC orthogonal waveform design for MIMO-HFSWR
abstract: Applying MIMO technology into high frequency surface wave radar is a popular topic in recent years. This paper presents a new orthogonal waveform apply to MIMO high frequency surface wave radar, which is named as Linear Frequency Modulation - Complete Complementary Code (LFM-CCC). LFM-CCC combines the superiority both of LFM and Complete Complementary Code, can keep complete orthogonal between waveforms, and avoid the performance degradation due to doppler shift and signal truncation. This paper introduces the structure of LFM-CCC first, and deduces the ambiguity function of that. Then presents the step signal processing method, to resolve the question of doppler sensitivity. At last, we analyse the performance of LFM-CCC in MIMO-HFSWR. The simulation results show that LFM-CCC has the same auto-correlation performance with LFM, and has complete ideal cross-correlation performance in the meantime, which proves that LFM-CCC has an excellent performance used in MIMO-HFSWR.

articleTitle: A track initiation method for radar target tracking based on B-spline curve interpolation
abstract: A novel efficient track initiation method based on B-spline curve interpolation is proposed. The framework of the proposed method is built based on a dynamic programming track-before-detect framework with B-spline curve interpolation. In order to effectively detect the target in the clutter area, B-spline curve interpolation algorithm is used to accumulate the energy of the candidate target along a valid curve rather than a straight line. The continuous smoothness of the B-spline ensures the continuity of the velocity acceleration of the track, and its locality enables the curve shape of the track to be adapted. Because the curvature of track curve is limited by dynamic overload, the curvature can be calculated by B-spline curve to limit the false track. Meanwhile, the measurement error of the radar system is used as a constraint condition. The experiment results show that the method proposed in this paper has better track initiation accuracy, lower error rate and faster detecting speed compared with several traditional track initiation algorithms.

articleTitle: A new classification method of SAR image based on OGMRF-RC model
abstract: Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) image classification is a key technique and research focus in the application of remote sensing. This paper proposes a new classification method of SAR image based on Object-based Gaussian-Markov Random Field model with Region Coefficients (OGMRF-RC), the new method use Fuzzy Probability (FP) represents the region's category probability, FP is obtained by regional posterior probability and edge information of neighborhood. Use FP to replace the unique class label of the region, which avoids the parameters estimation inaccurate of the feature field caused by the unique initial class label. And the parameter calculation method of feature field takes into account the feature information of all regions in the image. In this paper, we take the area around Baliwan in Kaifeng as study area, Sentinel-1 is used as the remote sensing data sources. FCM, K-means, classic MRF and OGMRF-RC are used as contrast methods, the experimental result demonstrates the accuracy of our method is better than these methods.

articleTitle: A low complexity long-time coherent integration method for ubiquitous radar target detection
abstract: The Ubiquitous Radar (UR) system illuminates a wide coverage volume and provides continuous and uninterrupted multifunction capability. The target detection of UR system suffers from two problems: one is the low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of received signals, and the other is the large amount of data generated by multiple beams, which will reduce the performance of real-time processing. Long-time coherent integration is commonly used to improve the SNR; however, the UR system takes a long integration time, leading to severe range migration and Doppler frequency shift. This paper combines dechirp and Keystone Transform (KT) to compensate the Doppler frequency shift and range migration, and a method based on Sub-band Double Carrier Frequency Conjugated Processing (SDCFCP) is proposed to avoid ambiguity factor searching. The proposed method retains good integration performance and effectively reduces the cost of calculation. Simulation results validate the performance of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A low-sidelobe adaptive beamforming algorithm with single snapshot
abstract: Most of the existing adaptive beamforming (ADBF) algorithms require sufficient statistically independent and identically distributed data to estimate the covariance matrix. However, the number of snapshots is limited in practice, resulting in the degradation of the ADBF methods. Most ADBF algorithms can not work in a single snapshot because of non-invertible rank-one sample covariance matrix. The proposed method generates a pseudo full-rank sample covariance matrix using iterative Toeplitz approximation method (ITAM) under a single snapshot and estimates the direction of arrival (DOA) by MUSIC. With the estimated DOA, the method proposed in this paper minimizes the array gain of interference, maintains the distortion-free response of desired signal and controls sidelobe level (SLL) with an additional constraint. To improve the robustness against the imprecision of DOA estimation in directions of interference, the null broadening technique is used. It is demonstrated by computer simulations that the proposed algorithm is superior to other adaptive single-snapshot beamforming methods.

articleTitle: HRRP target recognition based on triple gramian angular field with convolutional neural network
abstract: High resolution range profile (HRRP) target recognition based on deep learning methods is mainly dedicated to changing the 2-Dimensional (2-D) convolutional neural network (CNN) framework into a 1-Dimensional (1-D) feature extractor. In this paper, a new algorithm called triple gramian angular field with CNN (TGAF-CNN) is proposed for HRRP recognition in the low signal-to-noise (SNR) condition. Different from traditional methods, HRRP is transformed into a 2-D image by TGAF. Compared with GAF feature, TGAF feature extend channels to achieve feature fusion which can extract more temporal information for higher recognition precision and better robustness. Then, 2-D CNN is used for recognition. Experiments based on real data from gun models indicate that TGAF-CNN can improve the HRRP recognition accuracy by about 4% compared to conventional deep learning methods.

articleTitle: Scaled model experiments for bistatic ISAR system
abstract: In monostatic ISAR imaging, the radar cannot be imaged when there is no obvious change of viewing angle relative to the target. Nevertheless, the bistatic (multi-base) radar system can realize imaging by observing targets from multiple perspectives. In this paper, a bistatic ISAR imaging method is adopted, and its imaging principle is analyzed in detail. Then its signal processing model and signal processing flow are introduced. This method eliminates the migration through resolution cell (MTRC). Finally, this algorithm is verified by the scaled model experiment in the anechoic chamber.

articleTitle: Data augmentation for hrrp based on generative adversarial network
abstract: In radar automatic target recognition (RATR), the data-driven model has proven to be a powerful tool. Nevertheless, its high requirement on the training dataset becomes a major restriction in many critical applications, especially on high resolution range profile (HRRP) based RATR. Data augmentation methods can improve the capabilities of data-driven model by increasing data diversity. As a deep generative model, the generative adversarial network (GAN) has demonstrated the effectiveness in data augmentation. In this paper, the authors apply GAN to augment the training data in data-driven RATR based on HRRP. Specifically, a GAN with one-dimensional (1D) fully connected structure is trained on the acquired HRRP data to learn the distribution of the whole data set. Then, the resulting generator is used to generate artificial HRRPs as the supplement to the acquired HRRP data set. Finally, the RATR system is trained on the augmented data set. Experiment results show that the proposed GAN-based HRRP augmentation method outperforms traditional augmentation methods, such as time-shift and mirroring.

articleTitle: Super-resolution imaging method based on target null theory
abstract: Due to the extremely successful application in remote sensing, polarimetric radar systems are used to observe a large number of manmade targets, such as urban areas, ships and vehicles, etc. These targets contain many dihedral and trihedral structures, which can be strong scattering points in a radar image. However, due to the limitation of resolution, some scatters in one resolution cell cannot be resolved, making it difficult to achieve the fine structure of manmade targets. In order to solve this problem, a super-resolution imaging method based on target null theory is presented in this paper.

articleTitle: Robust adaptive beamforming based on covariance matrix reconstruction via correlation coefficient of steering vector
abstract: Traditional adaptive beamformers are sensitive to model mismatch and they have poor performances when the input signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) is close to or more than interference-to-noise ratio (INR). In this letter, a novel robust adaptive beamforming (RAB) algorithm based on twice interference-plus-noise covariance (INC) matrix reconstruction is proposed. Firstly, the desired signal (DS) steering vector is estimated by the alternating projection algorithm based on the antenna array geometry and angular sector prior information. Then, the proposed method obtains the eigenvalue corresponding to DS by correlation coefficient and takes the place of it by noise power to obtain the first INC matrix. Furthermore, the second precise covariance matrix is reconstructed based on the theoretical INC matrix expression. The interferences powers are estimated by the theoretical formulation of the interference covariance matrix (ICM), which is derived from the first INC matrix. The simulation results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm achieves good performance especially when the input SNR is high, and its performance is close to the optimal beamformer in the case of look direction error.

articleTitle: An optimal allocation algorithm of tracking time resources for multiple manoeuvring targets in phased array radar based on mutual information
abstract: For phased array radar (Phased-Array Radar, PAR) multi-target tracking, the target threat degree is different, and mutual information (Mutual Information, MI) is used as the target tracking performance quantitative index. This paper establishes an optimization model of time resource allocation for multi-target tracking based on the degree of threat. The model divides the target to be tracked into two categories based on the threat degree. Different categories use different time resource allocation methods, and multiplier method is used to solve the model. The simulation results show that the method can make the radar keep track of various targets in the best state and the utilization rate of time resources is high.

articleTitle: Antenna position optimization based on adaptive genetic algorithm for distributed array radar
abstract: The detection performance of distributed array radar would be heavily influenced by the inappropriate design of antenna positions. Thus, an antenna position optimization method based on adaptive genetic algorithm is proposed. In the proposed method, the antenna position is directly coded as a chromosome with multiple constraints. And the fitness value of the chromosome is calculated according to the peak side lobe level (PSLL) of the beam pattern. Then, the probabilities of crossover and mutation are adaptively calculated for the chromosome. And the two-point crossover method and one-point mutation method are applied based on the adaptive probabilities. Because of the adaptive probabilities, the proposed method can not only obtain the antenna positons with lower PSLL, but also can get approximate PSLL with other methods by fewer antennas. Based on the simulation with linear coherent aperture radar, the proposed method is verified and the antenna positions with lower PSLL is get compared with conventional methods.

articleTitle: Robust knowledge-aid mainlobe maintain and jamming cancellation in two-dimensional digital array radar
abstract: Conventional adaptive beamforming cannot deal with the presence of both main and sidelobe jamming, which will lead to distortion and losing the ability of detecting target. To solve the complicated electromagnetic jamming problem, this letter proposes mainlobe maintain techniques for 2-D array. First, the jamming covariance matrix is estimated along azimuth and elevation dimensions, which is based on the knowledge-aid of jamming angle. The Linearly Constrained Minimum Variance (LCMV) beamforming is then adopted for mainlobe maintenance along azimuth and elevation separately. For the problem of prior knowledge accuracy for jamming angle, the jamming covariance matrix is in the form of integral to extend the width of side lobe jamming nulls. After mainlobe maintenance, mainlobe jamming can be cancelled and then do the monopulse angle measurement.

articleTitle: Adaptive mainlobe jamming suppression based on sparse reconstruction
abstract: In the complex jamming environment, the mainlobe jamming will extremely reduce the detection capabilities of radar. In this paper, an adaptive mainlobe jamming suppression based on sparse reconstruction is proposed. The steering vectors are estimated by using the maximize (MSNR) criterion. Besides, the oblique projection with ℓ1-norm singular value decomposition (OP-ℓ1-SVD) is performed to adaptively suppress the mainlobe jamming and DOAs estimation of the target with high precision. The demonstrate the proposed method which is based on a practically uniform linear array (ULA) model can resist at least two mainlobe jammings.

articleTitle: The optimal design of radar complementary waveform sets with sparse frequency
abstract: Sets of sequences with good correlation properties are desired in many active sensing and communication systems. However, in the crowded spectrum environment, the radar signal will be seriously interfered by other signals with the same frequency. In order to reduce the interference and improve the detection performance of the radar, it is necessary to design the optimal complementary waveform sets with sparse frequency. In this paper, we consider the complementary sets of sequences (CSS) design problem with good sparse frequency characteristics and low autocorrelation sidelobe characteristics. For this optimization problem, a cyclic iterative algorithm is proposed to solve the formulated model. In the process of cyclic iteration, the discrete Fourier transform is used to solve the above model step by step to reduce the load of calculation. Finally, numerical simulation shows that the optimized complementary waveforms have good sparse frequency characteristics and low autocorrelation sidelobe characteristics, which verify the effectiveness of the design method.

articleTitle: A hybird I/Q imbalance compensation approach for receiver array
abstract: Homodyne receiver architecture has been regarded as a promising solution to construct a low-cost, high-integration, power-efficient multi-function element-level digital phased array. However, one of the intrinsic drawbacks of homodyne architecture, namely in-phase and quadrature imbalance (I/Q imbalance) has not been fully addressed for the receiver arrays in previous articles, especially for broadband surveillance application dealing with multi-uncooperative signals. In this paper, a hybrid correction approach called random quadrature phase shift - adaptive compensation (RQPS-AC) is put forward to compensate consistent, random, and wideband I/Q imbalance for receiver arrays with arbitrary element number with only moderate computational resource requirement. Both the modified signal model and the two-stage correction structure are detailed. Following simulation results and comparison among existing algorithms demonstrate an optimal image rejection ratio (IRR) performance of our approach, with image signals successfully suppressing below the noise floor.

articleTitle: Research on grating lobe suppression technology of stepped frequency chirp signal
abstract: Stepped frequency chirp signal (SFCS) will inevitably introduce grating lobes during wideband synthesis processing, and system components as well as connection lines will introduce errors in the signal generation process. These errors will cause the grating lobes to deteriorate, making weak targets possible covered by grating lobes. To solve this problem, this paper first discusses the influence of waveform parameters on the grating lobe level, and then proposes the method of estimating the intra-pulse and inter-pulse magnitude error and phase error (MEPE) based on strong scattering point echoes, and conducting error compensation to achieve the purpose of grating lobe suppression (GLS). Both the simulation experiment and the processing results of the collected data by P-band uninhabited aerial vehicle radar verify the method.

articleTitle: High resolution SAR imagery with fully flexible prior
abstract: Followed by the development of high-resolution Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) imagery, the statistical characteristics of the scenes or targets of interests become highly complicated and dynamically varying. It is therefore difficult to extract the elaborated features for further classification and recognition. In this paper, a fully flexible prior, named by generalized Gaussian distribution (GGD), is introduced for the feature enhancement of SAR imagery in Bayesian inference manner. Due to the flexibility of the prior model, detailed structure of the scenes or targets can be resolved in the Bayesian inference way. To accommodate for the non-conjugacy of the prior, the Bayesian inference is developed in a hierarchical manner, which guarantees closed-form solutions of the features. Considering the difficulties in solving the posterior of the target image, the variable splitting scheme of Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM) is adopted, which is capable of separating the joint optimization into multiple sub-problems. This can simplify the computational complexity in a great extent. Finally, a proximity modified Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) sampling method is applied to solve the posterior, which ensures the computational efficiency with a satisfying level. Raw SAR data of stationary scene and moving target are used for the verification, and evaluations of Phase Transition Diagram (PTD) analysis is performed to show the superiority of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Adaptive strategy optimization with multi-agent machine learning in the game of radar countermeasure
abstract: Traditional radar countermeasure usually acts with some pre-defined strategies, ignoring the dynamic changes of both sides. In this paper, the scenario of radar countermeasure is represented as a two-player zero-sum dynamic game, where each player adaptively optimizes its own strategy. Specifically, according to game theory, two effective multi-agent machine learning methods, i.e. multi-stage minimax backward induction and deep counterfactual regret minimization are utilized to obtain the final strategies for both players. The experimental results demonstrate that the learned strategies for both players are more effective and reasonable than some simple strategies.

articleTitle: Maneuver behaviors identification under various window lengths based on deep 1D convolutional neural network
abstract: As more and more highly maneuver targets appear in the radar field of vision, new requirements are placed on the situational awareness and detection capabilities of maneuver targets. In order to enhance the intelligent perception ability of maneuver targets, a maneuver behavior recognition method based on deep learning is considered. Though the architecture of convolutional neural network(CNN) realizes feature extraction automatically from typically two dimensional (2D) or three dimensional (3D) signals, such as pictures and videos respectively, since the method of 2D/3D model in the image processing of CNN is not fitting for time series signal of maneuver behaviors, so under the analysis of behaviors' sequence characteristics and further modifying of the usual 2D CNN architecture, a one dimension deep convolutional neural network(1D-CNN) model is constructed to extract data features. Also, the sliding sampling of behavior's data under different time window lengths is utilized for the network's input, and the behavior recognition results by proposed model are analysed. The comparative experiments show that the proposed methods has a better performance in behavior recognition than deep belief networks (DBN) and SVM methods. The results prove that the proposed model can effectively and precisely realize the identification of maneuver behaviors, meanwhile, the setting of various window can accomplish behaviors recognition dynamically.

articleTitle: An approach for jamming distance boundary analysis of ground-based radar based on aerial target RCS fluctuation model
abstract: As an important jamming mode in electronic countermeasure, deception jamming has the characteristics of low cost and flexibility, which can effectively interfere the target detection performance of ground-based radar. This paper mainly analyses the jamming distance boundary based on the RCS Swerling fluctuation model of aerial target. To realize the successful radar cross section (RCS) deception, the mathematic derivation of the relative range boundary is accomplished, and the real simulation results conform to the theoretical analysis results. This corresponding analysis results can effectively provide the theoretical reference for the development and adjustment of electronic equipment in practical engineering application.

articleTitle: Vital signs monitoring using an IR-UWB radar based on edge computing
abstract: Ultra-wideband (UWB) pulse-Doppler radars play an important role in non-contact vital signs monitoring, such as respiration and heartbeat. Not constraining the movement of the person is the advantage of wireless vital signs detection using radars. This paper focuses on continuous monitoring of vital sings using an impulse-radio (IR) UWB radar. Orthogonal demodulation and difference phase methods were used to solve the problem that heart rate signals are susceptible to harmonic interference from the respiration signal. This algorithm has lower computational complexity and less bandwidth requirement. Furthermore, this paper provides a fresh look at the concept of combining the UWB radar technology and edge computing by first discussing the feasibility and potential of application in artificial intelligence (AI). Moreover, a case study where controlling the change of intelligent lamps by radar, it has been verified that the combination of edge computing and radar detection technology can meet the requirements of the AI.

articleTitle: Through-the-wall radar imaging by exploiting multipath propagation and structure of target scene
abstract: Compressive sensing (CS) based through-the-wall radar imaging (TWRI) exploits group sparsity of the target in the multipath propagation to achieve high resolution with limited measurements. This paper extends the CS based TWRI to further include cluster structure of the target. A structure-ware prior is imposed to statistically encourage spatial extent cluster structure of target scene and model group sparsity due to multipath propagation. Expectation propagation scheme is used for the approximate posterior inference. The proposed nonparametric Bayesian algorithm can achieve substantial improvements in terms of preserving target contiguity and suppressing isolated spurious targets compared to other state-of-art algorithms.

articleTitle: Dense false-target jamming suppression method by utilizing BI-phase random coded waveform for space time adaptive processing
abstract: The performance of conventional space-time adaptive processing would deteriorated due to dense false-target jamming. Thus, a dense false-target jamming suppression method utilizing bi-phase random coded waveform is proposed. In the proposed method, the phase codes of bi-phase random coded waveform are generated by M sequence codes. Then the generated waveform is applied to the transmitting signal to reduce the correlation among coherent processing intervals. In the following, the matched filter is designed based on the transmitting waveform to suppress the jamming. Finally, the clutter is suppressed by jointly adaptive filtering in space and time domain. Simulation results verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A method of aircraft target recognition for meter wave-radar based on convolutional neural network
abstract: For meter-wave radar, the time-frequency image is an important technique for aircraft target recognition because of its rich micro-motion characteristics. The traditional pattern recognition method is difficult to extract the important features of time-frequency image, the probability of target recognition is low, and the recognition robustness is poor under low SNR. In order to solve these problems, this paper presents an aircraft target recognition method based on convolutional neural network, whose core idea is to take advantage of automatic and comprehensive image feature extraction by convolutional neural network, improve the recognition probability and noise robustness. Firstly, the time-frequency image datasets for different attitude are generated by modeling the common aircraft fretting characteristics. Secondly, four types of classic network are trained, including AlexNet, VGG19, GoogLeNet and ResNet50.
