Thirdly, aircraft recognition is implemented by the trained network, and the performance of network is analyzed. The simulation dataset proved the deep learning method is more than 14.5% more accurate than the traditional time-frequency feature and classification method, and more robust for noise. Furthermore, the excellent performance of proposed method is proved by measured dataset, with the recognition rate's improvement of more the 21.8%.

articleTitle: Space-borne tri-band SAR for ship detection in medium and high sea conditions
abstract: For ship target detection applications under complex sea conditions, the ship/sea contrast of traditional single-band spaceborne Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) is low, and the ship target detection performance decreases sharply. In this paper, a concept of spaceborne tri-band common caliber SAR system is proposed. The antenna technology of tri-band common caliber SAR is adopted to reduce the antenna area and weight, and the electromagnetic scattering information of L, S and X bands can be obtained simultaneously. This paper introduces the tri-band SAR echo information joint processing method. Firstly, the joint processing from the perspective of SAR signal is carried out, and quickly detect the ship target location, then small scene imaging of target area is obtained. After that, through the tri-band SAR image fusion processing, further enhance the Signal-Clutter-Noise Ratio (SCNR) and outline of the ship target information, and improve the ship target detection performance of complex sea condition.

articleTitle: Anti-jamming method based on multi-instance multi-label learning
abstract: This paper analyses jamming recognition and countermeasure based on MIML (multi-instance multi-label learning). We first use the kernel clustering algorithm for signal sorting to determine the interference signal and its frequency. Based on the MIML framework, it extracts more efficient and comprehensive time-frequency distribution characteristics in the interference signal in the form of compound signal. After recognizing the modulation mode of interference, the particle swarm optimization algorithm is used to search for the waveform with the lowest correlation with the interference waveform. By adjusting the waveform parameters, the waveform in the working range is as uncorrelated with the interference as possible, and the interference is eliminated based on waveform optimization. Finally, simulations are carried out to examine the performance of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Null broadening adaptive beamforming based on polarisation covariance matrix reconstruction
abstract: The rapid movement of global navigation satellite system (GNSS) receiver is responsible for the interference steering vector mismatch, which degrades the performance of traditional polarization domain beamforming algorithm. In order to address this problem, a new beamforming algorithm based on polarization domain covariance matrix reconstruction is proposed in this paper, which can broaden the interference null. First, the algorithm analyses the relationship between the interference power and the eigenvalue of the simple covariance matrix, which obtains a simple method to estimate the interference power. Then, we can utilize the interference prior information to construct the steering vector correlation matrix. Therefore, the interference-plus-noise covariance matrix is reconstructed by the correlation matrix and the estimated interference power. Finally, the effectiveness of the algorithm is verified by numerical simulations. Simulation results show that this algorithm can effectively avoid the performance degradation caused by interference steering vector mismatch, which has better robustness than traditional polarization domain beamforming algorithm, and it is able to provide similar signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) close to the optimal value in case of GNSS receiver moving fast.

articleTitle: Chaotic dynamics of ionospheric clutter from high frequency surface wave radar
abstract: The detection performance of high frequency surface wave radar is impacted by the ionospheric clutter. In order to suppress the ionospheric clutter, it is important to research the physical mechanism of ionosphere. In this paper, it is demonstrated, convincingly for the first time, the chaotic dynamics of the ionospheric clutter. The results are obtained using the actual data collected from a series of experiments in Weihai Radar Station, China. The study includes the stationarity and nonlinearity test, phase-space reconstruction, correlation dimension analysis and Lyapunov exponents analysis. And finally, it is found that ionospheric clutter in HFSWR is a chaotic dynamical process with relatively few degrees of freedom, in contrast to the stochastic approach where the ionospheric clutter is viewed as a random process with a large number of degrees of freedom[1]. Also, this new approach will further provide an original way to analyse the ionospheric clutter suppression method.

articleTitle: Sparsity-based space-time adaptive processing using convolutional neural network
abstract: In this paper, a deep learning framework for space-time adaptive processing is developed. Firstly, a set of clutter covariance matrixes (CCMs) are modeled based on the prior parameters of radar and navigation system with respect to all possible levels of non-ideal factors, and the columns of each CCM is formulated as undersampled noisy linear measurements of the sparse coefficients corresponding to angle-Doppler spectrum. Then the original spectrum coefficients, obtained by least-square estimation from the modeled CCMs and known space-time steering dictionary, are used as input to train the convolutional neural network (CNN). Meanwhile, the corresponding labels can be obtained by the exact spectrum of modeled CCMs via minimum variance distortionless response algorithm. Once trained, the CNN can be used to predict angle-Doppler spectrum coefficients that corresponds to a new measurement vector in near real time. Simulations results have demonstrated the superiority of the proposed method in both clutter suppression performance and computation efficiency.

articleTitle: Probability hypothesis density filter with low detection probability
abstract: Conventional Gaussian mixture probability hypothesis density filter (GM-PHD) suffers from targets missing and decreased tracking accuracy under the condition of low detection probability. To tackle these problems, an improved GM-PHD algorithm is proposed in this paper. The phenomenon of weight sag, which accounts for the performance degradation is analyzed. A strategy to retain the Gaussian components of real targets is then designed to alleviate weight sag. In the mean time, we propose an adaptive weight attenuation method to reject the false targets. Simulation results show that the improved GM-PHD algorithm has better tracking performance than GM-PHD under different conditions of low detection probability and promise its application values.

articleTitle: Weak moving target coherent integration detection based on compressed sensing
abstract: At present, moving target detection (MTD) for weak targets is a great challenge in radar signal processing field. To improve the detection performance of the weak target with constant radial velocity further, a novel coherent integration detection algorithm, improved axis rotation MTD based on compressed sensing (IAR-MTD-CS), is proposed in this paper.IAR-MTD-CS could eliminate line range migration by IAR transform, coherently integrate the targets' echoes via MTD,realize range-Doppler plane sparsity by threshold processing, detect the weak targets and estimate the motion parameters via CS. IAR-MTD-CS has a better performance than IAR-MTD and MTD and has a lower signal-to noise ratio application scenario than CS, which is verified by some simulation experiments.

articleTitle: A fast parameter estimation method and aliasing analysis for multiple chirp signals based on fractional autocorrelation
abstract: In modern electronic warfare, frequency space is becoming more and more density. In the meantime, chirp signal is widely used in many radar systems. Thus, the ultra-wideband radar reconnaissance receiver is possible to intercept multiple chirp signals. This paper focuses on the parameter estimation of multiple chirp signals intercepted by the non-cooperative receiver. The closed formula of the fractional autocorrelation is given and the envelope detector is employed sto estimate the multiple chirp signals. In addition, the aliasing of the envelope detector is analysed mathematically and the fast parameter estimation algorithm is proposed. Compared with time-frequency method, the computational complexity of the proposed method is low. Simulation results show the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: A robust eigenspace-based adaptive beamforming algorithm
abstract: This paper proposes a new algorithm PCDMR (Principle Component and Dominant Mode Rejection) based on a judgment structure, which can help to choose the better one from PC (Principle Component) and DMR (Dominant Mode Rejection) in different signal circumstances. The simulation results show the PCDMR has fine and robust performances.

articleTitle: High-precision clock recovery based on OOK
abstract: This paper proposes a high-precision clock recovery method for the pseudo code ranging system based on the direct sequence spread spectrum OOK system. The delay phase-locked tracking loop (DDL) is used to track and lock the received pseudo code signal and restore the clock information, and then we can complete the clock information conversion through calculations. The results of FPGA simulation and verification show that the clock recovered by the method at receiver in the optical fiber or wireless remote terminal has small transient deviation and high frequency stability. It can provide a stable reference clock for each station in the entire system and eliminate the clock uncertainty between different base stations.

articleTitle: Research on vehicle recognition technology based on multi-feature-SVM method
abstract: Vehicle recognition is the important information detected in intelligent transportation systems. Mature research methods mostly use induction coils, lasers, cameras, etc. for recognition, while the use of radar for vehicle recognition is relatively rare. This paper proposes a vehicle identification technology based on the multi-feature-SVM method, which processes millimeter-wave radar echo data, adopts vehicle length acquisition technology based on one-dimensional range spectrum broadening method and target scattering cross-sectional area acquisition based on gain compensation method Technology, extract the two effective vehicle identification features of vehicle length and target scattering cross-sectional area, obtain temporary vehicle classification results through the SVM best model, and finally combine the multi-frame fusion method to remove random errors that may occur in the discrimination process to ensure the reliability of the output results. The results show that the vehicle identification method proposed in this paper can achieve 92% accuracy, ideal results and strong practicability.

articleTitle: Fractional fourier transform based cadence velocity diagram technique for human motion recognition
abstract: Human motion recognition (HMR) is playing an increasingly key role in many fields including public security, medical treatment and health care. In this paper, we propose a fractional Fourier transform (FrFT) based cadence-velocity diagram (CVD) based method, to improve the classification rate, which can effectively distinguish similar human motions in certain traditional feature domains such as the time-frequency (TF) domain. Besides, we also incorporate the feature in FrFT based CVD domain with the range feature, which can be regarded as the multi-domain feature. Then six human daily motions are then classified by the convolutional neural network (CNN) with the above multi-domain feature. Experimental results based on real data has demonstrated that the proposed method can achieve a high classification rate.

articleTitle: A novel method for InSAR phase filtering
abstract: In order to reduce the phase unwrapping problems caused by phase noise, it is necessary to study the filtering method to obtain high-quality interferogram. In this paper, a novel cascade filtering algorithm combining a median filter with a mean filter based on side window filter (SWF) framework is developed to suppress interferometric phase noise. Except for the performance of denoising, the proposed method also has good performance in preserving phase fringe. The experiments on the simulated data and the real data are conducted to prove the effectiveness of the proposed filtering method.

articleTitle: Covariance matrix reconstruction algorithm based on minimum atomic norm for coprime array
abstract: To solve the problem that Direction of Arrival(DOA) estimation based on virtual array interpolation does not fully utilize covariance matrix information, the reconstruction of covariance matrix of coprime array is transformed into low-rank matrix completion and atomic norm optimization, and proposes the reconstruction algorithm of covariance matrix of mutual array based on atomic norm.In this algorithm, the Toeplitz covariance matrix is expressed as the Toeplitz completion problem by the generalized augmented method, and then the truncated singular value threshold(SVT) method is used as the reference in the atomic norm optimization problem to carry out the optimization solution and transformed to achieve fast positive definite Toeplitz covariance matrix reconstruction. The algorithm makes full use of the information contained in the coprime array to improve the stability of DOA estimation algorithm and reduce the computational complexity.

articleTitle: Research on high precision angle measurement method based on new millimetre wave array
abstract: Millimetre-wave radar has become the core sensor of modern cars due to its low cost, high precision, and all-weather, all-weather advantages, and will play an important role in the realization of automatic driving in the future. For vehicle-mounted millimetre-wave radars, the contradiction between the angular resolution and the view FOV of detection angle is an important issue to be solved urgently. This article focuses on the research of the vehicle-mounted millimetre wave radar angle measurement method, and proposes a new millimetre wave radar array processing method, which solves the problem of angle ambiguity through phase compensation, and achieves a larger angle measurement range while ensuring high angular resolution. At the same time, high-precision measurement of the pitch angle is completed.

articleTitle: Simulation research on ground-air bistatic radar clutter
abstract: Aiming at the problem of ground clutter in ground-air cooperative bistatic radar, a mathematical model of clutter is established. And based on the model, the clutter's space-time characteristics are analyzed. Then, the range doppler spectral characteristics of clutter are numerically simulated. The simulation results show that the geometry of the ground-air bistatic radar makes the space-time two dimensional spectral distribution of clutter not only change with the geometry parameters of the bistatic radar, but also with the range sum. Finally, an important conclusion is obtained that the ground-air bistatic radar clutter exhibits serious non-stationarity and range-variation.

articleTitle: A synthetic layout method for distributed nested circular array based on ant colony algorithm
abstract: In order to reduce the sidelobe level of the distributed nested circular array, the distributed nested circular array is sparsely arranged based on the ant colony algorithm. After the ant colony continues to search and move, the optimal array element position distribution is finally found, which has the array element position with the lowest peak sidelobe level. The simulation shows that under the condition that the number of array elements is constant, the peak side lobe level of the antenna array pattern is effectively reduced.

articleTitle: Calculation and analysis of phase center on circularly polarized microstrip antenna
abstract: A three-feeding mechanism is introduced for circularly polarized (CP) microstrip antennas to posses stable phase center. Basing on the phase relationship and applying the least square method, the phase center of the CP antennas has been presented by theoretical calculation and analysis. The simulated results approve the advantage of the centrosymmetric feeding configuration, and the stability of phase center of the three-fed antenna is less than 1 mm in the main lobe range, while that of the traditional dual-fed CP antenna is as large as 4 mm. Furthermore, a simple and efficient evolution approach is introduced to obtain a accurate solution of the mean phase center. The simulated result shows that the location of mean phase center ,which is optimized by the Geese particle swarm optimization in a least-square sense, can reduce almost half phase deviation on phase radiation pattern, comparing with the centre of stability sphere.

articleTitle: Design and implementation of multi-feature fusion kernel correlation filtering algorithm based on HLS
abstract: In order to balance the accuracy and real-time performance of the moving target tracking system, an optimized design and implementation method based on high-level synthesis (HLS) of multi-feature fusion with kernel correlation filtering algorithms on FPGA is designed. This design improves the KCF algorithm with LBP and HOG features, and proposes a new dimensionality reduction method for LBP, which enhances the real-time performance while maintaining effective extraction of target features. The algorithm is implemented with FPGA, and a well acceleration effect is obtained on the basis of high precision. In test, the frame rate reaches 35 frames per second. Finally, it is verified through simulation that this feature extraction method can be used to process various image data such as infrared detection and SAR radar imaging, and has a wide range of applications.

articleTitle: Multi-scale and densely arranged target detection in SAR images with a gated feature pyramid network and oriented bounding boxes
abstract: Target detection in SAR images plays an important role in remote sensing, but still presents many challenges in the deep learning era. The deep learning-based detector performs well. However, the results also showed that the Faster R-CNN detector is not able to detect ships of different sizes and those that are densely arranged near the shore. In order to solve the two problems above, we propose a detector with a Gated Feature Pyramid Network and oriented bounding boxes. The Gated Feature Pyramid Network can selectively build a feature pyramid with channel-wise and space-wise attention modules. Channel-wise attention can be viewed as the process of selecting semantic attributes to detect ships with different scales. This is helpful for classification. Space-wise attention pays more attention to the semantic-related regions. This is helpful for localization. The oriented bounding boxes can locate ships tightly and thus recognize and locate them with a high level of accuracy, especially for the densely arranged ships. The anchors are also redesigned to best fit ships in SSDD+. Oriented Region-of-Interest aligning is used to generate a fixed-length vector without misalignment on small ships. Angle-related intersection-of-union is used to prepare positive and negative oriented proposals. It can compute the real overlap of two oriented bounding boxes. The multi-task loss function with angle information is used to train the model. The results of SSDD+ show that the proposed detector can adapt to complex situations with multi-scale and densely arranged ships.

articleTitle: A 3D reconstruction method for group target split detection
abstract: The group target in 3D space is composed of a large number of individuals. In the process of group target movement, some individuals that can form a small group may be split from the whole. To achieve stable tracking of group targets, it is necessary to detect the split of group targets in time. Therefore, this paper proposes a 3D model reconstruction method based on 2D information to detect the split of the group targets. It uses the reconstructed ellipsoid to represent the shape of the 3D space group target and then the split judgment can be made by the volume change rate of the ellipsoid. Due to the calculation process of directly obtaining the ellipsoid parameters in the 3D space is complicated and the calculation amount is large, this method uses the projection idea to project the ellipsoid onto the coordinate plane, and then the projected ellipse parameters can be used to reconstruct the 3D ellipsoid. Simulation results prove the effectiveness of the new method.

articleTitle: Robust phase-only transmit nulling for adaptive wideband arrays
abstract: Phase-only algorithm can reduce the complexity of the system. However, in the case of systematic error, the null formed by the ideal phase-only algorithm is too narrow, resulting in the insufficient interference suppression. A new study of the robust phase-only transmit nulling for adaptive wideband arrays is introduced in this paper. Firstly, the filter bank behind each array element partitions the transmit signal into independent subbands. In each subband, the interference noise covariance matrix is optimized to widen the null. And the phase-only weighted solution is obtained by reiterative uniform weight optimization (RUWO). In the end, the synthesis filters reconstruct the wideband transmit adaptive digital beam. Theoretical analyses and simulation results show that the proposed algorithm improves the width and depth of the null in the interference direction. The algorithm enhances the robustness of the beam and can be easily realized in engineering.

articleTitle: Compensation of Faraday rotation of PALSAR in China
abstract: Due to the electron density and the geomagnetic field within the ionosphere, full polarization space-borne SAR systems at L-band or lower frequencies, such as the Phased Array type L-band Synthetic Aperture Radar (PALSAR), will suffer the effect of Faraday rotation. The corresponding compensation therefore should be considered. In this paper, by using a series of the PALSAR data sets in different Chinese regions, compensation based on the scattering matrix shows better results than that from the Alaska Satellite Facility.

articleTitle: Ground target locating based on direction determination in satellite-borne
abstract: Target locating in satellite-borne is an important task for satellite detection. A simulation model for ground target locating based on direction determination in satellite-borne is proposed in this paper. The target geographical location can be worked out by the spherical geometry method based on the elevation angle and azimuth angle of the emitter signal with the satellite position and the orbit elements at the same time. The precision of target locating algorithm within different direction determination errors is also analyzed in this paper. And a data fusion method is given for raising the precision of target locating algorithm. In the experiment, the satellite simulation model is utilized for generating the orbit position data of the satellite and the signal direction data. In addition, the comparison of the target locating with different direction determination precisions is given. Finally, several constructive suggestions are made for practical engineering applications.

articleTitle: Target detection in anechoic chamber based on the interrupted transmitting and receiving of PCM signal
abstract: Phase coded modulation (PCM) signal has been widely used in target detection at the out-field. However, when the PCM signal is utilized in the anechoic chamber for target detection, the target echo returns before the signal is fully transmitted, which results in the signal coupling at the receiver. In this paper, the interrupted transmitting and receiving (ITR) is adopted to solve the problem. Then, the procedure of target detection with PCM signal in anechoic chamber is proposed. The constraints of the ITR parameters are discussed according to the anechoic chamber size and the PCM signal parameters. By conducting the numerical simulations, the effectiveness of the proposed target detection method is verified.
